options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Aravalli Range is the oldest fold (residual) mountain range in India, dating back to the Precambrian (Proterozoic) era.

subject: Environment
q: Match List-I (National Park) with List-II (Location): a. Kaziranga — 1. Chikkamagaluru b. Kudremukh — 2. Palghat c. Silent Valley — 3. Nagpur d. Pench Valley — 4. Golaghat Nawgaon In the sequence of this a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching National Parks: a. Kaziranga — 4. Golaghat & Nagaon (Assam); b. Kudremukh — 1. Chikkamagaluru (Karnataka); c. Silent Valley — 2. Palakkad/Palghat (Kerala); d. Pench Valley — 3. Nagpur (Maharashtra) -> 4 1 2 3.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following lakes is situated in Bihar?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Anupam Lake is located in the Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary in Kaimur (Bhabua) district of Bihar.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following Lakes of India is located in Assam?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chapanala Lake is located in Nagaon district of Assam (whereas Kolleru is in Andhra Pradesh, Sala Lake is in Arunachal Pradesh, and Hamirsar Lake is in Gujarat).

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following waterfalls of India is located in Goa?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Dudhsagar Falls (meaning 'Sea of Milk') is a spectacular four-tiered waterfall on the Mandovi River located in the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park in Goa, along the border with Karnataka.

subject: Geography
q:
Match the following (Festivals — States):
I. Myoko Festival — a. Arunachal Pradesh
II. Chapchar Kut — b. Manipur
III. Sekrenyi — c. Mizoram
IV. Sangai — d. Nagaland I II III IV
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Northeast Festivals: I. Myoko Festival — a. Arunachal Pradesh (Apatani tribe); II. Chapchar Kut — c. Mizoram; III. Sekrenyi — d. Nagaland (Angami tribe); IV. Sangai Festival — b. Manipur -> a c d b.

subject: Geography
q: Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal was set up in 2010 to resolve the water dispute between which of the following States?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in 2010 to adjudicate the sharing of Vansadhara River waters between Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.

subject: Economics
q: Bharatmala Pariyojna was launched in October 2017. The total length of National Highways approved in it was:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I was approved in October 2017 for the development of 34,800 km of National Highways (including 10,000 km balance NHDP road works).

subject: Economics
q: Which of the following is NOT one of the weakest currencies in the world?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Omani Rial (OMR) is one of the highest-valued (strongest) currencies in the world (~$2.60 USD per OMR), whereas the Iranian Rial, Laotian Kip, and Lebanese Pound are among the weakest.

subject: Economics
q:
Match the Awards (List-I) with their Dimensions (List-II):
1. Ramon Magsaysay Award — a. Science Fiction
2. Pulitzer Prize — b. Journalism, Literature, Music
3. Templeton Prize — c. Asia's Highest Honour
4. Hugo Award — d. Spiritual, Religious 1 2 3 4
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Awards: 1. Ramon Magsaysay Award — c. Asia's Highest Honour; 2. Pulitzer Prize — b. Journalism, Literature, Music; 3. Templeton Prize — d. Spiritual/Religious dimension; 4. Hugo Award — a. Science Fiction -> c b d a.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements about Bihar's GSDP:
1. In 2019-20 percentage growth rate of Bihar GSDP was more than GDP growth rate of India.
2. In 2018-19 percentage growth rate of Bihar GSDP was less than GDP growth rate of India.
3. In 2023-24 as per quick estimate the percentage growth rate of GSDP of Bihar was 9.2. How many statements are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct as per Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25 (in 2019–20 and 2018–19 Bihar's GSDP growth exceeded India's GDP growth, and quick estimates for 2023–24 placed growth at 9.2% / 14.5% nominal).

subject: Economics
q: As per MSME Act, the latest definition of small scale industry is based on:
options: (B) Investment and annual turnover in all sector
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Investment and annual turnover in all sector
exp: Under the revised MSME classification (effective July 1, 2020), enterprises are defined based on a composite criterion of both investment in plant & machinery/equipment and annual turnover across both manufacturing and services sectors.

subject: Economics
q: According to 2024-25 budget estimate, gross fiscal deficit of Bihar as percentage of its GSDP was:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to the Bihar Budget Estimate 2024–25, the gross fiscal deficit of Bihar was pegged at 2.98% (~3.0%) of GSDP, within the FRBM limit.

subject: Economics
q: Multi-dimensional poverty index has been included in which of the following?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), developed by OPHI and UNDP in 2010, is included in the UNDP's Human Development Report.

subject: Economics
q: The enterprises named as Shishu, Tarun and Kishore are associated with:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), loans are categorized into Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10/20 lakh) by MUDRA.

subject: Economics
q: Match the revolutions (List-I) with their fields (List-II): a. Black revolution — 1. Milk b. Blue revolution — 2. Food crop c. White revolution — 3. Petroleum d. Green revolution — 4. Fish a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Agricultural Revolutions: a. Black Revolution — 3. Petroleum/Crude oil; b. Blue Revolution — 4. Fish; c. White Revolution — 1. Milk; d. Green Revolution — 2. Food crops -> 3 4 1 2.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Which of the following statements are true in context of the UNGA resolution calling for a peaceful resolution of the Ukraine war?
I. The meeting was held in Chicago, USA on completion of three years of Russian invasion of Ukraine.
II. The resolution received 65 abstentions, 60 votes in favor and 36 votes against the call for de-escalation.
III. The US brought forward a rival resolution titled 'The Path To Peace'.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only Statement III is true: on the 3rd anniversary of the Ukraine war (Feb 2025), the US proposed a rival resolution titled 'The Path to Peace' at the UN in New York (not Chicago), while the main UNGA resolution passed with 93 in favor, 18 against, and 65 abstentions.

subject: Current Affairs
q: On January 10, 2025 India became ________ country to successfully carry out a satellite docking process in Low Earth Orbit.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: With ISRO's SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment) mission in January 2025, India became the fourth country in the world (after the USA, Russia, and China) to achieve autonomous satellite docking in orbit.

subject: Environment
q: What was the theme of Sustainable Energy for All Global Forum held in March 2025 in Barbados?
options: (B) From Goals to actions: Power the Future with Sustainable Energy
(D) Sustainable Energy for Equity, Security and Prosperity
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Sustainable Energy for Equity, Security and Prosperity
exp: The Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL) Global Forum held in Bridgetown, Barbados (March 12–13, 2025) had the theme 'Sustainable Energy for Equity, Security and Prosperity'.

subject: Environment
q: Assertion (A): Corruption is a major threat to climate action. Reason (R): It acts as a hindrance in reducing emissions and adapting to the unavoidable effects of global heating.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A), reflecting Transparency International's 2024/2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) theme on corruption and the climate crisis.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Match List-I (Bilateral Military Exercise) with List-II (Countries):
1. Varuna Naval — a. India–France
2. Dharma Guardian — b. India–Japan
3. Ekuverin — c. India–Maldives
4. Cyclone — d. India–Egypt 1 2 3 4
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Bilateral Military Exercises: 1. Varuna — a. India–France; 2. Dharma Guardian — b. India–Japan; 3. Ekuverin — c. India–Maldives; 4. Cyclone — d. India–Egypt -> a b c d.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which Indian opener won Best International Women's Cricketer at BCCI Awards 2025?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Indian opening batter Smriti Mandhana won the Best International Cricketer (Women) award at the BCCI Naman Awards in February 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In April 2022, Geographic Indication (GI) tag was awarded to which of the following by Govt. of India?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Mithila Makhana (fox nut from the Mithila region of Bihar) was awarded the Geographical Indication (GI) tag by the Government of India in 2022.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Which of the following Indian-Americans is/are a part of Trump 2.0 Cabinet?
I. Kashyap Kash Patel
II. Harmeet Dhillon
III. Dr. Jay Bhattacharya
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three Indian-Americans — Kash Patel (FBI Director), Harmeet Dhillon (Assistant AG for Civil Rights), and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya (NIH Director) — were appointed to the Trump 2.0 administration.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Union Home Minister Shree Amit Shah unveiled an 11ft. tall statue of which eminent personality in Jodhpur?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Union Home Minister Amit Shah unveiled an 11-foot-tall statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in Jodhpur, Rajasthan.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Bhartiya Janata Party returned to power in Delhi after how many years?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) returned to power in the Delhi Legislative Assembly in February 2025 after 27 years (having last governed Delhi from 1993 to 1998).

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Which among the following is true about the Panchayats Extension to the Scheduled Areas (PESA) Act?
1. It was enacted in 1996.
2. It accords statutory status to the Gram Sabhas in Scheduled V areas.
3. Section 4(i) of the Act mandates Gram Sabha or Panchayat consent before any land acquisition for development projects.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 2 are true: PESA was enacted in 1996 and empowers Gram Sabhas in Fifth Schedule areas. Statement 3 is inaccurate because Section 4(i) mandates consultation (not mandatory prior consent in all cases) with the Gram Sabha before land acquisition.

subject: Physics
q: Match the following lenses/mirrors with their correct applications: Column-I (Lenses/Mirrors) — Column-II (Application) i. Concave mirror — p. Used in cameras and projectors for focusing light ii. Convex mirror — q. Used in correcting myopia (short-sightedness) iii. Convex lens — r. Used in vehicles for rear-viewing iv. Concave lens — s. Used in shaving to produce magnified upright image i ii iii iv
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: i. Concave mirror — s. Shaving mirror (magnified upright image); ii. Convex mirror — r. Rear-view mirror in vehicles; iii. Convex lens — p. Cameras and projectors; iv. Concave lens — q. Correcting myopia -> s r p q.

subject: Physics
q: An ideal gas is taken around a closed cycle ABCA as shown in a p-V diagram. The coordinates of the points are: A(V, p); B(3V, 4p); C(3V, p). What is the work done during one complete cycle? [DIAGRAM: p-V graph — triangle ABCA, B at (3V,4p), A at (V,p), C at (3V,p)]
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Work done in the closed clockwise cycle ABCA equals the area of right triangle ABC: W = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × (3V − V) × (4p − p) = (1/2) × 2V × 3p = 3pV.

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): In simple harmonic motion, the potential energy of the particle is maximum at the extreme positions. Reason (R): At the extreme positions, the velocity of the particle is maximum.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In SHM, potential energy U = (1/2)kx² is maximum at the extreme positions (x = ±A), whereas velocity is zero at the extreme positions and maximum at the mean position; thus (A) is true but (R) is false.

subject: Physics
q: In an Alternating Current (AC) circuit, match the types of circuit (Column-I) with the phase relationship between current and voltage (Column-II): i. Pure Resistance (R) — p. Current leads voltage by 90° ii. Pure Capacitance (C) — q. Current and voltage are in same phase iii. Pure Inductance (L) — r. Current and voltage may or may not be in same phase iv. R-L-C Series Circuit — s. Current lags voltage by 90° i ii iii iv
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: i. Pure Resistance (R) — q. Current and voltage in same phase; ii. Pure Capacitance (C) — p. Current leads voltage by 90°; iii. Pure Inductance (L) — s. Current lags voltage by 90°; iv. R-L-C Series Circuit — r. May or may not be in phase -> q p s r.

subject: Physics
q: Which of the following statements is correct as the temperature increases?
options: (A) The resistivity of both semiconductor and conductor increases.
(B) The resistivity of both semiconductor and conductor decreases.
(C) The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases, whereas the resistivity of a conductor increases.
(D) The resistivity of a semiconductor increases, whereas the resistivity of a conductor decreases.
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) The resistivity of a semiconductor decreases, whereas the resistivity of a conductor increases.
exp: As temperature increases, carrier concentration increases exponentially in a semiconductor so its resistivity decreases, whereas increased thermal lattice scattering increases the resistivity of a metallic conductor.

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): Gauss's law in magnetostatics and electrostatics are respectively, ∮B·dS = 0 and ∮E·dS = q_enclosed/ε₀. Reason (R): Magnetic monopoles do not exist, whereas electric monopoles (isolated charges) exist.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A): ∮B·dS = 0 holds because isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist (magnetic field lines always form closed loops), whereas ∮E·dS = q/ε₀ holds because isolated electric charges exist.

subject: Physics
q: Two astronauts on the moon are standing 10 m apart. Astronaut A shouts toward Astronaut B and simultaneously flashes a light signal. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: (A) The light signal from Astronaut A will reach Astronaut B but not the sound.
(B) Neither sound nor light from Astronaut A will reach Astronaut B.
(C) Both sound and light from Astronaut A will reach Astronaut B at equal speed.
(D) Both sound and light from Astronaut A will reach Astronaut B but light will arrive slightly earlier.
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) The light signal from Astronaut A will reach Astronaut B but not the sound.
exp: The Moon has no atmosphere, and sound waves are mechanical waves requiring a material medium to propagate, whereas light is an electromagnetic wave that travels through vacuum.

subject: Physics
q: A particle is found to be at rest when observed from a reference frame S₁ and the same particle is found to move with a constant velocity when observed from another frame S₂. Which of the following statements is true?
options: (A) Both S₁ and S₂ are inertial frames.
(B) Both S₁ and S₂ are non-inertial frames.
(C) S₂ is an inertial frame but S₁ is a non-inertial frame.
(D) S₁ is an inertial frame but S₂ is a non-inertial frame.
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both S₁ and S₂ are inertial frames.
exp: Since the particle has zero acceleration in S₁ and moves with constant velocity (zero acceleration) in S₂, S₂ is moving at a constant velocity relative to S₁; hence both S₁ and S₂ are inertial reference frames.

subject: Physics
q: A car covers a displacement x with velocity v₁ and then another equal displacement x with velocity v₂. What is the average velocity for the entire journey?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total displacement = 2x; total time = x/v₁ + x/v₂. Average velocity = 2x / (x/v₁ + x/v₂) = 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂) (the harmonic mean).

subject: Physics
q: Consider the interaction forces between two protons separated by a distance of the order of 1 femtometer (10⁻¹⁵ m). The correct order of the strengths of the electromagnetic, gravitational and nuclear forces acting between them is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: At nuclear distances (~1 fm = 10⁻¹⁵ m), the strong nuclear force is the strongest, followed by the electromagnetic force (~1/137th), and the gravitational force (~10⁻³⁸) is the weakest: Nuclear > Electromagnetic > Gravitational.

subject: Chemistry
q: H₂O + C ——→ H₂ + CO. The above reaction is an example of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Passing steam over red-hot coke (H₂O + C → H₂ + CO, an equimolar mixture of CO and H₂) is the classic Water-Gas reaction (syngas).

subject: Chemistry
q: 'Superglue' is a polymer of which monomer?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Superglue is an fast-acting adhesive polymer formed by the anionic polymerization of cyanoacrylate monomers (such as methyl or ethyl 2-cyanoacrylate).

subject: Chemistry
q: The following structure is of: [DIAGRAM: Chemical structure — ring with HN, C=O groups and N-H (nitrogenous base structure)]
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The given pyrimidine ring structure with two keto (=O) groups at C2 and C4 and no methyl group at C5 is Uracil (2,4-dioxypyrimidine).

subject: Chemistry
q: A supercritical fluid is formed whenever:
options: (B) A substance is heated above its critical temperature
(C) A substance is heated far below its critical temperature
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) A substance is heated above its critical temperature
exp: A supercritical fluid is formed when a substance is heated and compressed above its critical temperature (T_c) and critical pressure (P_c).

subject: Chemistry
q: Barium appears primarily in ore(s) of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Barium occurs in nature primarily in two mineral ores: barite (barytes, BaSO₄) and witherite (BaCO₃).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following is the primary pigment involved in photosynthesis?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chlorophyll a is the universal primary photosynthetic pigment that directly participates in the light reaction center.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following best explains the pressure flow hypothesis in phloem transport?
options: (A) Movement of water only through xylem
(C) Osmotic pressure difference between source and sink
(D) Active transport of sugars from sink to source
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Osmotic pressure difference between source and sink
exp: Münch's Pressure Flow (Mass Flow) Hypothesis states that translocation of sugars in phloem is driven by an osmotic turgor pressure gradient between the source (leaves) and sink (roots/fruits).

subject: Environment
q:
In the light of new discovery of soil nematode Crassolabium dhritiae,
which of the following statements are true?
I. It was discovered in Keonjhar, Odisha.
II. It is named after the director of Zoological Survey of India i.e. Dr. Malti Mukherjee.
III. These organisms play a significant role in nutrient-cycling and decomposition of organic matter.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements I and III are true: the soil nematode Crassolabium dhritiae was discovered in Keonjhar, Odisha and aids in soil nutrient cycling. Statement II is false because it was named after ZSI Director Dr. Dhriti Banerjee (not Malti Mukherjee).

subject: Biology
q: Fluid Mosaic Model of plasma membrane was proposed by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Fluid Mosaic Model of the plasma membrane structure was proposed by S.J. Singer and Garth L. Nicolson in 1972.

subject: Biology
q: In plants, water is mainly transported through which tissue?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In vascular plants, water and dissolved minerals are transported upward from roots to shoots through the xylem tissue.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following correctly represents the law of segregation?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Mendel's Law of Segregation (monohybrid cross) yields a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (and 1:2:1 genotypic ratio; 3:1 is the standard monohybrid ratio contrasted with 9:3:3:1 dihybrid).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following statements about Erythromycin is incorrect?
options: (A) It cannot be produced in fermentation from a strain of the Saccharopolyspora erythraea
(B) For legionellosis, it has good coverage
(C) It can be used as antibiotic
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) It cannot be produced in fermentation from a strain of the Saccharopolyspora erythraea
exp: Statement (A) is incorrect because Erythromycin IS commercially produced by fermentation from the actinomycete Saccharopolyspora erythraea (formerly Streptomyces erythreus).

subject: Biology
q:
Consider the following stages of demographic transition:
I. High birth rate with low death rate
II. Low birth rate with low death rate
III. High birth rate with high death rate
Arrange these stages in correct chronological order:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chronological order of Demographic Transition stages: Stage 1: High birth rate with high death rate (III) -> Stage 2: High birth rate with declining/low death rate (I) -> Stage 3: Low birth rate with low death rate (II) -> III, I, II.

subject: Biology
q: Consider the following statements about Mendel's Laws: i. Mendel is called the father of genetics. ii. Law of segregation states that each gamete receives two alleles for a trait. iii. In a monohybrid cross, F2 phenotypic ratio is 3:1. iv. Law of independent assortment works only for traits on different chromosomes. Select the group of correct statements only:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements i, iii, and iv are correct. Statement ii is false because the Law of Segregation states that each gamete receives only ONE allele (not two) for each trait.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following statements about glycolysis is correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Glycolysis (EMP pathway) takes place in the cytoplasm (cytosol) of the cell, does not require oxygen, and does not directly release CO₂.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following statements is/are true about Vitamin B₁₂? a. It is also known as cobalamin. b. It is composed of cobalt-atoms. c. It consists of corrin rings.
options: (A) Only a and c are true
(B) a, b and c are true
(C) Only b and c are true
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) a, b and c are true
exp: All three statements (a, b, and c) are true: Vitamin B₁₂ is chemically known as cobalamin, contains a central cobalt ion, and features a tetrapyrrole-like corrin ring.

subject: Biology
q: Temporary parasites are:
options: (A) Free living but become parasitic if opportunity arises
(B) Complete their life cycle inside the host
(C) Live on the surface of host's body
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Temporary (intermittent) parasites (such as mosquitoes, bedbugs, and leeches) visit the host only temporarily to feed.

subject: Biology
q: Who is known as the father of genetics?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Gregor Johann Mendel is known as the Father of Genetics for his foundational pea plant inheritance experiments.

subject: Biology
q: Assertion (A): Transpiration helps in the ascent of sap. Reason (R): Transpiration increases osmotic pressure in roots.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are true (transpiration pull drives the ascent of sap and water loss increases osmotic concentration/suction pressure in mesophyll and root cells), with C/D as standard key.

subject: Biology
q: What is the correct order of stages in incomplete metamorphosis in insects?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Incomplete (hemimetabolous) metamorphosis in insects (such as grasshoppers and cockroaches) consists of three stages: Egg -> Nymph -> Adult (lacking a pupal stage).

subject: History
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Satyashodhak Samaj:
1. It was primarily aimed at challenging Brahminical dominance and promoting equality for lower castes.
2. It worked towards universal education for women and lower castes.
3. The Samaj promoted the idea of untouchability as a necessary social custom.
How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 2 are correct (Only two): Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to challenge Brahminical orthodoxy and promote education for women and Shudras/Ati-Shudras. Statement 3 is false.

subject: Biology
q: Which scientist worked independently and reached a similar conclusion to Darwin's?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Alfred Russel Wallace independently conceived the theory of evolution by natural selection, co-publishing with Charles Darwin in 1858.

subject: Biology
q: Hemoglobin carries oxygen to the blood and is __________ containing compound.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing (Fe²⁺) metalloprotein in red blood cells that transports oxygen.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which of the following towns is located in the westernmost part of Bihar?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Kaimur (Bhabua) is the westernmost district/town of Bihar, bordering Uttar Pradesh.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Match the following institutions with their establishment years:
1. Patna College — i. 1921 2. Prince of Wales Medical College — ii. 1863 3. Bihar Vidyapeeth — iii. 1900 4. Bihar School of Engineering — iv. 1940 5. Patna Women's College — v. 1925 1 2 3 4 5
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Patna institutions with establishment years: 1. Patna College — ii. 1863; 2. Prince of Wales Medical College (PMCH) — v. 1925; 3. Bihar Vidyapeeth — i. 1921; 4. Bihar School of Engineering (NIT Patna) — iii. 1900; 5. Patna Women's College — iv. 1940 -> ii v i iii iv.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Elementary Education Act was implemented in Bihar and Orissa in 1919 in which compulsory education for children of what age was passed?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Bihar and Orissa Primary/Elementary Education Act of 1919 introduced compulsory primary education for children aged 6 to 10 years.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which Committee was formed to establish Veterinary College in Patna in 1927?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Bihar and Orissa Veterinary College in Patna (established 1927) was set up following the recommendations of the Syed Fakhruddin Committee (then Education & Development Minister).

subject: Bihar Special
q: Assertion (A): Since 2021, November 15th is celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas to honour the contribution of tribal communities in Indian Freedom struggle. Reason (R): It is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Tilka Manjhi, one of the earliest tribal freedom fighters.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Assertion (A) is true (November 15 is celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas since 2021), but Reason (R) is false because November 15 marks the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, not Tilka Manjhi.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Assertion (A): Bihar is a backward State of the Country. Reason (R): It is characterized by regional disparities in the level of development.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct (Bihar is an economically backward state and exhibits inter-district regional disparities), though regional disparity is a characteristic rather than the primary cause of overall state backwardness.

subject: Geography
q: Match List-I (Industry) with List-II (Centre): a. Sugar — 1. Raurkela b. Paper — 2. Maholi c. Cement — 3. Chandrahati d. Iron and steel — 4. Sawai Madhopur a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Industries with Centres: a. Sugar — 2. Maholi (UP); b. Paper — 3. Churk/Chandrahati; c. Cement — 4. Sawai Madhopur (Rajasthan); d. Iron and Steel — 1. Rourkela (Odisha) -> 2 3 4 1.

subject: Economics
q: Match List-I (Goods and Services) with List-II (New GST Rates effective from September 22, 2025): a. Dishwashers — 1. 40%; b. Commercial yoga services — 2. 18%; c. Premiums on health insurance — 3. 5%; d. SUVs with engine capacity above 1500 CC — 4. Zero.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under the GST rate rationalization effective September 22, 2025: Dishwashers (18%, a-2), Commercial yoga services (5%, b-3), Health insurance premiums (Zero/Exempt, c-4), and luxury SUVs >1500 cc (40%, d-1).

subject: Geography
q: What is the other name of the partially submerged active stratovolcano Whakaari in the Bay of Plenty, New Zealand, which was recently under monitoring for undergoing 'heightened unrest'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Whakaari, located in the Bay of Plenty off the North Island of New Zealand, is internationally known as White Island.

subject: History
q:
Match the items of List-I (Key Aspects of the 2019 Rakhigarhi DNA Study) with List-II (Descriptions):
a) Source of the ancient DNA sample — 1) A mixture of ancient Iranian-related farmers/herders and Ancient Ancestral South Indians (AASI)
b) Primary ancestry components identified — 2) Steppe pastoralists associated with Indo-European migrations c) Notably absent ancestry in the IVC individual — 3) Skeletal remains of a woman from ~2500 BCE at Rakhigarhi, Haryana d) Broader genetic implications for modern Indians — 4) IVC populations as direct genetic ancestors without external Steppe input during the civilization's peak
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 2019 Rakhigarhi ancient DNA study (Shinde et al., Cell) analyzed a woman's skeleton (~2500 BCE, a-3), showed Iranian-related + AASI ancestry (b-1), absence of Steppe pastoralist ancestry (c-2), and confirmed IVC continuity (d-4).

subject: History
q: The forensic analysis of the 282 skeletons unearthed from an abandoned well in Ajnala, Punjab, in 2014, primarily confirmed their identity as Indian soldiers from the 1857 Sepoy Mutiny through which key combined evidence?
options: (A) Cranial measurements and carbon isotope values suggesting local Punjabi ancestry
(B) Mitochondrial DNA haplogroups and strontium isotope ratios indicating Gangetic plain origins
(C) Dental caries patterns and skeletal trauma from Partition-era violence
(D) Radiocarbon dating and the presence of European-style weapons
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Mitochondrial DNA haplogroups and strontium isotope ratios indicating Gangetic plain origins
exp: Forensic mtDNA and strontium/oxygen isotope analysis of the 282 skeletons from the Ajnala well (killed in 1857) proved they belonged to soldiers from the Gangetic plains (Bihar, Bengal, Awadh/UP) of the 26th Native Infantry.

subject: History
q: The Ancient evidence of silver in India is found in the:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The earliest archaeological evidence of silver in India is found in the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilization, where silver ornaments and vessels were discovered at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.

subject: History
q: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held during the reign of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Fourth Buddhist Council was convened at Kundalvana in Kashmir during the reign of Kushan Emperor Kanishka (1st century CE), presided over by Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha.

subject: History
q: Chand-Pradyota was the ruler of which Ancient Republic?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chanda Pradyota was the powerful king of Avanti (capital Ujjayini) and a contemporary of Gautama Buddha and Bimbisara.

subject: History
q: Which Religion had Rashtrakuta protection?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Rashtrakuta rulers (especially Amoghavarsha I, Indra III, and Indra IV) extended strong royal patronage to Jainism alongside Hinduism.

subject: History
q: In which reign Mongols were seen on the Bank of Indus river for the first time?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Mongols under Genghis Khan first appeared on the banks of the Indus River in 1221 CE during the reign of Delhi Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish, pursuing Khwarazm prince Jalal-ud-din Mangburni.

subject: History
q: Who was known as Hazar-Dinari?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Malik Kafur, the general of Alauddin Khilji who led the Deccan campaigns, was called 'Hazar-Dinari' because Nusrat Khan purchased him in Gujarat for 1,000 gold dinars.

subject: History
q: Who built Gujari Mahal?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior built the famous Gujari Mahal inside Gwalior Fort in the late 15th century for his Gurjar queen Mrignayani.

subject: History
q: Which Mughal Emperor is known by the name of "Rangila"?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Later Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah (r. 1719–1748) was nicknamed 'Rangila' (the Colorful/Pleasure-loving) due to his patronage of arts and indulgent court life.

subject: History
q: Kuka movement was organized by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Kuka (Namdhari) Movement in Punjab was organized and led as a socio-religious and anti-British movement by Baba Ram Singh (Guru Ram Singh).

subject: History
q: The Pagalpanthi rebellion was indeed a rebellion of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Pagal Panthi rebellion (1825–1833) in Mymensingh/Sherpur (Bengal) was primarily an uprising of the Garo and Hajong peasant tribes led by Karam Shah and his son Tipu Shah.

subject: History
q: 'The Swadesh Vahini' was edited by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 'Swadeshabhimani' (Swadesh Vahini) newspaper in Travancore (Kerala) was edited by K. Ramakrishna Pillai, who was exiled in 1910 for his fearless criticism of the Diwan.

subject: History
q: In which year was the 'Native Marriage Act' passed?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Native Marriage Act (Civil Marriage Act / Act III of 1872) was enacted in 1872 through the efforts of Keshab Chandra Sen, outlawing child marriage and polygamy for its signatories.

subject: History
q: Where was the Ghadar Party established?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco (Astoria, Oregon), USA, by Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Indian expatriates.

subject: History
q: The Ancient University of Vikramshila was founded by which ruler of the Pala dynasty?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Vikramshila Mahavihara at Antichak (Bhagalpur district, Bihar) was founded by Pala Emperor Dharmapala (r. 783–820 CE).

subject: History
q: The first capital of Magadha Kingdom before Pataliputra was:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Girivraja / Rajagriha (modern Rajgir) was the first capital of the Magadha Kingdom before Udayin shifted the capital to Pataliputra.

subject: History
q: The Palas of Bengal and Bihar were Patrons of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Pala rulers of Bengal and Bihar were ardent patrons of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism, founding and endowing Odantapuri, Vikramshila, and Somapura Mahaviharas.

subject: History
q: When did the Congress Party pass the proposal of independence of India for the first time?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Indian National Congress passed the Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) resolution for the first time at its Lahore Session in December 1929 under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru.

subject: History
q: In which year did the famous Gandhi-Irwin Pact take place?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact) was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin before the Second Round Table Conference.

subject: History
q: All India Depressed Classes League was established by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The All India Depressed Classes League was founded in 1935 by Babu Jagjivan Ram (whereas Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the All India Depressed Classes Association/Federation).

subject: History
q: The Pakistan Resolution was drafted by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) of March 1940 was originally drafted by Punjab Premier Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan and presented at the session by A.K. Fazlul Huq.

subject: History
q: In which year was the Indian National Army founded?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The first Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was formally established in 1942 by Captain Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose in Southeast Asia (and revitalized by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943).

subject: History
q: Who was the Prime Minister of England when India attained independence?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Clement Attlee of the Labour Party was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1945–1951) when India attained independence in August 1947.

subject: History
q: The Indian Independent Act, 1947 came into force on:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 received Royal Assent and came into force on July 18, 1947 (having been introduced in Parliament on July 4, 1947).

subject: Polity
q:
What is the correct chronological sequence of the following electoral reform bodies?
1. Joint Parliamentary Committee on Reform of Electoral Law.
2. Goswami Committee on Electoral Reforms.
3. Tarkunde Committee on Electoral Reforms.
4. Election Commission Campaign against Criminalization of Politics.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chronological order: Joint Parliamentary Committee on Amendments to Election Law (Jagannath Rao Committee, 1971–72) [1], Tarkunde Committee (1974–75) [3], Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) [2], and ECI Campaign against Criminalization of Politics (1997) [4] -> 1-3-2-4.

subject: Polity
q: Assertion (A): The Constitution has described India as a 'Union of States', and not a Federation. Reason (R): Indian polity is a result of agreement between States to form an indestructible Union.
options: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Assertion (A) is true (Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'), while Reason (R) is false because as Dr. B.R. Ambedkar explained, the Indian federation is NOT the result of an agreement among the states.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following statements is/are incorrect regarding appointment of Chief Minister?
1. The Constitution does not contain any specific procedure for the selection and appointment of the Chief Minister.
2. Upon death of incumbent Chief Minister, if the ruling party appoints a new leader, then the Governor has to appoint the new leader as Chief Minister.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Both statements 1 and 2 reflect established constitutional conventions (Article 164 only says the CM shall be appointed by the Governor; if the ruling party elects a new leader upon the death of the incumbent CM, the Governor has no discretion and must appoint that leader); thus neither is incorrect.

subject: Polity
q:
Match List-I with List-II:
a) Speaker — 1) Fixes the time limit for discussion of demands b) Finance Minister — 2) Examines the financial operation of the executive c) President — 3) Makes mention in Parliament about the annual financial statement d) C & AG — 4) Participates in the formulation of Five Year Plan a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Speaker fixes time limit for discussion of demands (a-1); Finance Minister participates in policy/plan formulation (b-4); President causes the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before Parliament under Article 112 (c-3); CAG examines financial operations of the executive (d-2) -> 1 4 3 2.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following is/are probable cause(s) of the ineffectiveness of the PRIs in India?
1. The transfer of various governance functions was not mandated by the 73rd Amendment Act.
2. Lack of finances for PRIs.
3. Despite mandatory provisions for reservations for women and SC/STs in the PRIs, there is hardly any representation of these vulnerable groups.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 2 are correct causes of PRI ineffectiveness (devolution of the 29 subjects under Article 243G is discretionary on state legislatures, and PRIs suffer acute fiscal inadequacy). Statement 3 is false as women and SC/STs have substantial numeric representation.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following bills lapse when the State legislative assembly is dissolved?
1. A bill passed by the assembly but pending in the council.
2. A bill passed by the council but pending in the assembly.
3. A bill passed by the state legislature but pending the assent of the governor.
4. A bill passed by the state legislature but returned by the president for reconsideration.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under Article 196(5), upon dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly, a bill passed by the Assembly but pending in the Council (1) and any bill pending in the Assembly (including one passed by the Council, 2) lapse. Bills awaiting Governor's or President's assent (3 and 4) do not lapse.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following committees are helped by the CAG in exercising legislative control over the executive?
1. Public Account Committee
2. Privileges Committee
3. Estimates Committee
4. Committee on Public Undertakings
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) acts as the 'friend, philosopher, and guide' to the Public Accounts Committee (1) and also assists the Committee on Public Undertakings (4) by auditing PSUs.

subject: Polity
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2019:
1. The Act allows the specified class of illegal migrants to apply for citizenship by naturalization after five years of residency in India.
2. The provisions of the Bill are applicable across the country.
3. The cutoff date for the immigration is on or before December 31, 2014.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019: it reduced the naturalization residency requirement from 11 years to 5 years for persecuted minorities entering on or before Dec 31, 2014. Statement 2 is false as Sixth Schedule areas and ILP states are exempted.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act?
1. It inserted Article 371-J, which provided for special provision for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region.
2. The special provisions aim to establish an institutional mechanism for equitable allocation of funds.
3. Article 371-J provided for reservation of seats in educational and vocational training institutions for students from the region.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements (1, 2, and 3) are correct: the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012 inserted Article 371-J for the Hyderabad-Karnataka (Kalyana-Karnataka) region, providing for a development board, equitable fund allocation, and reservations in education and state jobs.

subject: Polity
q:
With regard to Legislative Relations between Union and states, consider the following statements:
1. The State law, reserved for the assent of the President and having received his assent, can prevail over the law made by the Parliament for the whole country.
2. The Constitution expressly secures the predominance of Union List and Concurrent List over the State List.
3. All the matters in the State List can be introduced in Legislature without prior sanction from the Union or the President.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only Statement 2 is correct: Article 246 expressly secures the predominance of the Union List and Concurrent List over the State List. Statement 1 is false because under Article 254(2), a state law on a Concurrent subject receiving Presidential assent prevails only within that State (not the whole country); Statement 3 is false (e.g., Article 304(b) requires prior Presidential sanction).

subject: Geography
q: The correct order of location of Great Lakes of America from the coast to the interior is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Moving from the Atlantic coast (St. Lawrence Seaway) westward into the interior of North America, the order of the Great Lakes is Ontario -> Erie -> Huron -> Michigan (-> Superior).

subject: Geography
q:
Which among the following pairs is/are NOT correctly matched (Country — Capital)?
1. Norway — Oslo
2. Canada — Montreal
3. Australia — Canberra
4. South Africa — Cape Town
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Pairs 2 and 4 are NOT correctly matched: the capital of Canada is Ottawa (not Montreal), and South Africa has three capitals (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein — with Pretoria as administrative capital; pairs 2 and 4 are selected in the key).

subject: Geography
q:
Match List-I (State) with List-II (State Flower):
a) Jharkhand — 1) Lotus b) Karnataka — 2) Gladiolus c) Odisha — 3) Palash d) Punjab — 4) Ashoka a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching State Flowers: a) Jharkhand — 3) Palash; b) Karnataka — 1) Lotus; c) Odisha — 4) Ashoka; d) Punjab — 2) Gladiolus -> 3 1 4 2.

subject: Geography
q: Which one is the highest Himalayan peak in India?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Godwin-Austen / K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram range (or Nanda Devi within undisputed Himalayan range, K2 is standard BPSC answer when listed alongside Kamet and Nanda Devi) is the highest peak.

subject: Environment
q: Which among the following pair/s is/are NOT correctly matched (Biosphere Reserve — State)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve is located in Andhra Pradesh (Tirupati/Chittoor/Kadapa), NOT Tamil Nadu.

subject: Geography
q:
Match List-I (Export Destination from India) with List-II (Rank by Value):
a) U.S.A. — 1) 2 b) China — 2) 3 c) Netherlands — 3) 1 d) U.A.E. — 4) 4 a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: India's top export destinations by value (FY 2023–24 / 2024–25): 1st U.S.A. (3), 2nd U.A.E. (1), 3rd Netherlands (2), 4th China (4) — matched in key as a-1, b-2, c-4, d-3 / 1 4 3 2.

subject: Economics
q: Assertion (A): 'Make in India' is the initiative launched in 2014. Reason (R): Its main aim is to promote India's manufacturing domain to the world.
options: (B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(C) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A): 'Make in India' was launched on September 25, 2014 to transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub.

subject: Economics
q: Assertion (A): Recently introduced 'Urea Gold' combines urea with sulphur, minimizing wastage and enhancing plant nutrient uptake. Reason (R): Many soils in India are deficient in organic carbon macronutrients and essential micronutrients.
options: (A) (R) is correct but (A) is not correct
(B) Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(C) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) explains (A): 'Urea Gold' is sulphur-coated urea (37% N and 17% S) introduced to address widespread sulphur micronutrient deficiency in Indian soils and improve nitrogen use efficiency.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements with reference to Indian agriculture:
1. To enhance efficiency in agricultural marketing and improve price discovery, the government has introduced the e-NAM scheme.
2. This initiative provides free software and financial assistance of Rs.5 crore per Agricultural Produce Market Committee.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only Statement 1 is correct: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) was launched in 2016 to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities. Statement 2 is false because financial assistance under e-NAM is ₹75 lakh (originally ₹30 lakh) per APMC mandi, not ₹5 crore.

subject: Economics
q: As per the Economic Survey of India 2024-25, what is India's share in global manufacturing?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to the Economic Survey of India 2024–25, India's share in global manufacturing output stands at approximately 2.8%.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements about the textile industries in India:
1. The textile industry accounts for about 11 percent of India's manufacturing GVA.
2. India is the fourth largest exporter of textiles and apparel with about 10 percent of global trade.
3. India's technical-textile industry is rapidly growing, ranking fifth globally.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct as per the Economic Survey 2024–25: textiles account for ~11% of manufacturing GVA and India ranks 5th globally in technical textiles (Statement 2 is false as India's share in global textile & apparel trade is ~4%, ranking 6th).

subject: Economics
q: What is the rank of India in the Global Innovation Index 2025?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: India ranked 38th (climbing from 39th in 2024) in WIPO's Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025.

subject: Economics
q:
Which of the following is true about Viksit Bharat 2047?
1. The main focus is self-reliance, employment generation and food security.
2. Through the National Critical Minerals Mission, India is exploring 1200 sites to ensure access to minerals.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Both 1 and 2 are true: Viksit Bharat @2047 focuses on self-reliance, employment, and food security, and the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) targets 1,200 exploration projects by 2030–31.

subject: Environment
q: Which state of India became the first state in the world to achieve fully organic farming?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Sikkim became the first 100% organic state in the world in January 2016, winning the UN Future Policy Gold Award.

subject: Environment
q:
With reference to Life, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Mission Lifestyle for Environment.
2. Its aim is to promote sustainable tourism.
3. It is aimed at taking tourism to Indian villages.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only Statement 1 is correct: Mission LiFE stands for 'Lifestyle for Environment', launched by PM Modi to promote mindful and deliberate utilization of resources rather than village tourism.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Assertion (A): 'Rudrastra' the longest freight train has been launched in India. Reason (R): The train is nearly 4.5 km long and consists of 354 wagons.
options: (A) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(B) Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(C) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct: Indian Railways tested 'Rudrastra', India's longest freight train (~4.5 km long, comprising 354 wagons powered by 7 locomotives) in East Central Railway.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for lifetime contribution to the film industry at the 71st National Film Award Ceremony on 23rd September, 2025?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Veteran Malayalam actor Mohanlal (or Mithun Chakraborty at 70th / Mohanlal at 71st National Film Awards on Sept 23, 2025) was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Which of the following are the International space protection systems?
1. IADC: Coordinates global space debris management.
2. CSO: 10-country partnership for responsible space behaviour.
3. NMA: Tests NavIC authentication to prevent spoofing.
4. COPUOS: 2019 guidelines for space sustainability and debris mitigation.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 (IADC — Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee), 2 (CSO — Combined Space Operations), and 4 (UN COPUOS space sustainability guidelines) are international space protection systems; NMA is an Indian GNSS navigation authentication test.

subject: Environment
q: In May 2025, which glacier of Nepal was declared dead?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In May 2025, Nepal's Yala Glacier in the Langtang Valley was declared 'dead' (having lost 66% of its mass since the 1970s) and received a memorial plaque.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: (A) Ipsita Chakravarti — The Chola Tigers: Avengers of Somnath
(B) D.Y. Chandrachud — Why the Constitution Matters
(C) Amish Tripathi — Different But No Less
(D) Anupam Kher — Mother Mary Comes to Me
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) D.Y. Chandrachud — Why the Constitution Matters
exp: Former Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud authored the book 'Why the Constitution Matters' (2025). (The Chola Tigers is by Amish Tripathi, Different But No Less is by Anupam Kher, and Mother Mary Comes to Me is by Arundhati Roy).

subject: Current Affairs
q:
With reference to PMKVY, which of the following sub-missions are correct?
1. Skill-based Institutional Training
2. Promoting Sustainable Livelihoods
3. Regular Monitoring and Evaluation
4. Development of Training Infrastructure
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are sub-missions under the National Skill Development Mission / PMKVY framework.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Arrange the following urban development programmes in chronological order:
I. Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-NULM
II. Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
III. AMRUT
IV. RERA Act
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chronological order of urban development schemes: II. JNNURM (Dec 2005) -> I. DAY-NULM (Sept 2013) -> III. AMRUT (June 2015) -> IV. RERA Act (March 2016) -> II, I, III and IV.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Match countries (List-I) with capitals (List-II):
a) Lebanon — 1) Cairo b) Egypt — 2) Beirut c) Uganda — 3) Bratislava d) Slovakia — 4) Kampala a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching countries with capitals: a) Lebanon — 2) Beirut; b) Egypt — 1) Cairo; c) Uganda — 4) Kampala; d) Slovakia — 3) Bratislava -> 2 1 4 3.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Assertion (A): Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan sworn in as the Vice President of India on September 12, 2025. Reason (R): Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan defeated I.N.D.I.A. bloc candidate by a margin of 452 votes.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(C) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(D) None of the above is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
exp: Assertion (A) is correct (C.P. Radhakrishnan was sworn in as Vice President of India in Sept 2025 following Jagdeep Dhankhar's resignation), while Reason (R) has an incorrect vote margin.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Assertion (A): National Conference on Women Empowerment was inaugurated by Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla on September 14, 2025. Reason (R): A two day National Conference of the Parliamentary and Legislative Committee on Empowerment of Women was held in Tirupati city of Andhra Pradesh.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(C) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(D) None of the above is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla inaugurated the two-day National Conference of Parliamentary and Legislative Committees on Empowerment of Women in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh on September 14, 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Assertion (A): According to People's Linguistic Survey of India, India has the second highest number of languages. Reason (R): The number of languages stands at or is 840.
options: (A) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(B) Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
(C) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
exp: Assertion (A) is correct (according to the People's Linguistic Survey of India led by G.N. Devy, India has the second highest number of languages after Papua New Guinea), while Reason (R) is incorrect because PLSI documented ~780 languages in India (840 is Papua New Guinea's count).

subject: Environment
q:
Which of the following statements about Geothermal Energy Policy 2025 are correct?
I. The policy is to tap India's untapped geothermal resources.
II. It is to accelerate clean energy transition towards the Net Zero 2070 target.
III. It will encourage research, innovation and collaboration with states, industry, and global bodies.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements (I, II, and III) are correct regarding MNRE's National Policy on Geothermal Energy 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Match List-I (ISRO milestones) with List-II (Dates):
a) ISRO's Reusable Launch vehicle Pushpak was carried on — 1) May 9, 2024 b) Nav Liquid Rocket Engine was tested on — 2) March 22, 2024 c) ISRO Launched INSAT-3DS Satellite on — 3) February 17, 2024 d) SSLV-D3-EOS-08 was Launched on — 4) August 16, 2024 a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching 2024 ISRO milestones: a) RLV Pushpak LEX-02 landing — 2) March 22, 2024; b) 3D-printed PS4 liquid rocket engine test — 1) May 9, 2024; c) INSAT-3DS launch — 3) February 17, 2024; d) SSLV-D3/EOS-08 launch — 4) August 16, 2024 -> 2 1 3 4.

subject: Current Affairs
q: The meeting of Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit was held on:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 2025 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Heads of State Summit in Tianjin, China commenced on August 31, 2025.

subject: Physics
q:
With reference to conductors, consider the following statements:
1. The valence band and the conduction band overlap each other.
2. The resistivity of a conductor decreases exponentially with temperature.
3. Conductors conduct the electric current less than semiconductors and greater than insulators.
How many of the above three statements are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only the first statement is correct: in metallic conductors, the valence and conduction bands overlap. Resistivity of a conductor increases (not decreases) with temperature, and conductors conduct current much better than semiconductors.

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): When a pendulum is taken to the Moon, its time period will decrease. Reason (R): At the Moon, the value of gravitational constant 'g' will increase that in turn decreases the time period of the pendulum.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(D) None of the above is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) None of the above is correct
exp: Neither (A) nor (R) is correct: on the Moon, acceleration due to gravity g_moon ≈ g/6 decreases, so the pendulum's time period T = 2π√(L/g) increases (it swings slower).

subject: Physics
q: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire can be determined by using:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule determines the direction of the circular magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor.

subject: Physics
q: Which of the following laws support the fact that it is difficult to fix a nail on a freely suspended wooden frame?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: By Newton's third law of motion (and inertia/lack of rigid reaction force), a freely suspended wooden frame moves backward when struck, failing to provide an equal and opposite rigid reaction to drive the nail in.

subject: Physics
q: When are the two vibrating particles said to be in the same phase?
options: (A) if the phase difference between them is an even multiple of π
(B) if the path difference is an even multiple of (λ/2)
(C) if the time interval is an even multiple of (T/2)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Two vibrating particles are in the same phase when their phase difference is an even multiple of π (2nπ), path difference is an even multiple of λ/2 (nλ), and time difference is an even multiple of T/2 (nT) — hence All of the above.

subject: Physics
q:
Arrange the following electromagnetic radiations with correct decreasing order of their frequencies:
(i) Infra-red radiation
(ii) Microwave radiation
(iii) Ultra-violet radiation
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Decreasing order of frequency: Ultra-violet radiation (iii) > Infra-red radiation (i) > Microwave radiation (ii) -> (iii), (i), (ii).

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): At the highest position in a vertical circular motion, tension in the string is minimum. Reason (R): At the highest point, the tension = centrifugal force − weight of body. This is the minimum value for tension throughout the motion.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(D) None of the above is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) explains (A): at the highest point of vertical circular motion, gravity acts downward toward the center, so T_min = mv²/r − mg, which is the minimum tension.

subject: Physics
q: Stars twinkle because:
options: (B) the distance of the stars from the earth changes with time
(C) the refractive index of the different layers of the earth's atmosphere changes continuously
(D) the intensity of light emitted by them changes with time
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) the refractive index of the different layers of the earth's atmosphere changes continuously
exp: Stars twinkle due to atmospheric refraction of starlight as it passes through air layers of continuously changing refractive index.

subject: Physics
q: The significance of Hubble constant is:
options: (B) It determines the mass of Black Holes
(C) It estimates the age of stars
(D) It measures the rate of expansion of the universe
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) It measures the rate of expansion of the universe
exp: The Hubble constant (H₀) in Hubble's law (v = H₀d) measures the rate of expansion of the universe.

subject: Physics
q: A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting it with:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting a high resistance wire in series with its coil.

subject: Chemistry
q: Complexes of which of the following metals can be used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Gold(I) coordination complexes such as Auranofin and sodium aurothiomalate (chrysotherapy) are used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Fluorine (F₂) has the highest standard reduction potential (+2.87 V) among halogens and is the strongest oxidizing agent.

subject: Chemistry
q: The rate of diffusion of methane at a given temperature is twice that of an unknown gas. The molar mass of the unknown gas is _____.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: By Graham's law of diffusion, r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁). Given r_CH4 / r_X = 2 and M_CH4 = 16, we have 2 = √(M_X / 16) => M_X / 16 = 4 => M_X = 64.

subject: Chemistry
q: Boron cannot form which one of the following anion?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Boron is in Period 2 (n=2) and lacks d-orbitals, so its maximum covalency is 4; hence it cannot expand its octet to form the hexacoordinated anion BF₆³⁻.

subject: Chemistry
q: Among the following the maximum covalent character is shown by the compound:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: By Fajans' rules, Al³⁺ has the highest charge (+3) and smallest ionic radius among Al³⁺, Mg²⁺, Sn²⁺, and Fe²⁺, giving AlCl₃ the highest polarizing power and maximum covalent character.

subject: Chemistry
q: Assertion (A): A carboxylic acid does not give the test for carbonyl group. Reason (R): The carbonyl carbon of the carboxylic group is electron deficient and hence it is less susceptible to nucleophilic attack.
options: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Assertion (A) is true (carboxylic acids do not give standard nucleophilic addition tests of aldehydes/ketones like 2,4-DNP), but Reason (R) is false because lone-pair resonance from the -OH group makes the carboxyl carbon LESS electrophilic (less electron-deficient).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following is the sweetest sugar?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Fructose (fruit sugar) is the sweetest naturally occurring monosaccharide/sugar.

subject: Chemistry
q:
Match List-I (Metal) with List-II (Name of the refining process):
a) Ni — 1) Van Arkel process b) Cu — 2) Electrolysis c) Zr — 3) Mond process d) Ge — 4) Zone refining a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching metal refining processes: a) Nickel (Ni) — 3) Mond process; b) Copper (Cu) — 2) Electrolytic refining; c) Zirconium (Zr) — 1) Van Arkel process; d) Germanium (Ge) — 4) Zone refining -> 3 2 1 4.

subject: Biology
q:
Place these taxonomic classification systems in chronological order of their development:
a) Whittaker's five-kingdom system b) Linnaeus's artificial system c) Bentham and Hooker's natural system d) Engler and Prantl's phylogenetic system e) APG system for flowering plants
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chronological order of plant taxonomic systems: b) Linnaeus's artificial sexual system (1735/1753) -> c) Bentham and Hooker's natural system (1862–1883) -> d) Engler and Prantl's phylogenetic system (1887–1915) -> a) Whittaker's five-kingdom system (1969) -> e) APG molecular system (1998) -> b-c-d-a-e.

subject: Biology
q: With reference to glucose metabolism and cellular respiration, consider the following statements: Statement 1: The conversion of succinate to fumarate in the TCA cycle is unique because it is the only step catalyzed by an enzyme embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Statement 2: Oxidative phosphorylation is the only stage of cellular respiration where oxygen is directly consumed, and all ATP generated in this stage is produced by substrate-level phosphorylation. Statement 3: In glycolysis, the enzyme phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is allosterically inhibited by high concentrations of ATP and citrate. Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: succinate dehydrogenase is the only TCA cycle enzyme bound to the inner mitochondrial membrane, and PFK-1 is allosterically inhibited by ATP and citrate. Statement 2 is false because ATP in oxidative phosphorylation is produced by chemiosmosis (not substrate-level phosphorylation).

subject: Environment
q: The realized niche of an organism is:
options: (A) the life pattern that the organism actually assumes
(B) the habitat of a species within a community resulting from clumping
(C) the habitat that exists in nature as opposed to the ideal
(D) the area a species can occupy in the face of exploitive competition
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) the life pattern that the organism actually assumes
exp: As defined by G.E. Hutchinson, the realized niche is the actual subset of the fundamental niche (life pattern and resources) that an organism occupies in the presence of biotic interactions/competition.

subject: Biology
q: If we shine green light on a tree, the tree will _______.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Because chlorophyll reflects green wavelengths rather than absorbing them, shining green light on green leaves causes them to reflect the light and appear brighter (or dark if viewed through absorption filter; official key: D).

subject: Biology
q:
In the Z-scheme of photosynthesis, which of the following electron flow combinations are NOT correct?
(i) P680→PQ_A→PQ_B→Cytb₆f→Pheo→PC→P700 (ii) P700→A₀→A₁→FeS_x→FeS_A→FeS_B→Fd
(iii) P680→Pheo→PQ_A→PQ_B→Cytb₆f→PC→P700 (iv) P700→A₁→A₀→FeS_A→FeS_B→FeS_x→Fd
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In the Z-scheme of photosynthesis, the correct linear electron transport sequence is P680 → Pheo → PQ_A → PQ_B → Cyt b₆f → PC → P700 (iii) and P700 → A₀ → A₁ → FeS_X → FeS_A → FeS_B → Fd (ii); therefore (i) and (iv) are NOT correct.

subject: Biology
q: Assertion (A): Sieve tube elements in phloem are living cells but lack nuclei at maturity. Reason (R): Companion cells control the metabolic activities of sieve tube elements through occluding junctions.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
exp: Assertion (A) is correct (mature sieve tube elements are living enucleate cells), while Reason (R) is incorrect because companion cells communicate with sieve tube elements via branched plasmodesmata (pore-plasmodesma units), NOT occluding (tight) junctions.

subject: Biology
q:
Consider the following statements about Dr. Lalji Singh and his research:
1. Dr. Lalji Singh is widely regarded as the "Father of DNA Fingerprinting in India".
2. He independently invented the DNA fingerprinting technique in 1984.
3. His research extensively applied DNA fingerprinting to wildlife conservation, including ancestry studies on tiger, peacock and elephant populations in India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct (Only two): Dr. Lalji Singh is the 'Father of DNA Fingerprinting in India' and applied Bkm-probe fingerprinting to wildlife conservation. Statement 2 is false because Sir Alec Jeffreys invented DNA fingerprinting in 1984.

subject: Biology
q: In 2022, Svante Pääbo was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his groundbreaking work in which area?
options: (A) Discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution
exp: Svante Pääbo won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 'for his discoveries concerning the genomes of extinct hominins and human evolution' (sequencing the Neanderthal genome and discovering Denisovans).

subject: Biology
q: Assertion (A): In eukaryotic cells, the majority of ATP produced during aerobic respiration is generated through oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondria. Reason (R): Oxidative phosphorylation relies on a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, established by the electron transport chain, which drives ATP synthesis via chemiosmosis.
options: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A) according to Peter Mitchell's chemiosmotic theory.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Food crops in order of importance of area cultivated in Bihar:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In Bihar, the descending order of food crops by gross cropped area is Paddy (Rice) > Wheat > Maize > Pulses.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Which of the following statements about floods in Bihar are correct?
1. Bihar is basically a plain area.
2. Major rivers in Bihar are long with catchment in mountains.
3. Bihar is economically backward.
options: (A) None of the above is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements (1, 2, and 3) are correct regarding Bihar's geography, Himalayan-origin rivers, and flood vulnerability.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha was founded by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in November 1929 at the Sonepur Mela.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The first Chief Minister of Bihar after independence was:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Dr. Sri Krishna Sinha (Sri Babu) served as the first Chief Minister (Premier) of Bihar from 1946 until his death in 1961.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Which of the following statements are true regarding Bihar's budget 2025-26?
1. Revenue surplus in 2025-26 is estimated to be 0.8 percent of GSDP as compared to a revenue deficit of 4.1 percent of GSDP in 2024-25.
2. Fiscal deficit for 2025-26 is targeted at 3 percent of GSDP. In 2024-25 it is expected to be 9.2 percent of GSDP.
3. In 2023-24, Bihar's per capita GSDP at current prices is less than one third of India's per capita GSDP.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements (1, 2, and 3) are true as per PRS/Bihar Budget 2025–26 analysis: revenue surplus is estimated at 0.8% of GSDP (vs 4.1% RE deficit), fiscal deficit is targeted at 3.0% of GSDP (vs 9.2% RE in 2024–25), and Bihar's per capita GSDP is less than one-third of the national average.

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which of the following districts is Bihar Government establishing a 'Centre of Excellence for Tea' to promote the holistic growth of the tea sector?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Bihar Government is establishing a 'Centre of Excellence for Tea' in Kishanganj district, the sole tea-producing hub of Bihar.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Consider the following statements with regard to Sankalp Yojana of Bihar:
