1. Sankalp Yojana is a centrally sponsored scheme funded by the World Bank.
2. It has introduced innovative programmes to increase the productivity of agriculture in Bihar.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Only Statement 1 is correct: SANKALP (Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion) is a World Bank-assisted centrally sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Skill Development, not an agricultural productivity scheme.

subject: Biology
q: Assertion (A): The mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) haplogroups M31 and M32 observed in the Onge and Great Andamanese populations represent ancient maternal lineages that have undergone in situ evolution on the Andaman Islands in isolation from mainland South Asian populations. Reason (R): Complete mtDNA sequencing revealed that the coding region mutations defining M31 and M32 do not overlap with autochthonous mainland Indian M lineages.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: Whole-mtDNA genome studies (Thangaraj et al.) demonstrated that Andamanese haplogroups M31 and M32 carry unique non-overlapping coding mutations, confirming long-term in situ isolation on the Andaman Islands.

subject: Economics
q: The GST Reforms 2025, by lowering GST rates on essential and mass-consumption items, primarily addressed two major economic challenges: employment generation and ______.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 2025 GST rate reductions were designed to boost household consumption by improving affordability alongside employment generation.

subject: History
q: Which of the following Gods is referred to as 'Ritasya Gopa' in the Rigveda?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In the Rigveda, Varuna is revered as 'Ritasya Gopa' — the guardian and upholder of the cosmic and moral order (Rita).

subject: History
q: Which area did Alexander grant to King Pururaj?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: After the Battle of the Hydaspes (326 BCE), Alexander the Great restored Porus (Pururaj) and granted him territories between the Jhelum (Hydaspes) and Beas (Hyphasis) rivers.

subject: History
q: Ashoka's high officers went on 'Nirikchatan' for administrative visit in Ujjaini and Taxila in every .......... years.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to Ashoka's Separate Rock Edict I (Kalinga Edict), while imperial officers toured every 5 years, the provincial governors at Ujjayini and Taxila sent officers on inspection (Anusamyana/Nirikshan) every 3 years.

subject: History
q: Which one of the following scholars was associated with King Kanishka?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Ashvaghosha (author of Buddhacharita and Saundarananda) was the court poet and spiritual advisor of Kushan king Kanishka.

subject: History
q: On which victory Alauddin Khilji was granted governorship of Awadh in addition to Kara?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Following his successful raid on Bhilsa (Vidisha) in 1292 CE, Sultan Jalaluddin Khilji rewarded Alauddin Khilji with the governorship of Awadh in addition to Kara-Manikpur.

subject: History
q: Under which Sultan of Delhi did Muhammad Bin Tughlaq work before becoming the ruler?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Before his father Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's accession, Jauna Khan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) served as Akhur-bek (Master of the Horse) under Khusrau Shah.

subject: History
q:
Who led the Mughal army in the battle of Haldighati?
(1) Bhagwan Das
(2) Man Singh
(3) Akbar
(4) Asaf Khan
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In the Battle of Haldighati (18 June 1576), the Mughal army was led by Kunwar Man Singh of Amber and Asaf Khan (2 and 4).

subject: History
q: In which field was the terminology 'Rai' connected during Shershah's period?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: During Sher Shah Suri's reign, 'Rai' (or Ray) was the official schedule/table of crop yields and land revenue assessment rates.

subject: History
q: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched? (Institution — Year of establishment)
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Calcutta Hindu College was established in 1817 (by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, David Hare, and Radhakanta Deb), not 1798. Calcutta Madrasa (1781), Benaras Sanskrit College (1791), and Fort William College (1800) are correctly matched.

subject: History
q:
Who of the following were sent to the court of the Shah of Persia (Iran) as British envoy during Lord Wellesley's period from India?
(1) John Malcolm
(2) Mehdi Ali Khan
(3) Raja Shiv Prasad
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Lord Wellesley sent Mehdi Ali Khan (1799) and Captain John Malcolm (1800) as British envoys to the court of Fateh Ali Shah of Persia to counter French and Afghan threats (Both 1 and 2).

subject: History
q: Under whose Chairmanship was an irrigation commission set up in 1901?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Lord Curzon appointed the Indian Irrigation Commission in 1901 under the chairmanship of Sir Colin Scott-Moncrieff.

subject: History
q: Which of the following rulers merged Avanti in the Magadh Empire after the victory?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Shishunaga, founder of the Shishunaga dynasty, defeated the Pradyota dynasty and permanently annexed the kingdom of Avanti into the Magadha Empire.

subject: History
q: On whom was an attempt to murder made at Muzaffarpur in 1908?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: On 30 April 1908 at Muzaffarpur (Bihar), revolutionaries Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb aimed at Magistrate Douglas Kingsford.

subject: History
q: Who was the first President of Indian National Conference held in December 1883?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Ananda Mohan Bose presided over the first session of the Indian National Conference organized by Surendranath Banerjee in Calcutta in December 1883.

subject: History
q: Which Indian freedom fighter said, "We will not achieve any success in our labour if we croak once a year like a frog"?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak criticized the mendicant politics of the early Moderates by remarking, 'We will not achieve any success in our labours if we croak once a year like a frog.'

subject: History
q: Which Viceroy's period was called "Missions, Omissions and Commissions"?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Lord Curzon's viceroyalty (1899–1905) was dubbed a 'reign of Missions, Omissions, and Commissions' due to his numerous administrative commissions (Police, Universities, Irrigation, Famine).

subject: History
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lucknow Pact 1916:
1. This was marked for re-union of Moderate and Extremists parties.
2. B. G. Tilak and Annie Besant dominated the Lucknow session.
3. The Congress and League pact was done for United Scheme of Constitutional Reforms.
4. Ferozshah Mehta participated in this session.
Select the correct statements:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct regarding the 1916 Lucknow Session (presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar). Statement 4 is incorrect because Pherozeshah Mehta had already died in November 1915.

subject: History
q: In which month of 1905 was the 'Partition of Bengal' declared?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The official decision/announcement of the Partition of Bengal was declared by the British Government on 19/20 July 1905 (and came into effect on 16 October 1905).

subject: History
q: In which language was the first issue of 'Gadar' magazine published?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The first issue of the 'Ghadar' newspaper was published from San Francisco on 1 November 1913 in Urdu (followed by the Gurmukhi edition in December 1913).

subject: History
q: Who hired the 'Camagatamaru' ship to go to Vancouver?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Baba Gurdit Singh Sandhu chartered the Japanese steamship 'Komagata Maru' in 1914 to carry 376 Indian passengers from Hong Kong to Vancouver, Canada.

subject: History
q: What was the age of Mahatma Gandhi when he returned to India from South Africa?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Born on 2 October 1869, Mahatma Gandhi was 45 years old when he returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.

subject: History
q: Who of the following died on the day of commencement of Non-co-operation Movement?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak passed away in Bombay on 1 August 1920, the very day the Non-Cooperation Movement was launched.

subject: History
q: Which date is observed as 'Direct Action Day' by the Muslim League in 1946?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The All-India Muslim League observed 16 August 1946 as 'Direct Action Day', triggering the Great Calcutta Killings.

subject: Polity
q: The 93rd Amendment of the Constitution relates to:
options: (B) Reservation for women in legislative assemblies
(C) Reservation for Other Backward Classes in educational institutions
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Reservation for Other Backward Classes in educational institutions
exp: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005 inserted clause (5) in Article 15, empowering the State to make special provisions (reservations) for socially and educationally backward classes (OBCs), SCs, and STs in admission to educational institutions.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following provisions in the Indian Constitution are NOT correctly matched?
1. Article 280 — Election Commission of India
2. Article 315 — Union Public Service Commission
3. Article 324 — Finance Commission
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Pairs 1 and 3 are NOT correctly matched: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, while Article 324 provides for the Election Commission of India. Pair 2 (Article 315 — UPSC) is correctly matched.

subject: Polity
q: Who is the author of 'Rethinking Democracy'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The celebrated political science book 'Rethinking Democracy' (2005) was authored by Prof. Rajni Kothari.

subject: Polity
q: During which Prime Minister's tenure was the National Commission to Review the Constitution formed?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), chaired by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah, was set up in February 2000 during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

subject: Polity
q: Assertion (A): The Supreme Court of India cannot declare a bad law valid. Reason (R): The Supreme Court of India follows the procedure established by law.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are correct; but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Assertion (A) is wrong and Reason (R) is correct in traditional constitutional jurisprudence: under Article 21 ('procedure established by law' as originally interpreted in A.K. Gopalan), the Supreme Court could only examine whether a law was enacted by a competent legislature following prescribed procedure, not strike down a law merely for being 'bad' or unjust.

subject: Polity
q: Match List I with List II: (a) Estimates Committee — (i) Examination of Appropriated Accounts (b) Public Accounts Committee — (ii) Suggestions for Economy in Expenditure (c) Subordinate Legislation — (iii) Examination of rules made by executive departments under laws passed by the legislature (d) Public Sector Undertakings Committee — (iv) Review of the performance of public sector undertakings a b c d
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Parliamentary Committees: (a) Estimates Committee — (ii) Suggestions for economy in expenditure; (b) Public Accounts Committee — (i) Examination of appropriation accounts; (c) Committee on Subordinate Legislation — (iii); (d) Committee on Public Undertakings — (iv) -> (ii) (i) (iii) (iv).

subject: Polity
q: Assertion (A): According to Article 312 of the Indian Constitution, the Rajya Sabha can create new All India Services in the national interest. Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha can define national interest in a comprehensive manner.
options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true; but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Assertion (A) is true (under Article 312, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting in the national interest, Parliament can create new All India Services), whereas Reason (R) is false.

subject: Polity
q:
With reference to the Modi government, consider the following statements:
1. The Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched on 2 October 2014.
2. The Agnipath scheme for the Indian armed forces was launched in 2022.
3. The PM Mudra Yojana scheme was launched in 2015 to provide subsidized loans to Micro and Small Enterprises.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements are correct: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014, PM MUDRA Yojana was launched on 8 April 2015, and the Agnipath defence recruitment scheme was launched in June 2022.

subject: Polity
q: In which article is the provision on reservation of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to Panchayat given?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Article 243D of the Indian Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in Panchayats.

subject: Polity
q: In January 2015, who among the following was appointed as the first C.E.O. of NITI Aayog of India?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Sindhushree Khullar (IAS) was appointed as the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog in January 2015.

subject: Polity
q:
In which order were the following placed in the Constitution of India?
(i) Right to freedom of religion
(ii) Change of state name
(iii) Imposition of President's rule in a state
(iv) Mention about the Indian Administrative Services
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Constitutional order by Article number: (ii) Change of state name (Article 3) -> (i) Right to freedom of religion (Articles 25–28) -> (iv) All India / Indian Administrative Services (Article 312) -> (iii) Imposition of President's rule in a state (Article 356) -> (ii)(i)(iv)(iii).

subject: Geography
q: Considering the Tropic of Cancer, which of the following Iron & Steel plants is the odd one?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bokaro Steel Plant (~23°40'N) lies north of the Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N), whereas Rourkela, Bhilai, and Jamshedpur all lie south of the Tropic of Cancer.

subject: Environment
q: Given below are two statements about monsoon forests. Assertion (A): Monsoon forests are called par excellence. Reason (R): As they form the natural cover almost all over India.
options: (A) Both (A) & (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
(B) (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(C) (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both (A) & (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A)
exp: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) explains (A): Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are called the monsoon forests par excellence of India because they form the most widespread natural vegetation cover across the country.

subject: Geography
q:
Match List-I with List-II (Himalayan features):
a) Typical Hogback Topography — I. Himadri b) Flat floored structural valleys — II. Lesser Himalayas c) Broad synclinal valleys — III. Between Himadri and Himachal d) Hispar glacier — IV. Between Siwalik and Himachal
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching Himalayan geomorphological features: a) Typical Hogback Topography — IV. Between Siwalik and Himachal (Siwalik dip slopes); b) Flat-floored structural valleys (Duns) — III; c) Broad synclinal valleys (Kashmir/Kathmandu) — I/II -> a-IV, b-III, c-I, d-II.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following states are almost identical in their shapes?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh have nearly identical compact polygonal shapes along the western Himalayas.

subject: Geography
q:
Which of the following statements about Satpura is NOT correct?
I. Satpura runs west-east
II. Satpura is known as Mahadeo hills in central India
III. Satpura is the northern boundary of Peninsular plateaus
IV. Satpura is longer than Vindhya ranges
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Statement IV ('Satpura is longer than Vindhya ranges') is NOT correct: the Vindhya range (~1,050–1,200 km) is longer than the Satpura range (~900 km).

subject: Geography
q: What is 'Marusthali' in the Thar desert?
options: (B) Region of moving sands and low rainfall
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Region of moving sands and low rainfall
exp: 'Marusthali' ('Land of the Dead') refers to the arid western core of the Thar Desert characterized by shifting sand dunes (dhrian) and very low rainfall.

subject: Geography
q:
Match the rivers (List-I) with their origins (List-II):
I. Mahananda — a) Shivpuri Range, Nepal
II. Bagamati — b) Mahabharat range, Nepal
III. Kamala — c) Nampa, Nepal
IV. Ghagra — d) Sikkim
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Matching rivers with origins: I. Mahananda — d) Darjeeling/Sikkim hills; II. Bagmati — a) Shivapuri Range, Nepal; III. Kamla — b) Mahabharat Range (Sindhuli), Nepal; IV. Ghaghara (Karnali) — c) Mapchachungo/Nampa region -> I-d, II-a, III-b, IV-c.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following Dun's is in the west of Dun valley?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Pinjore Dun (Pijori Dun) in Himachal Pradesh/Haryana lies to the west of Dehra Dun valley, whereas Kotli Dun and Patli Dun lie to its east in Kumaon.

subject: Geography
q:
Consider the following statements about the Troposphere and stratosphere:
1. The Troposphere contains almost all weather phenomena.
2. The stratosphere is mostly free of clouds and has the ozone layer.
3. The Mesosphere protects Earth by burning meteoroids. Which statement is/are correct?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements (1, 2, and 3) are correct: weather phenomena occur in the Troposphere, the Stratosphere contains the ozone layer and is ideal for flying, and meteors burn up in the Mesosphere.

subject: Economics

subject: Physics
q:

exp: Statements I and II are correct: φ is the work function and no photoelectrons are emitted if hv < φ. Statement III is false because increasing light intensity increases the number of photoelectrons (photocurrent), not their maximum kinetic energy.

q:

subject: Reasoning
q:

II. Some fruits are tomatoes.

(D) Both conclusions I and II follow
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Neither conclusion I nor II follows
exp: Tomatoes only partially overlap with apples (so some tomatoes may be guavas, I does not follow) and fruits need not overlap with tomatoes (II does not follow).

subject: Reasoning
q:
Statements: All candies are chocolates. Some chocolates are lollipops. Conclusions:

(C) Both conclusions I and III follow
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: From 'All candies are chocolates', its immediate conversion 'Some candies are chocolates' (III) definitely follows, whereas negative conclusions I and II do not follow from all-affirmative premises.

subject: Reasoning

ansText: (D) Either conclusion I or III follows
exp: Conclusions I ('Some books are diaries') and III ('No diary is a book') form a complementary I-E pair; since neither follows individually, Either I or III follows.

q: OWL is encoded as 513212; DOVE is encoded as 40512250, then CRAB is encoded as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: BAT is encrypted as 3, NEST is encrypted as 232, then a possible decrypted text of 140 is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Product of alphabetical positions minus/divided by pattern: for BAT (2×1×20 = 40) or base-product encryption gives BABIM / ADAMI.

subject: Reasoning
q: ANT is encoded as ANT, BIRD is encoded as BDIR, MIAOU is encoded as AIMOU, then RAPHEL is encoded as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The letters of each word are arranged in alphabetical order: R, A, P, H, E, L sorted alphabetically is AEHLPR.

subject: Reasoning
q: AGENCY is encoded as 123456, BARLEY is encoded as 971846, LECLIN is encoded as 992034, then ABCLEY is encoded in order as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: By direct substitution/frequency mapping from the given words, ABCLEY is coded as 672941.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code, '256' means 'you are beautiful', '589' means 'birds are lovely' and '254' means 'flowers are beautiful'. The digit in the code that indicates 'flowers' is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: '2' and '5' correspond to 'are' and 'beautiful' (common to 256 and 254), leaving '4' for 'flowers'.

subject: Reasoning
q: If NWPFFO is the code for MUMBAI, the code for SHIMLA is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Shifts are +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, +6: M+1=N, U+2=W, M+3=P, B+4=F, A+5=F, I+6=O. For SHIMLA: S+1=T, H+2=J/I, I+3=L/J, M+4=Q, L+5=Q, A+6=G -> TIJOQG / TJLQQG.

subject: Reasoning
q: 'HAMLET' is related to 'VILLAGE' in the same way as 'METROPOLIS' is related to:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A hamlet is a small settlement/type of village; similarly, a metropolis is a large city.

subject: Reasoning
q: Which indicates a similar relationship as 'LOWER' has with 'WORLE'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In LOWER (1,2,3,4,5) -> WORLE (4,2,5,1,3) or rearranging the same letters: AMONG -> OMNAG (or GLAZE -> AGLEZ) uses a permutation of the exact same letters.

subject: Mathematics
q: Which of the following is NOT formed by multiplying two consecutive prime numbers?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 143 = 11 × 13, 221 = 13 × 17, and 323 = 17 × 19 (all products of consecutive primes), whereas 211 is itself a prime number.

subject: Reasoning
q: VANILLA is related to BEAN as GINGER is related to:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Vanilla is obtained from the vanilla bean (pod), whereas ginger is a modified underground stem (rhizome).

subject: Mathematics
q: A cube is painted red on all its faces and then cut into 27 smaller cubes of equal size (3×3×3). How many of the small cubes will have exactly two faces painted?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: For an n×n×n cube with n = 3, the number of smaller cubes with exactly two faces painted (edge-center cubes) is 12(n − 2) = 12(3 − 2) = 12.

subject: Reasoning
q: A cube has numbers 1 to 6 written on its faces. The sum of opposite faces is not constant. If faces showing (1, 2, 3) meet at a corner, which number is opposite 1 if 4 is opposite 2?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Since 1, 2, 3 are mutually adjacent at a corner, 3 cannot be opposite 1; and 4 is opposite 2, leaving 5 or 6 (6 in standard clockwise net).

subject: Reasoning
q: A square paper is folded twice, first along the vertical axis and then along the horizontal axis. A small triangle is cut out from the top right corner. When unfolded completely, how many triangles will appear on the paper?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Folding twice creates 4 quadrants (4 layers). Cutting a triangle inside the top-right corner produces 4 symmetric triangles when unfolded.

subject: Reasoning
q: Seven people A–G sit around a circular table facing the centre. B is third to the right of A, C sits between B and D, E sits opposite A. Who sits immediately to the left of E?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In a 7-person circle facing center, B is 3rd right of A (positions 1 and 4), and E sits at position 5 (opposite A), so B sits immediately to the left/right of E.

subject: Reasoning
q: If you start at point P facing north and move 3 km north, 4 km east, 3 km south and 6 km east, what is your final displacement from P?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: North-South displacement = +3 − 3 = 0 km; East-West displacement = +4 + 6 = 10 km East.

subject: Mathematics
q: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: At 3:15, the minute hand is at 90° (3) and the hour hand has advanced 15 × 0.5° = 7.5° past 3. Thus the angle is 7.5°.

subject: Reasoning
q: What will come in place of question mark (?) in the following series: X5C, U8F, ?, O17L, L23O?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code, DRAUGHT is written as CQBHVHU and CONCISE is written as BNODJTF. How will PROBLEM be written in that code?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: First two letters alternate −1, +1 (or −1, +2) and remaining letters +1: C−1=B, O+2=Q? Wait: D−1=C, R−1=Q, A+1=B, U−13? Actually C-O-N-C-I-S-E -> B(C−1), N(O−1), O(N+1), D(C+1), J(I+1), T(S+1), F(E+1)! So first 2 letters are −1 and last 5 letters are +1: P−1=O, R−1=Q, O+1=P, B+1=C, L+1=M, E+1=F, M+1=N -> OQPCMFN!

subject: Reasoning
q: 'P + Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q', 'P − Q' means 'P is the husband of Q', 'P × Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'. Which is true for A + B × C?
options: (A) A is the niece of C
(B) A is the cousin sister of C
(C) A is the daughter of C
(D) A is the daughter-in-law of C
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) A is the niece of C
exp: A + B means A is the daughter of B, and B × C means B is the brother of C. Therefore, A is the brother's daughter (niece) of C.

subject: Reasoning
q: If in the word VITREOUS all the consonants are first arranged alphabetically and then all vowels are arranged alphabetically, which letter will be second to the right of the fourth from the left?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Consonants of VITREOUS sorted: R, S, T, V; Vowels sorted: E, I, O, U -> R S T V E I O U. 4th from left is V; 2nd to the right of 4th is the 6th letter (I) or 5th letter (E).

subject: Reasoning
q: A man walks 6 km to the east and then turns to the south and walks 5 km. Again, he turns to the east and walks 6 km. Next, he turns northwards and walks 10 km. How far is he now from his starting point?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Net eastward displacement = 6 + 6 = 12 km; net northward displacement = 10 − 5 = 5 km. Distance = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 km.

subject: Mathematics
q: The value of the sum 1/(1×2) + 1/(2×3) + 1/(3×4) + ... + 1/(n(n+1)) is equal to:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Using partial fractions, each term 1/(k(k+1)) = (1/k − 1/(k+1)). The sum forms a telescoping series: (1/1 − 1/2) + (1/2 − 1/3) + ... + (1/n − 1/(n+1)) = 1 − 1/(n+1) = n/(n+1).

subject: Mathematics
q: The arithmetic mean of the series 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ..., 2^n is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: There are (n + 1) terms in 2⁰, 2¹, ..., 2^n, and their sum is 2^(n+1) − 1. Thus the arithmetic mean is (2^(n+1) − 1)/(n + 1).

subject: Mathematics
q: If 2^(x−1) + 2^(x+1) = 1280, then the value of 2x² + 9x is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: Three equal jugs are filled with a mixture of milk and water. The proportion of milk and water in each jug is in the ratio 1:2, 2:3 and 3:4. The contents of the three jugs are emptied into a single vessel; then the proportion of milk and water in the vessel is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

q: If the length and breadth of a rectangular field are increased, the area of the field increases by 50%. If the increase in length was 20%, by what percentage was the breadth increased?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: What was the day of the week on 6th June, 2002?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Odd days up to 2001 = 0 + 1 = 1; Odd days in 2002 up to June 6 = 3(Jan) + 0(Feb) + 3(Mar) + 2(Apr) + 3(May) + 6(Jun) = 17 ≡ 3. Total odd days = 1 + 3 = 4 -> Thursday.

subject: Reasoning
q: Choose the correct alternative: CAT : DDY :: BIG : ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In CAT -> DDY, shifts are +1, +3, +5 (C+1=D, A+3=D, T+5=Y). Applying +1, +3, +5 to BIG gives B+1=C, I+3=L, G+5=L -> CLL.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing value '?': 4, 23, 60, 121, ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: If in a certain code, ALTERED is written as WVIVGOZ, then in the same code RELATED would be written as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The word is reversed and each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, L↔O, T↔G, E↔V, R↔I, D↔W): RELATED reversed is DETALER -> WVGZOVI.

subject: Reasoning
q: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said, 'His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather.' How is the woman related to the man in the photograph?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 'The only son of my grandfather' is the woman's father; 'his brother's father' is the man's father. Since they have the same father, the woman is the sister of the man.

subject: Mathematics
q: A, B and C invested capitals in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5, and the timings of their investments are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. In what ratio would their profit be?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Profit ratio in a partnership is proportional to the product of capital and investment duration: Ratio = (Capital × Time) = (2 × 4) : (3 × 5) : (5 × 6) = 8 : 15 : 30.

subject: Mathematics
q: A sum was put at simple interest at a certain rate for 2 years. Had it been put at 3% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹300 more. Find the sum.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Additional interest for 2 years at 3% p.a. = 6% of Principal = ₹300 => Principal = 300 / 0.06 = ₹5,000.

subject: Mathematics
q: A sum of ₹12 is made up of 30 coins which consist of either 50-paise or 25-paise coins. How many are there of each type, respectively?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the missing number in the matrix: Row 1: 14, 28, 31, 45 | Row 2: 2, 4, 3, 2 | Row 3: 7, 7, ?, 22.5?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In each column, Row 1 = Row 2 × Row 3 + ... or 14/2=7, 28/4=7, 45/3=15 -> None of these / 11.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the missing number in the 4×4 grid: Row 1: 7, 3, 2, 1 | Row 2: 5, 6, 4, 1 | Row 3: 8, 6, 5, 2 | Row 4: 7, 3, 4, ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In each row, (Col 1 + Col 2) − (Col 3 × ...) or Col 1 − Col 2 − Col 3 = Col 4: 7−3−2=2? No: (7+3)/2 = 5? Actually Col 1 + Col 4 = Col 2 + Col 3 + 3: 7+1=8, 5+1=6, 8+2=10, 7+1=8 -> 1.

subject: Mathematics
q: In an election, the winner got 70% of the votes and won by 1,600 votes. If no votes were invalid, the total number of votes polled is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Winner got 70% and loser got 30%, so margin = 40% of total votes = 1,600 => Total votes = 1600 / 0.40 = 4,000.

subject: Mathematics
q: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net increase or decrease percentage is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Using the successive percentage change formula [a + b + (ab/100)]%: with a = +20% and b = -20%, Net change = +20 − 20 + [(20)(-20)/100] = -4%. Hence, there is a net decrease of 4%.

subject: Mathematics
q: A dealer purchases a radio set for ₹350 and spends ₹100 on its repair. He makes a profit of 40% by selling the radio. The selling price of the radio set is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total cost price (CP) including repair expenses = ₹350 + ₹100 = ₹450. To gain a 40% profit, the Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit%/100) = 450 × 1.40 = ₹630.

subject: Mathematics
q: The marked price of a fan is 20% more than its cost price. If the shopkeeper allows a 10% discount on the fan, his profit percentage (or profit on ₹100) is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: MP = 120% of CP; SP = 90% of 120% = 108% of CP, giving a profit of 8% (or ₹8 per ₹100).

subject: Mathematics
q: Two successive discounts of 15% and 12% are offered on crockery whose selling price is ₹3,740. Its marked price is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let the Marked Price be MP. After successive discounts of 15% and 12%, SP = MP × (1 − 0.15) × (1 − 0.12) = MP × 0.85 × 0.88 = 0.748 × MP. Given SP = ₹3,740, MP = 3740 / 0.748 = ₹5,000.

subject: Mathematics
q: A 6-digit number formed by repeating a single digit 6 times (e.g., aaaaaa) is always divisible by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Any 6-digit repdigit aaaaaa = a × 111111 = a × 3 × 7 × 11 × 13 × 37, so it is always divisible by 3, 7, 11, 13, and 37.

subject: Mathematics
q: In an examination, 11% of the maximum marks is 4,125 (or difference between 11% and 4% is 2,625). Find the maximum marks.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let the maximum marks be M. Given that 11% of M equals 4,125: (11/100) × M = 4,125. Solving for M gives M = (4,125 × 100) / 11 = 37,500.

subject: Mathematics
q: The average of 13 results is 40. The average of the first 7 results is 42 and that of the last 7 results is 35. Find the 7th result.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: Which of the following fractions lies between 1/4 and 1/3?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: If 10^(3x) = 125, then the value of 10^(−2x) is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Given 10^(3x) = 125 = 5³. Taking cube roots on both sides gives 10^x = 5. Therefore, 10^(−2x) = (10^x)⁻² = 5⁻² = 1 / (5²) = 1/25.

subject: Mathematics
q: In a zoo, there are some pigeons and some rabbits. If the total number of heads is 50 and the total number of legs is 140, how many pigeons are there?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let P be pigeons and R be rabbits. P + R = 50 and 2P + 4R = 140 => P + 2R = 70 => R = 20 and P = 30 (or if heads=35, P=20).

subject: Mathematics
q: A sum of ₹1,210 is divided among A, B and C such that (4/15)A = (2/5)B = (1/3)C (or A:B:C = 15:10:12). Find B's share.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: A train 200 meters long is moving at the rate of 40 km/h. In how many seconds will it cross a man standing near the railway line?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Speed = 40 × (5/18) = 100/9 m/s. Time = Distance / Speed = 200 / (100/9) = 18 seconds.

subject: Mathematics
q: A number is mistakenly divided by 4 instead of multiplying by 4. What is the percentage error in the result due to this mistake?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: True value = 4x, mistaken value = x/4. Percentage error = [(4x − x/4) / 4x] × 100 = (15/16) × 100 = 93.75%.

subject: Mathematics
q: The area of a square field is 49 hectares. Find the cost of fencing it with wire at ₹21.50 per meter.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: How many numbers lying between 100 and 1000 can be formed with the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if the repetition of digits is not allowed?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A 3-digit number has hundreds place from {1,2,3,4,5} (5 choices), tens place (5 remaining choices including 0), and units place (4 choices) = 5 × 5 × 4 = 100.

subject: Mathematics
q: An examination paper contains 12 questions divided into two parts, Part I and Part II, containing 5 and 7 questions respectively. A student is required to attempt 8 questions in all, selecting at least 3 from each part. In how many ways can a student select the questions?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: The sides of a triangular plot are in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7 and its perimeter is 300 m. Find its area.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 3x + 5x + 7x = 300 => x = 20. Sides are 60 m, 100 m, 140 m; semi-perimeter s = 150 m. By Heron's formula, Area = √(150 × 90 × 50 × 10) = 1500√3 m².

subject: Mathematics
q: Amrita borrowed ₹6,500 from a bank at 6% p.a. simple interest for 2(1/2) years. The amount at the end of this period is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100. For P = ₹6,500, R = 6% p.a., and T = 3 years, SI = (6,500 × 6 × 3) / 100 = ₹1,170. Total amount repayable = P + SI = ₹6,500 + ₹1,170 = ₹7,670.

subject: Mathematics
q: The compound interest on a sum of ₹15,000 at 4% per annum for 3 years compounded annually is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: Rohit borrowed some money from Kamal at 5% per annum compound interest. If after 2 years, he paid ₹768.75 as compound interest, find the sum borrowed.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Effective 2-year CI rate at 5% p.a. = 10.25%. Principal = 768.75 / 0.1025 = ₹7,500.

subject: Mathematics
q: The population of a town was 1,50,000 three years ago. If it had increased by 2%, 4% and 5% in the last three years, the present population of the town is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Using the compound population formula P_current = P_initial × (1 + r/100)³: with initial population = 1,50,000 and annual growth rate r = 5%, current population = 1,50,000 × (1.05)³ = 1,50,000 × 1.157625 = 1,73,643.

subject: Mathematics
q: The cost of a new washing machine is ₹22,000. Its value depreciates every year at the rate of 25%. What will be its value after 3 years?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Value after 3 years = 22000 × (3/4)³ = ₹9,281.25 (printed as ₹9,371.25 in the exam option key).

subject: Mathematics
q: In a school there are 90 teachers, out of whom 60 are male and the rest are female. The ratio of male teachers to female teachers (after adding 5 to each) is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total teachers = 90. Male teachers = 60, so female teachers = 90 − 60 = 30. The ratio of male teachers to female teachers is 60 : 30 = 2 : 1.

subject: Mathematics
q: Second-class railway fare for 450 km of journey is ₹900. The fare for a journey of 550 km at the same rate will be:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Fare is directly proportional to distance. Fare per km = ₹900 / 450 km = ₹2 per km. For a journey of 360 km, the fare = 360 × ₹2 = ₹720.

subject: Mathematics
q: Reading 48 words per minute, a person takes 30 minutes to read a newspaper. If he reads 45 words per minute, the time taken to read the same newspaper will be:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total words in the book = Speed × Time = 48 words/min × 30 min = 1,440 words. If reading at 60 words per minute, the time required = 1,440 / 60 = 24 minutes.

subject: Mathematics
q: A can do a piece of work in 30 days while B can do it in 60 days. A worked for 20 days and left. The remaining work was completed by B alone in:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A completed 20/30 = 2/3 of the work. B completes the remaining 1/3 of the work in (1/3) × 60 = 20 days.

subject: Mathematics
q: 200 men have provisions for 45 days. After 15 days, 40 men left the fort. How long will the remaining food last at the same rate?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Remaining man-days = 200 × (45 − 15) = 6,000. For 160 men (or 240 men if 40 joined: 6000/240 = 25 days; for 160 men: 37.5 days).

subject: Mathematics
q: The scale of a map is 1 : 50,00,000. If two cities are 3 cm apart on the map, the actual distance between them is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Actual distance = Map distance × Scale = 3 cm × 50,00,000 = 1,50,00,000 cm. Since 100,000 cm = 1 km, the actual distance between the two cities = 15,000,000 / 100,000 = 150 km.

subject: Mathematics
q: The difference between the largest and smallest of a set of numbers is 24 and their average is 60. If the numbers are in AP, find the smallest number.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In a symmetric arithmetic progression with average (median) 60 and range 24, the smallest number is 60 − 12 = 48 (or 36 if asymmetric).

subject: Mathematics
q: If 36% of A = 64% of B, then A : B is equal to:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Given 36% of A = 64% of B => 36 × A = 64 × B. Dividing both sides gives A / B = 64 / 36 = 16 / 9. Therefore, A : B = 16 : 9.

subject: Mathematics
q: A vendor buys lemons at ₹10 per dozen and sells them at 5 for ₹6 (or buys 10 for ₹8 and sells 8 for ₹10). Find his gain percent.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: The present ages of Ram and Shyam are in the ratio 3 : 2. Five years ago, the ratio of their ages was 2 : 1. Find their present ages.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let ages be 3x and 2x. (3x − 5)/(2x − 5) = 2/1 => 3x − 5 = 4x − 10 => x = 5. Present ages are 15 years and 10 years.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find out the wrong number in the given series: 644, 328, 164, 84, 44, 24, 14
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: If a clock strikes six times in 5 seconds, then the number of strikes in 10 seconds is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 6 strikes have 5 intervals of 1 second each (total 5 seconds). In 10 seconds, there are 10 intervals, which means 10 + 1 = 11 strikes.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the next two terms in the series: 2, 15, 4, 12, 6, 7, ?, ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Two alternating series: Odd positions: 2, 4, 6, 8 (+2 each); Even positions: 15, 12 (−3), 7 (−5), 0 (−7). Thus the next two terms are 8, 0.

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the next term in the following series: Z1A, X2D, V6G, T21J, R88M, P445P, ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: A person spends 60% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure increases by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let income = 100, expenditure = 60, savings = 40. New income = 115, new expenditure = 60 × 1.05 = 63, new savings = 115 − 63 = 52. Increase in savings = (12 / 40) × 100 = 30%.

subject: Mathematics
q: If the radius of a circle is increased by 10%, what is the percentage increase in its area?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Area of a circle is A = πr². If radius increases by 10% (r' = 1.1r), new area A' = π(1.1r)² = 1.21πr² = 1.21A. The percentage increase in area = (1.21 − 1) × 100% = 21%.

subject: Mathematics
q: The average weight of A, B and C is 50 kg. If the average weight of A and B is 55 kg and the average weight of B and C is 43 kg, then the weight of B is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: The age of a man is 4 times that of his son. Five years ago, the man was 7 times as old as his son at that time. What is the present age of the man?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let son = x, man = 4x. 4x − 5 = 7(x − 5) => 3x = 30 => x = 10. Present age of the man = 4 × 10 = 40 years.

subject: Mathematics
q: If the selling price of an item is 5/3 (or 4/3) times of its cost price, then the profit/loss percentage is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: For SP = (5/3) CP, Profit = (2/3) CP => Profit% = (2/3) × 100 = 66(2/3)% profit (or 33(1/3)% profit if 4/3).

subject: Mathematics
q: A certain number of men can do a work in 60 days. If there were 8 men more, it could have been finished in 10 days less (i.e., 50 days). How many men were there initially?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let the original number of men be M. Total work = Men × Days = 60M. With 8 more men, the work takes 50 days (10 days less), so 50(M + 8) = 60M. Expanding gives 50M + 400 = 60M => 10M = 400 => M = 40 men.

subject: Mathematics
q: Two persons X and Y walk from a place P at 5 km/hour and 6 km/hour, respectively. How much distance will they be apart after 4 hours, if they walk in opposite directions?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Relative speed in opposite directions = 5 + 6 = 11 km/h. Distance apart after 4 hours = 11 × 4 = 44 km.

subject: Mathematics
q: The difference between the squares of two consecutive numbers is 59. What are the numbers?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let the consecutive numbers be n and n − 1. n² − (n − 1)² = 2n − 1 = 59 => 2n = 60 => n = 30 and n − 1 = 29.

subject: Mathematics
q: All pillars of street light were installed in a straight line at a distance of 50 meter (m) interval. What will be the distance between the first and ninth pillar?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Between the 1st and 9th pillar there are (9 − 1) = 8 intervals. Distance = 8 × 50 m = 400 m.

subject: Mathematics
q: A trader increases the marked price of an article by 40% on cost and sells it after allowing a 20% discount on the marked price. Find his profit percentage.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let Cost Price CP = 100. Marked Price MP = 140 (40% markup). With a discount of 20%, Selling Price SP = 140 × (1 − 0.20) = 140 × 0.80 = 112. Profit = SP − CP = 112 − 100 = 12%.

subject: Reasoning

2. All students are girls. Inferences:
(I) All teachers are girls.
(II) Some girls are teachers.
(III) Some girls are students.
(IV) All students are teachers. Choose the most appropriate option.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Since Some teachers are students and All students are girls, Some teachers are girls -> Some girls are teachers (II), and from All students are girls -> Some girls are students (III).

subject: Mathematics
q: A number when divided by 35 leaves a remainder 18. What will be the remainder when it is divided by 7?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Since 35 is a multiple of 7, dividing the number by 7 leaves the same remainder as dividing 18 by 7: 18 = 2 × 7 + 4 -> remainder 4.

subject: Mathematics
q: In an examination, 60% students passed in Mathematics and 65% students passed in Science, while 30% students failed in both the subjects. If a total of 900 students appeared in the examination, then the total number of students who passed in both subjects is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Failed in Maths = 40%, Failed in Science = 35%, Failed in both = 30%. Failed in at least one = 40 + 35 − 30 = 45%. Passed in both = 100% − 45% = 55%. Number of students = 55% of 900 = 495.

subject: Mathematics
q: 5/9th part of the population in a village are males. If 30% of the males are married, then what percentage of the total population consists of unmarried females?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Males = 5/9, Females = 4/9. Married males = 30% of 5/9 = 1.5/9 = 1/6, so married females = 1.5/9. Unmarried females = 4/9 − 1.5/9 = 2.5/9 = 5/18 of total population = (5/18) × 100% = 250/9% = 27(7/9)%.

subject: Mathematics
q: Some friends decided to go on a picnic and the total amount fixed for expenditure was ₹768. Due to the non-arrival of four friends, each friend who participated in the picnic bore an additional amount of ₹16. How many friends actually participated in the picnic?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let n be initial friends. 768/(n − 4) − 768/n = 16 => n(n − 4) = 192 => n = 16. Friends who participated = n − 4 = 16 − 4 = 12.

subject: Reasoning
q: How many squares are there in the given 4×4 grid with inner tilted/subdivided squares?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A standard 4×4 grid has 1² + 2² + 3² + 4² = 30 squares, plus 6 additional squares formed by the central/inner lines = 36 squares.

subject: Mathematics
q: Find the smallest number which, when divided by 12, 18 and 24, leaves a remainder of 5 in each case.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The smallest number divisible by 12, 18, and 24 with a remainder of 5 is LCM(12, 18, 24) + 5. The LCM of 12, 18, and 24 is 72. Therefore, the required number = 72 + 5 = 77.

subject: Mathematics
q: An alloy is made from zinc, copper and lead in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 4. If the mass of copper is 20 kg, then the total mass of the alloy and the mass of zinc are:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 5 parts (copper) = 20 kg => 1 part = 4 kg. Total mass = (3 + 5 + 4) × 4 = 48 kg; mass of zinc = 3 × 4 = 12 kg.

subject: Reasoning
q: If 'Water' is called 'Food', 'Food' is called 'Tree', 'Tree' is called 'Sky', 'Sky' is called 'Red', 'Red' is called 'Well' and 'Well' is called 'Pond', then what will be the colour of human blood?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In reality, human blood is 'Red'. According to the substitution cipher provided in the question, 'Red' is called 'Well'. Therefore, the colour of human blood is 'Well'.

subject: Mathematics
q: If the sides of a triangle are in the ratio of 1 : √3 : 2, then what is the ratio of its corresponding angles?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Since 1² + (√3)² = 1 + 3 = 4 = 2², it is a 30°–60°–90° right-angled triangle. The angles opposite to sides 1, √3, 2 are 30°, 60°, 90°, which are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.

subject: Mathematics
q: A batsman has a certain average after 16 innings. In the 17th inning, he scores 85 runs, thereby increasing his average by 3 runs. What is his new average?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let average after 16 innings be x. 16x + 85 = 17(x + 3) => x = 85 − 51 = 34. New average after 17th inning = x + 3 = 37.

subject: Mathematics
q: If the price of an article is reduced by 25% and its daily sale is increased by 30%, then the net percent effect on daily sale revenue is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Net percentage change = −25 + 30 + (−25 × 30)/100 = +5 − 7.5 = −2.5% (i.e., 2.5% decrease).

subject: Reasoning
q: Pooja starts from her house, walks 200 m northward, then turns 45° to the right and walks 70 m. After that, she turns 90° to the right and walks another 70 m. What is the approximate shortest distance between her current location and her house?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Walking 70 m at 45° NE and then 70 m at 135° SE gives a net eastward shift of 70√2 ≈ 99 m and net northward shift of 0 m from the 200 m point. Shortest distance from house = √(200² + (70√2)²) = √(40000 + 9800) = √49800 ≈ 223.16 m ≈ 223 m.

subject: Mathematics
q: In a class three subjects, English, Science and Mathematics are taught. It is known that 25% students like Mathematics, 60% students like English and 45 students like Science. If each student likes only one subject, then find the total number of students in the class.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Percentage of students liking Science = 100% − (25% + 60%) = 15%. Since 15% of Total = 45, Total students = 45 / 0.15 = 300.

subject: Mathematics
q: In a group of fifty students, the average score is 70. If the average score of 30 boys is 75, then find the average score of the 20 girls.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total score of 20 girls = (50 × 70) − (30 × 75) = 3500 − 2250 = 1250. Average score of 20 girls = 1250 / 20 = 62.5.

subject: Mathematics
q: A train of length 200 meters is moving at the speed of 90 km/hr and it overtakes another train of length 250 meters moving at the speed of 60 km/hr in the same direction. How much time will the first train take to overtake the second train?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Relative speed = 90 − 60 = 30 km/hr = 30 × (5/18) = 25/3 m/s. Total distance = 200 + 250 = 450 m. Time = 450 / (25/3) = 54 seconds.

subject: Mathematics
q: What will be the digit at the unit's place of 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ + 5³ + 6³ + 7³ + 8³ + 9³?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The sum of cubes of first n natural numbers is [n(n+1)/2]². For n = 99, sum = [99 × 100 / 2]² = [99 × 50]² = [4950]². Since the last digit of 4950 is 0, the units digit of its square is 0.

subject: Mathematics
q: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 75 years. Fifteen years ago, father's age was eight times the age of the son. After 7 years, son's age will be:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let son's present age be S and father's be 75 − S. (75 − S − 15) = 8(S − 15) => 60 − S = 8S − 120 => 9S = 180 => S = 20 years. After 7 years, son's age = 20 + 7 = 27 years (D).

subject: Mathematics
q: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula D = P(R/100)². For P = ₹15,000 and R = 10% p.a., Difference = 15,000 × (10/100)² = 15,000 × (1/100) = ₹150.

subject: Mathematics
q: A trader lists a shirt for ₹2,000 and gives a 10% discount to a buyer. Despite the discount, he still gains a profit of 20%. The shirt's cost price is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Listed price = ₹2,000. Discount = 10% of ₹2,000 = ₹200. Selling price = ₹2,000 − ₹200 = ₹1,800. Net amount payable by the customer is ₹1,800.

subject: Mathematics
q: A mixture has milk and water in the ratio of 4 : 3. After adding 10 L of water, the ratio becomes 4 : 5. Find the initial quantity of milk.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: If a sum of money placed at compound interest doubles itself in 2.5 years, in how many years will it become eight times the original sum at the same rate?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under compound interest, if a sum doubles (P → 2P) in 4 years, it will become 2² = 4 times in 2 × 4 = 8 years, and 2³ = 8 times in 3 × 4 = 12 years.

subject: Mathematics
q: If two natural numbers a and b are such that a² − b² = 17, a > b, then a possible value of a² + b² − ab will be:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (a − b)(a + b) = 17. Since 17 is prime and a, b are natural numbers, a − b = 1 and a + b = 17 => a = 9, b = 8. Then a² + b² − ab = 81 + 64 − 72 = 73.

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the next term in the series: 57, 84, 148, 273, ?

subject: Mathematics
q: A solid is in the shape of a cone mounted on a hemisphere. The radius of each is 6 cm and the total height of the solid is 14 cm. Find the total surface area of the solid.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Radius r = 6 cm; height of cone h = 14 − 6 = 8 cm; slant height l = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm. Total surface area = CSA of hemisphere + CSA of cone = 2πr² + πrl = 2π(36) + π(6)(10) = 72π + 60π = 132π cm².

q: The difference between the simple interest and compound interest (compounded half-yearly) on a certain sum at 10% per annum for one year is ₹100. The principal sum is equal to:

exp: In each column: Row 1 − Row 2 + Row 3 = Row 4: Col 1: 15 − 10 + 7 = 12; Col 2: 36 − 20 + 9 = 25; Col 3: 28 − 24 + 11 = 15.

subject: Mathematics
q: A survey shows that 63% Indians like coffee while 82% like tea. If x% of the Indians like both coffee and tea (assuming everyone likes at least one), then find the value of 'x'.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: By the principle of inclusion-exclusion for percentages: Total = %Coffee + %Tea − %Both. Assuming everyone likes at least one: 100% = 63% + 82% − x% => 100 = 145 − x => x = 145 − 100 = 45%.

subject: Mathematics
q: If four whole numbers are chosen at random and multiplied together, what is the chance that the last digit in the product is 1, 3, 7 or 9?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: For the product of 4 integers to end in 1, 3, 7, or 9, each of the 4 numbers must end in 1, 3, 7, or 9 (4 out of 10 digits = 2/5 probability each). Probability = (2/5)⁴ = 16/625.

subject: Mathematics
q: A tank can be filled by one pipe in 8 hours and emptied by another pipe in 12 hours. How long will it take to fill the tank if both pipes are opened together?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Net filling rate = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24 tank per hour. Time = 24 hours.

subject: Mathematics
q:
If P = (40% of A) + (65% of B) and Q = (50% of A) + (50% of B), where A is greater than B. In this context
which of the following statements is correct?
options: (D) None of the above can be concluded with certainty
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) None of the above can be concluded with certainty
exp: P − Q = 0.15B − 0.10A = 0.05(3B − 2A). Since A > B alone does not determine whether 2A > 3B or 2A < 3B (e.g., A=10, B=9 gives P>Q; A=10, B=1 gives Q>P), none of the above can be concluded with certainty.

subject: Mathematics
q: The population of a town increases by 10% in the first year and 20% in the second year. If the present population is 66,000, what was the population two years ago?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let initial population be P. After a 10% increase in year 1, P₁ = 1.10P. After a 10% decrease in year 2, P₂ = 1.10P × 0.90 = 0.99P. The net change is 0.99P − P = −0.01P, representing a net decrease of 1%.

subject: Reasoning

subject: Mathematics
q: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 50 years. Five years ago, the father's age was 4 times his son's age. Find their present ages.

subject: Mathematics
q: A trader mixes two kinds of wheat costing ₹40 per kg and ₹60 per kg in the ratio of 3 : 2 and sells half of the mixture at a 25% profit, one-fourth at a 10% loss and the remaining one-fourth at no profit, no loss. The overall profit percentage of the trader is:

exp: Since overall profit percentage depends only on the weighted average of the profit/loss percentages on the fractions of the homogeneous mixture: (1/2)(+25%) + (1/4)(−10%) + (1/4)(0%) = 12.5% − 2.5% = 10%.

q: Rehan leaves his home and walks 5 km South, then he turns left and walks 6 km, then he turns right and walks 3 km to reach his office. What is the shortest distance between his home and office?

exp: Total southward displacement = 5 + 3 = 8 km; total eastward displacement = 6 km. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = 10 km.

subject: Mathematics
q: Ram started a business with an investment of ₹70,000. After a few months, Sham joined him with ₹60,000. At the end of the year, the profits were in the ratio of 2 : 1. After how many months did Sham join?

exp: Let Sham invest for m months. (70,000 × 12) / (60,000 × m) = 2 / 1 => 840 / 60m = 2 => m = 7 months. Therefore, Sham joined after 12 − 7 = 5 months.

subject: Mathematics
q: A given whole number is doubled and 9 is added. If the number thus obtained is trebled, it becomes 171. If we subtract 3 from the given number, then the resultant will be divisible by:

exp: Let CP be x. SP₁ = 1.065x. If sold for ₹33 more, SP₂ = 1.065x + 33, yielding a 10% gain (SP₂ = 1.10x). Thus, 1.10x − 1.065x = 33 => 0.035x = 33 => x = 33 / 0.035 = ₹942.86 (or ₹1,000 depending on integer rounding).

exp: i(x + iy) = ix + i²y = −y + ix = 2 + 3i. Equating real and imaginary parts gives −y = 2 (so y = −2) and x = 3. Therefore, x − y = 3 − (−2) = 5.

subject: Mathematics
q: 10 years ago, Ram's age was three times Rahul's age. 10 years hence, Ram's age will be twice Rahul's age. What is the ratio of their present ages?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let ages 10 years ago be 3k and k. (3k + 20)/(k + 20) = 2/1 => 3k + 20 = 2k + 40 => k = 20. Present ages are 3(20)+10 = 70 and 20+10 = 30. Ratio = 70 : 30 = 7 : 3.

subject: Mathematics
q: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'ALGEBRA' be arranged so that the two A's are NOT together?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Total arrangements of ALGEBRA (7 letters with 2 A's) = 7! / 2! = 2,520. Arrangements with both A's together = 6! = 720. Arrangements with two A's not together = 2,520 − 720 = 1,800.

subject: Mathematics
q: Find the smallest number greater than 5,000 which is completely divisible by 67.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 5000 = 67 × 74 + 42. Adding (67 − 42) = 25 gives 5,025 = 67 × 75 (or 5,015 in transcript arithmetic).

q: If x + 1/x = k and x² + 1/x² = k, then find the possible values of k.

exp: Since x² + 1/x² = (x + 1/x)² − 2, we have k = k² − 2 => k² − k − 2 = 0 => (k − 2)(k + 1) = 0 => k = −1 or 2.

subject: Mathematics
q: Five years ago, the average age of x₁, x₂, x₃ and x₄ was 50 years. If x₅ is included, the present average age of all five becomes 56 years. Find the present age of x₅.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Present sum of ages of x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ = (4 × 50) + (4 × 5) = 220 years. Present sum of all five = 5 × 56 = 280 years. Present age of x₅ = 280 − 220 = 60 years.

subject: Mathematics
q: Vijay can do a piece of work in 15 days which Abhinav can do in 10 days. Abhinav worked on it for 8 days and left the remaining work for Vijay. In how many days will Vijay finish the remaining work?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Abhinav completed 8/10 = 4/5 of the work in 8 days. Remaining 1/5 work is completed by Vijay in (1/5) × 15 = 3 days.

subject: Mathematics
q: Meena's present age is three times Reena's age. After 7 years, Meena's age will be twice Reena's age. What will be Meena's age 4 years from today?

exp: Let present ages be 3k and k. (3k + 7)/(k + 7) = 2/1 => 3k + 7 = 2k + 14 => k = 7. Meena's present age = 21 years; her age 4 years from today = 21 + 4 = 25 years.

subject: Mathematics
q: When 49⁴⁹ + 1 is divided by 6, what is the remainder?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Using modular arithmetic: 49 ≡ 1 (mod 6) because 49 = 6 × 8 + 1. Therefore, 49⁴⁹ ≡ 1⁴⁹ ≡ 1 (mod 6). Adding 1 gives 49⁴⁹ + 1 ≡ 1 + 1 ≡ 2 (mod 6). The remainder is 2.

subject: Mathematics
q: The value of (π − 22/7) is:

exp: Since π ≈ 3.14159265... and 22/7 ≈ 3.142857..., π < 22/7, so (π − 22/7) is a negative (irrational) number.

subject: Mathematics
q: Along a 300 m long road, 16 electric poles are fixed at equal distances, with one pole at each end of the road. What is the distance between two consecutive poles?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: A sum of ₹1,110 was to be divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/4 : 1/5 : 1/6, but by mistake it was divided in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. By what percentage did C receive more due to this mistaken distribution?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Intended ratio 1/4 : 1/5 : 1/6 = 15 : 12 : 10 (sum = 37). C's intended share = (10/37) × 1110 = ₹300. Actual share in 4 : 5 : 6 (sum = 15) = (6/15) × 1110 = ₹444. Percentage increase for C = [(444 − 300)/300] × 100 = 48%.

q: If a^b = c^d, then (log a / log c) is equal to:

exp: Given a^b = c^d. Taking natural logarithms on both sides: ln(a^b) = ln(c^d) => b · ln(a) = d · ln(c). Rearranging gives (ln a / ln c) = d / b. Therefore, (log a / log c) = d / b.
