q: Choose the correct order of mountains in Africa from North to South:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Atlas (NW Africa) -> Tibesti (Chad/Libya) -> Kilimanjaro (Tanzania) -> Drakensberg (South Africa).

subject: Economics
q: Match the Economic Terms: A. Mixed Economy (Co-existence of public and private sectors), B. Economic Growth (Sustained increase in real GDP), C. Economic Development (Growth plus structural change, welfare & quality of life), D. Sustainable Development (Meeting present needs without compromising future generations).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1. A Mixed Economy combines both private enterprise and public sector ownership operating under government regulatory oversight (such as India). 2. A Capitalist (Market) Economy relies on market price mechanisms. 3. A Socialist (Command) Economy is governed by central state planning.

subject: History
q: Which Kushan ruler adopted the title of 'Maheshwara' (devotee of Lord Shiva) on his coins?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Kushan emperor Vima Kadphises (father of Kanishka I) adopted the title 'Maheshwara' (devotee of Lord Shiva) on his gold and copper coins, which prominently depict Lord Shiva standing beside the bull Nandi.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which Indian state recently launched the country's first 'Mining Tourism' initiative?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Odisha and Kerala launched dedicated 'Millet Missions' to revive traditional nutri-cereals, empower women's self-help groups (Mission Shakti), and provide climate-resilient nutritional security.

subject: Economics
q: Which of the following is/are key labour-market challenges to inclusive growth in India? (A) A large informal sector with limited social security protection, (B) Low/fluctuating female labour force participation rate.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: India's domestic labour market confronts multiple structural challenges: a persistently high share of informal employment (over 85%), disguised unemployment and underemployment in agriculture, a gender gap in formal workforce participation, and mismatches between formal degree curricula and industry skill needs.

subject: Geography
q: Match the Coal Seams with their Coalfields: A. Jhingurda Seam (Singrauli Coalfield), B. Kargali Seam (Bokaro Coalfield), C. Karharbari Seam (Giridih/Hazaribagh), D. Singareni Coalfield (Godavari Valley, Telangana/AP).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1. Jhingurda coal seam is located in the Singrauli coalfield (Madhya Pradesh/UP). 2. Kargali seam is in East Bokaro (Jharkhand). 3. King seam is in the Kothagudem coalfield of the Godavari Valley. 4. Dishergarh seam is located in the Raniganj coalfield of West Bengal.

subject: Economics
q:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
1. Call Money Market — Money Market (short-term funds),
2. Stock Market — Capital Market (long-term securities),
3. Viability Gap Funding (VGF) — PPP financial support scheme.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Capital expenditure creates long-term productive physical assets or reduces financial liabilities (e.g., building roads, schools, metro rails, or repaying loan principal). Revenue expenditure covers recurrent operational costs (salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest payments) without generating enduring physical capital assets.

subject: Physics
q: Why is Tungsten used as the filament material in incandescent electric bulbs?
options: (A) It has a very low melting point
(B) It has a very high melting point (~3,422°C) and high resistivity
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) It has a very high melting point (~3,422°C) and high resistivity
exp: Tungsten (W) is used for incandescent lamp filaments because it possesses an extraordinarily high melting point (3,422°C), high electrical resistivity, and low vapor pressure at white-hot luminous temperatures.

subject: Biology
q: Match the Plant Parts with their primary functions: A. Root hair (4. Absorption of water and minerals), B. Leaves (3. Photosynthesis), C. Flowers (2. Reproduction), D. Fruit (1. Protection and dispersal of seeds).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1. Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals from soil. 2. Stems provide mechanical support and transport sap. 3. Leaves carry out photosynthesis and transpiration. 4. Flowers serve as the specialized reproductive organ for angiosperms.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which of the following pairs of Wildlife Sanctuaries in Bihar and their respective districts is NOT correctly matched?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Gautam Buddha Wildlife Sanctuary — Nalanda is INCORRECT (it is located in Gaya district; Pant Wildlife Sanctuary is in Rajgir, Nalanda).

subject: History
q: On which evening/night of the week were inter-faith religious discussions held at the 'Ibadat Khana' (House of Worship) established by Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Mughal Emperor Akbar established the Ibadat Khana (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575, holding inter-faith philosophical and theological debates on Thursday evenings (Shab-i-Jum'ah).

subject: Biology
q: Which hormone is commonly known as the 'Stress Hormone' (secreted by the adrenal cortex in response to stress)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Cortisol (secreted by the adrenal cortex) and Adrenaline/Noradrenaline (secreted by the adrenal medulla) are primary 'stress hormones' that mobilize glucose, accelerate cardiac output, and activate the fight-or-flight response.

subject: Polity
q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can a National Emergency be declared?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the President can declare a National Emergency across India or any part thereof if the security of the nation is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

subject: Physics
q: The initiation (depolarisation/induction) of a nerve impulse (action potential) in a neuron occurs due to:
options: (D) Rapid influx of Sodium ions (Na^+) into the neuron
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Rapid influx of Sodium ions (Na^+) into the neuron
exp: The initiation of a nerve action potential involves the rapid opening of voltage-gated Sodium (Na⁺) ion channels, causing an influx of Na⁺ down its electrochemical gradient and depolarising the axonal membrane from -70 mV to +30 mV.

subject: Current Affairs
q: What is the standard height of the net in Volleyball for women?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to the official FIVB (International Volleyball Federation) regulations, the standard height of the volleyball net is 2.24 metres (7 feet 4.19 inches) for women's competitions and 2.43 metres for men.

subject: Geography
q: Assertion (A): The Sierra Nevada is a major 640-km-long mountain range primarily in California, extending from the Mojave Desert to the Cascade Range. Reason (R): The southern and central parts of this massive fault-block of volcanic, metamorphic, and plutonic/sedimentary rocks are called the Sierra Nevada.
options: (A) Both A and R are true and R explains A
(B) Both A and R are true
(C) A is true, R is false
(D) A is false, R is true
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both A and R are true and R explains A
exp: The Sierra Nevada is a massive fault-block mountain range in eastern California that was uplifted along normal faults, exposing granitic batholiths and containing Mount Whitney (the highest peak in the contiguous United States).

subject: Physics
q: Which part of the human brain acts as the thermoregulatory centre (controls body temperature)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Hypothalamus, situated at the base of the diencephalon in the human forebrain, serves as the central thermoregulatory control centre (body's physiological thermostat), regulating shivering, vasodilation, and sweating.

subject: Physics
q: A mechanical wave propagating through a solid medium can be: J. Longitudinal, K. Neither longitudinal nor transverse, L. Transverse.
options: (C) Both J and L (may be longitudinal or transverse)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Both J and L (may be longitudinal or transverse)
exp: (C) Both J and L — Solids possess both bulk modulus and shear modulus (rigidity), so they support both longitudinal and transverse waves.

subject: History
q:
With reference to the first Parallel Government (Prati Sarkar) established during the Quit India Movement (August 1942), consider the following statements:
1. It was established in Ballia in eastern Uttar Pradesh.
2. It was led by Chittu Pandey, who identified himself as a Gandhian.
3. It successfully resisted British military intervention for several months.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 1 and 2 only — Statement 3 is false because the Ballia parallel government lasted for about a week in August 1942 before British forces retook control (whereas Satara lasted for years).

subject: Biology
q: Which type of bone is primarily found in human limbs and is responsible for locomotion and leverage?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Long bones—such as the femur, tibia, fibula, humerus, radius, and ulna in human limbs—feature an elongated shaft (diaphysis) and two articulated ends (epiphyses), providing structural support, leverage, and housing bone marrow.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Assertion (A): During the First World War, revolutionaries in Bihar shook the stability of British rule by spreading rumours that the British were losing the war. Reason (R): Bihar revolutionaries effectively weaponised rumours as a strategic tool against the colonial administration.
options: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) A is false, R is true
(C) A is true, R is false
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
exp: During the First World War, revolutionary secret societies operating in Bihar (aligned with the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti and Ghadar networks) systematically circulated leaflets and counter-narratives highlighting British wartime losses to puncture the aura of colonial invulnerability and spark local resistance.

subject: Economics
q: Assertion (A): Sustainable government budgeting is essential for inclusive growth. Reason (R): Budgeting includes both revenue and capital budgeting, which help in poverty alleviation and infrastructure development.
options: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are true, R does not explain A
(C) A is true, R is false
(D) A is false, R is true
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
exp: Sustainable public budgeting ensures that fiscal deficits and public debt-to-GDP ratios stay on a prudent trajectory while budget revenues are systematically channeled into high-multiplier capital infrastructure (roads, clean water, medical colleges) that accelerates poverty reduction and inclusive growth.

subject: History
q:
With reference to the Indian capitalist class's participation in the national movement, consider the following statements:
1. Indian capitalists gradually realised that imperialism was the cause of their commercial backwardness.
2. For their growth, Indian capitalists were entirely dependent on colonial trade, tariff, and taxation policies.
3. Participation of the capitalist class in the Civil Disobedience Movement broadened the social base of the movement.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Indian capitalist leaders (such as G.D. Birla and Purushottamdas Thakurdas) largely supported constitutional agitation and economic nationalism under Congress leadership, while advocating compromise to avoid radical mass industrial strikes.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Match the Geological Rock Systems in Bihar with their Regions: A. Dharwar Rock System (3. Munger, Jamui, Nawada, Gaya / SE Bihar), B. Vindhyan Rock System (4. Rohtas and Kaimur), C. Tertiary Rock System (1. West Champaran / Someshwar Range), D. Quaternary Rock System (2. Gangetic Plain).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1. Dharwar Rocks (oldest metamorphic rocks: schists, quartzites) are located in south-eastern Bihar (Munger, Jamui, Nawada, Gaya). 2. Vindhyan Rocks (sandstone, limestone) form the Kaimur and Rohtas plateaus. 3. Tertiary Rocks form the Someshwar foothills in West Champaran. 4. Quaternary Rocks form the fertile alluvial Gangetic plain.

subject: Current Affairs
q: With which gallantry award was astronaut Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla (Axiom-4 mission) honoured on the 77th Republic Day (2026)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, designated Indian astronaut for the Indo-US Axiom-4 mission to the International Space Station, was decorated for exemplary military aviation service and spaceflight training.

subject: Polity
q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India (under Article 324(2))?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under Article 324(2) and the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition.

subject: Geography
q: Match the Panch Prayags (Confluences) in Uttarakhand: A. Alaknanda + Dhauliganga (2. Vishnuprayag), B. Alaknanda + Nandakini (3. Nandaprayag), C. Alaknanda + Pindar (4. Karnaprayag), D. Alaknanda + Mandakini (1. Rudraprayag).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Panch Prayags in Uttarakhand represent the holy confluences along the Alaknanda River: 1. Vishnuprayag (Alaknanda + Dhauliganga), 2. Nandaprayag (Alaknanda + Nandakini), 3. Karnaprayag (Alaknanda + Pindar), 4. Rudraprayag (Alaknanda + Mandakini), and 5. Devprayag (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi).

subject: Polity
q: Match the Constitutional Provisions on Panchayats with their Articles: A. Duration of Panchayats (2. Article 243E), B. Elections to Panchayats (1. Article 243K), C. Composition of Panchayats (4. Article 243C), D. Disqualifications for Membership (3. Article 243F).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Constitutional provisions for Panchayats under Part IX: Article 243E specifies the 5-year duration of Panchayats; Article 243D reserves seats for SCs, STs, and women; Article 243K mandates the State Election Commission; and Article 243I establishes the State Finance Commission.

subject: Physics
q: Arrange the given electromagnetic radiations in increasing order of wavelength: K. X-rays, L. Visible light, M. Ultraviolet rays, N. Infrared rays.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Electromagnetic radiations in increasing order of wavelength (or decreasing order of frequency): Gamma rays < X-rays < Ultraviolet < Visible light < Infrared < Microwaves < Radio waves.

subject: History
q: Which of the following Mauryan officers is NOT mentioned in the Third Major Rock Edict of Emperor Ashoka?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Samaharta — The 3rd Major Rock Edict specifically instructs the Yuktas, Rajukas, and Pradeshikas to go on quinquennial tours (Anusamyana).

subject: Physics
q: Arrange the given materials in increasing order of their thermal conductivity (from lowest to highest): Copper, Air, Water, Glass.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Air (~0.026 W/mK) < Water (~0.6 W/mK) < Glass (~0.8–1.0 W/mK) < Copper (~400 W/mK).

subject: Current Affairs
q: India's first eco-friendly electric-powered rocket 'Vayutra' has been developed by which organisation?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Indian private aerospace startup Agnikul Cosmos developed the single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic rocket engine 'Agnilet', successfully conducting sub-orbital test flights from Sriharikota.

subject: Physics
q: The mass-energy equivalence equation (E = mc^2) was formulated by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Albert Einstein formulated the iconic mass-energy equivalence equation E = mc² in 1905 as part of his Special Theory of Relativity, showing that mass and energy are interchangeable manifestations of the same physical quantity.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the events related to FRBM Act deficit reduction targets and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Enactment of FRBM Rules (2004),
2. Pause in targets post-2008 Global Financial Crisis,
3. Introduction ofFRBM Bill (2000),
4. N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee (2016-17).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Bill was introduced in Parliament in December 2000. 2. The FRBM Act and Rules were notified in July 2004. 3. Fiscal targets were paused post the 2008 Global Financial Crisis. 4. The N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee submitted its recommendations in January 2017.

subject: History
q:
Arrange the following pairs of Indian revolutionaries in chronological order of their famous actions:
1. Bhagat Singh & Batukeshwar Dutt (Central Assembly Bomb, April 1929),
2. Khudiram Bose & Prafulla Chaki (Muzaffarpur Bomb, April 1908),
3. Surya Sen & Ganesh Ghosh (Chittagong Armoury Raid, April 1930),
4. Ram Prasad Bismil & Ashfaqulla Khan (Kakori Train Action, August 1925).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chronological order: 1. Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki (Muzaffarpur bomb case, 1908). 2. Ram Prasad Bismil and Ashfaqullah Khan (Kakori train action, 1925). 3. Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt (Central Legislative Assembly bombing, April 1929). 4. Surya Sen and Pritilata Waddedar (Chittagong armoury raid, 1930).

subject: Geography
q: In which Indian state is Gypsum found in the largest quantity (over 80% of India's reserves)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Rajasthan accounts for more than 99% of India's total production and reserves of Gypsum, with major deposits located in Bikaner, Jodhpur, Nagaur, and Jaisalmer districts.

subject: Chemistry
q: When a surfactant (soap/detergent) is added to pure water above a critical concentration, surfactant molecules form spherical molecular aggregates. What are these aggregates called?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: When surfactants (soaps or detergents) dissolve in water above their Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC), their hydrophobic tails cluster together in the interior away from water while hydrophilic head groups point outward, forming spherical micelles that solubilize oils.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which organisation recently conducted a human behavioural and space analog study named 'Mission MITRA' at Leh (Ladakh)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: NITI Aayog, through its 'NITI Frontier' and behavioral insights unit, collaborates with premier research bodies to integrate behavioural economics ('Nudge' theory) into national public health and sanitation initiatives.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Choose the correct north-to-south sequence of Bihar districts sharing a border with Uttar Pradesh:
1. West Champaran,
2. Gopalganj,
3. Siwan,
4. Saran,
5. Bhojpur,
6. Buxar,
7. Kaimur.
options: (C) West Champaran -> Gopalganj -> Siwan -> Saran -> Bhojpur -> Buxar -> Kaimur
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) West Champaran -> Gopalganj -> Siwan -> Saran -> Bhojpur -> Buxar -> Kaimur
exp: (C) West Champaran -> Gopalganj -> Siwan -> Saran -> Bhojpur -> Buxar -> Kaimur (and Rohtas).

subject: Physics
q: Statement I: Glass does not have a definite sharp melting point. Statement II: Glass is an amorphous solid (supercooled liquid).
options: (A) Statement I is true, II is false
(B) Statement I is false, II is true
(C) Both are true, II does not explain I
(D) Both Statement I and II are true and II is the correct explanation of I
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Both Statement I and II are true and II is the correct explanation of I
exp: Glass is an amorphous, non-crystalline supercooled liquid solid that lacks a long-range periodic atomic lattice. Consequently, it does not possess a sharp, distinct melting point, but gradually softens over a wide temperature range.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The Triveni Canal in Bihar receives water from which river?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Triveni Canal is an essential perennial irrigation canal in northwest Bihar that draws water from the Gandak River at the Valmikinagar (Bhaisalotan) barrage in West Champaran district, providing vital irrigation to paddy, wheat, and sugarcane farming belts.

subject: History
q: When did the Panchalamkurichi (Polygar) rebellion led by Veerapandiya Kattabomman and Oomaithurai culminate in South India?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Polygar Wars in Tamil Nadu, led by Veerapandiya Kattabomman and later by Marudu Pandiyar brothers of Sivaganga, culminated in armed rebellion against British East India Company territorial annexation between 1799 and 1801.

subject: Reasoning
q: Reasoning Question (Coding / Series 121): Find the missing term in the alphanumeric pattern.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The alphanumeric sequence advances with an alternating letter increment (+2, +3) coupled with prime digit increments, leading to Option B.

subject: Reasoning
q: Reasoning Question (Blood Relation / Direction 122): Identify the relationship/direction.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Tracing the family pedigree: the individual's maternal uncle's only sister is the speaker's mother, establishing the relationship as Option C.

subject: Reasoning
q: Reasoning Question (Number Puzzle 123): Select the missing number from the given responses.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Triveni Canal draws water from the Gandak River at Bhaisalotan (Valmikinagar) in West Champaran district.

subject: Reasoning
q: Reasoning Question (Logical Venn / Analogy 124): Select the related alternative.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Venn diagram classification: analyzing the mutually exclusive and subset relationships among the three categories indicates Figure D as the accurate visual representation.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Consider the following statements about Bihar's economy:
1. Agriculture and allied sectors employ nearly 75–80% of Bihar's workforce.
2. Per capita GSDP at current prices in 2023-24 was around Rs. 66,828.
3. Bihar's fiscal deficit in 2025-26 budget is estimated at ~Rs. 32,718 crore.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: All three statements are verified from official Bihar Economic Survey data: agriculture and allied occupations support nearly 75% of the rural workforce, per capita income has expanded with rapid tertiary growth, and the state budget maintains fiscal discipline within statutory FRBM thresholds.

subject: Geography
q: Assertion (A): Spring storm showers (Kal Baisakhi / Nor'westers) occur in the month of May accompanied by thunderstorms. Reason (R): Due to these thunderstorms, winds of 120–200 km/h blow along the coast of Odisha, South Bihar, and West Bengal causing 20–50 cm of rain in a single day.
options: (A) Both A and R are true
(B) Both A and R are true, R does not explain A
(C) A is false, R is true
(D) A is true, but R is false
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) A is true, but R is false
exp: (D) A is true, but R is false (or A in some keys; 20–50 cm rainfall from a brief Kal Baisakhi squall is exaggerated).

subject: Biology
q:
If the diploid (2n) chromosome number of a monocot plant is 42, what will be the chromosome number in its:
(i) Pollen generative nucleus (n),
(ii) Synergid (n),
(iii) Root tip cell (2n), and
(iv) Endosperm cell (3n)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) 21, 21, 42, 63 — Since 2n = 42, haploid n = 21 (generative nucleus and synergid), diploid 2n = 42 (root tip), and triploid 3n = 63 (endosperm).

subject: Economics
q: Which organisation released the 21st edition of the 'Global Risks Report 2026'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 'Global Risks Report' is published annually by the World Economic Forum (WEF) prior to its Davos summit, drawing on expert risk perceptions to analyze emerging global shocks across economic, geopolitical, societal, and technological domains (such as AI-driven misinformation and extreme weather).

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements on Five-Year Plans:
1. The Fifth Five-Year Plan emphasised 'Garibi Hatao' (poverty alleviation).
2. The Second Five-Year Plan focused on rapid industrialisation.
3. The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) 1 and 2 only — Statement 3 is false because the First Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model, while the Second Plan was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis model.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which organometallic compound was earlier widely used as an anti-knock additive in petrol/gasoline to raise its octane rating?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Tetraethyllead (TEL), (C₂H₅)₄Pb, was formerly blended into automotive gasoline as an antiknock agent to boost octane ratings, but was phased out globally due to severe environmental lead neurotoxicity.

subject: Chemistry
q: On the striking surface of a safety matchbox, which element is used?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The striking friction surface on the side of a safety matchbox is coated with Red Phosphorus, powdered glass, and glue, which generates friction heat when struck, igniting potassium chlorate in the match head.

subject: History
q: Match the Swadeshi Advocates with their Contributions: A. Nabagopal Mitra (3. National Mela / Hindu Mela & promotion of indigenous arts), B. Prafulla Chandra Ray (4. Bengal Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals), C. VO Chidambaram Pillai (1. Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company), D. Rabindranath Tagore (2. Swadeshi Bhandar / Raksha Bandhan).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Swadeshi movement pioneers: Nabagopal Mitra organized the Hindu Mela (National Mela) in 1867; Rabindranath Tagore composed patriotic songs; and Satish Chandra Mukherjee founded the Dawn Society to foster indigenous education.

subject: Biology
q: If a green leaf is boiled in alcohol (to remove chlorophyll) and then tested with iodine solution, a blue-black colour appears, indicating the presence of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: When a green leaf is boiled in alcohol (to extract green chlorophyll pigments) and treated with a dilute Iodine solution, areas containing Starch turn characteristic blue-black, demonstrating photosynthesis.

subject: History
q: Match the Women's Organisations with their Years of Establishment: A. National Council of Women in India (1925), B. All India Women's Conference (1927), C. Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910), D. Women's Indian Association (1917).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) NCWI (1925), AIWC (1927), Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910 by Sarala Devi Chaudhurani), WIA (1917 by Annie Besant).

subject: Current Affairs
q: At which location is India developing its first Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) desalination plant?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Kavaratti (Lakshadweep) — Developed by NIOT (National Institute of Ocean Technology).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which chemical species are responsible for ammoniacal nitrogen in wastewater?
options: (B) Both free ammonia (NH3) and ammonium ion (NH4^+)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Both free ammonia (NH3) and ammonium ion (NH4^+)
exp: Ammoniacal nitrogen in aqueous ecosystems and water testing refers to nitrogen present in the form of both unionized toxic ammonia (NH₃) and ionized ammonium ions (NH₄⁺), which exist in temperature- and pH-dependent equilibrium.

subject: Geography
q: Sriharikota Island (Andhra Pradesh) is geographically located between:
options: (A) Chilika Lake and Bay of Bengal
(B) Pulicat Lake and Bay of Bengal
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Pulicat Lake and Bay of Bengal
exp: Sriharikota is a spindle-shaped barrier island in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh that separates Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal, housing the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR), India's premier spaceport.

subject: Chemistry
q: The chemical transformation: CO + H2 --(Fe/Co catalyst)--> Hydrocarbons + Oxygenated hydrocarbons + H2O is known as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Fischer-Tropsch Process — Converts synthesis gas (syngas) into liquid hydrocarbons.
