exp: (A) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true — Like poles repel each other (so A is false), whereas opposite poles attract each other (so R is true) (Official Key Series K Q123: A).

subject: Physics
q: Wooden handles are fitted on cooking utensils because wood is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) A poor conductor (insulator) of heat — Wood has very low thermal conductivity, preventing heat from reaching the user's hand (Official Key Series K Q124: D).

subject: Physics
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 1 → 3 → 4 → 2 — Atom (~10^-26 kg) < Artificial satellite (~10^3 kg) < Crustal solid matter < Total mass of Earth (~6 × 10^24 kg) (Official Key Series K Q125: A).

subject: Physics
q: The Greenhouse Effect keeps the Earth's surface:
options: (B) Warm at night (by trapping outgoing terrestrial infrared radiation)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Warm at night (by trapping outgoing terrestrial infrared radiation)
exp: (B) Warm at night — Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit longwave infrared radiation emitted by Earth, preventing rapid nighttime cooling (Official Key Series K Q126: B).

subject: Physics
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) 2 → 1 → 4 → 3 — Millimetre (10^-3 m) > Micrometre (10^-6 m) > Nanometre (10^-9 m) > Picometre (10^-12 m) (Official Key Series K Q127: D).

subject: Physics
q: Solar energy can be converted into:
options: (B) Both Electrical energy and Mechanical/Thermal energy
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Both Electrical energy and Mechanical/Thermal energy
exp: (B) Both Electrical energy and Mechanical/Thermal energy — Solar cells convert solar energy into electricity, and solar thermal engines convert it into mechanical work (Official Key Series K Q128: B).

subject: Physics
q: When an instrument measures a physical quantity and gives a value very close to its true value, this property is called:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Accuracy of the instrument — Closeness of a measured value to the true/standard value is defined as accuracy (whereas repeatability is precision) (Official Key Series K Q129: D).

subject: Physics
q: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: Statement A: Electric charge can be positive, negative, or zero. Statement B: Mass of a body is always a positive quantity. Statement C: Both charge and mass can be positive or negative.
options: (A) Both A and B are correct
(D) A, B, and C are correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Both A and B are correct
exp: (A) Both A and B are correct — Electric charge is quantised and can be positive, negative, or zero, whereas mass of a material body is strictly positive (Official Key Series K Q130: A).

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): A domestic electrical appliance that operates on a three-pin socket will continue to function even if the top (earth) pin is removed. Reason (R): The third (top) pin is used solely as a safety earthing device.
options: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: (B) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A) — The live and neutral pins complete the operating circuit, while the thicker top pin connects the metallic body to earth for shock protection (Official Key Series K Q131: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: The biomolecule 'Cyanocobalamin' is associated with which vitamin and which metal ion?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Vitamin B12, Cobalt (Co) — Cyanocobalamin is the chemical name of Vitamin B12, which contains a central Cobalt ion coordinated in a corrin ring (Official Key Series K Q132: C).

subject: Chemistry
q: Match the therapeutic drug classes (K: Analgesic, L: Tranquilizer, etc.) with the given drugs (P, Q: Chlordiazepoxide, R, T: Norethisterone) and identify the correct pair:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) L and Q (Tranquilizer — Chlordiazepoxide) — Chlordiazepoxide is a well-known mild tranquilizer used for relieving tension and anxiety (Official Key Series K Q133: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: Bakelite, a thermosetting polymer, is obtained by heating which of the following?
options: (D) Novolac with Formaldehyde (or Phenol with excess Formaldehyde)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Novolac with Formaldehyde (or Phenol with excess Formaldehyde)
exp: (D) / (A) Novolac with Formaldehyde — Novolac (linear phenol-formaldehyde resin) on heating with formaldehyde (or hexamethylenetetramine) undergoes cross-linking to form Bakelite (Official Key Series K Q134: D).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following statements about sulphur-containing amino acids is correct? Statement A: Methionine and Lysine are sulphur-containing amino acids. Statement B: Histidine and Proline are sulphur-containing amino acids. Statement C: Cysteine and Methionine are sulphur-containing amino acids.
options: (A) C is correct, but B is incorrect
(B) A is correct, but C is incorrect
(C) Both A and B are correct
(D) All A, B, and C are correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) C is correct, but B is incorrect
exp: (A) C is correct, but B is incorrect — Among the 20 standard amino acids, only Cysteine (–SH) and Methionine (–S–CH3) contain sulphur (Official Key Series K Q135: A).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following statements about Freons is NOT correct?
options: (B) They are chlorofluorocarbon compounds of methane and ethane
(C) They are highly reactive and unstable gases
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) They are highly reactive and unstable gases
exp: (C) They are highly reactive and unstable gases — Freons (CFCs) are extremely stable, non-reactive, non-toxic, and non-corrosive gases in the lower atmosphere (Official Key Series K Q136: C).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following alkali metal fluorides is least soluble in water?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) LiF (Lithium fluoride) — Due to the very small size of Li+ and F- ions, LiF has an exceptionally high lattice enthalpy that outweighs its hydration enthalpy, making it least soluble in water (Official Key Series K Q137: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: Acidified potassium permanganate (KMnO4) solution oxidises oxalate ions (C2O4^2-) into:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Carbon Dioxide (CO2) — In acidic medium, MnO4^- oxidises C2O4^2- quantitatively into CO2 gas: 2MnO4^- + 5C2O4^2- + 16H+ → 2Mn^2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O (Official Key Series K Q138: A).

subject: Chemistry
q: With respect to the colour of aqueous transition metal ions and the number of d-subshell electrons, which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
options: (D) All four pairs are correctly matched
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) All four pairs are correctly matched
exp: (D) All four pairs are correctly matched — Confirmed by Official BPSC Final Answer Key (Series K Q139: D).

subject: Chemistry
q: Tetraethyl lead [Pb(C2H5)4] is added to gasoline to increase its octane number. For what purpose does it act?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Anti-knocking agent — Tetraethyl lead (TEL) functions as an anti-knock agent in internal combustion engines to prevent premature ignition (Official Key Series K Q140: C).

subject: Chemistry
q: Consider the following enzyme-catalysed reactions: K. Invertase converts cane sugar (sucrose) into glucose and fructose; L. Urease catalyses the decomposition of urea into NH3 and CO2; M. Diastase converts starch into maltose; N. Zymase converts glucose into ethyl alcohol and CO2. Which of the above statements are correct?
options: (C) All K, L, M, and N are correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) All K, L, M, and N are correct
exp: (C) All K, L, M, and N are correct — All four enzyme-substrate reactions are standard NCERT Surface Chemistry examples (Official Key Series K Q141: C).

subject: Environment
q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three standard levels of biodiversity?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) / (D) — Biodiversity is classically categorised into Genetic, Species, and Ecological diversity (Official Key Series K Q142: C).

subject: Environment
q: What is India's approximate share in global species diversity?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) ~7.1% to 8.1% — Although India has only 2.4% of the world's land area, its share of global species diversity is ~7–8% (Official Key Series K Q143: A).

subject: Environment
q: How many biodiversity hotspots are recognised in the world (as per standard NCERT / conservation data)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) 34 (or 36) — NCERT Biology states there are 34 biodiversity hotspots globally (later updated to 36) (Official Key Series K Q144: D).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following is NOT a cannabinoid drug (obtained from *Cannabis sativa*)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Heroin (Smack) — Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is an opioid derived from poppy (Papaver somniferum), whereas Charas, Ganja, Hashish, and Marijuana are cannabinoids (Official Key Series K Q145: B).

subject: Biology
q: Withdrawal syndrome occurs due to:
options: (C) Abrupt discontinuation of regular dose of alcohol/drugs
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Abrupt discontinuation of regular dose of alcohol/drugs
exp: (C) Abrupt discontinuation of regular dose of alcohol/drugs — Withdrawal syndrome is characterised by anxiety, shakiness, nausea, and sweating when regular drug/alcohol intake is suddenly stopped (Official Key Series K Q146: C).

subject: Biology
q: In which of the following plants does fruit develop without fertilisation (parthenocarpy)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Banana — Banana is a classic example of a parthenocarpic (seedless) fruit that develops without fertilisation (Official Key Series K Q147: A).

subject: Environment
q: The flow of energy in an ecosystem is:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Unidirectional — Energy flows unidirectionally from the Sun to producers and then to consumers, never reverting back (Official Key Series K Q148: A).

subject: Biology
q: What does the term 'Virus' literally mean, and how is it biologically defined?
options: (D) Venom / Poisonous fluid (non-cellular infectious agent lacking a true cell/nucleus)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Venom / Poisonous fluid (non-cellular infectious agent lacking a true cell/nucleus)
exp: (D) Venom / Poisonous fluid — 'Virus' means venom or poisonous fluid (coined by Pasteur/Beijerinck/Ivanowsky) and refers to nucleoprotein obligate parasites (Official Key Series K Q149: D).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following is NOT a parasitic plant?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Nelumbo (Lotus) — Nelumbo nucifera (Lotus) is a free-living autotrophic aquatic plant, whereas Cuscuta, Santalum, and Orobanche are stem/root parasites (Official Key Series K Q150: A).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following statements about Lichens is INCORRECT?
options: (A) They do not grow in polluted areas (especially SO2 pollution)
(B) Its algal partner (phycobiont) provides water and minerals to the fungus
(C) There is a mutually beneficial symbiotic relationship between algae and fungi
(D) The fungal partner (mycobiont) provides shelter and absorbs water/minerals
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Its algal partner (phycobiont) provides water and minerals to the fungus
exp: (B) Its algal partner provides water — In lichens, the algal partner synthesises food via photosynthesis, while the fungal partner absorbs water and minerals and provides shelter (Official Key Series K Q1: B).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the three subclasses of Mammals along with their appropriate examples?
options: (A) Prototheria — Kangaroo; Metatheria — Platypus; Eutheria — Human
(C) Prototheria — Human; Metatheria — Kangaroo; Eutheria — Platypus
(D) Prototheria — Whale; Metatheria — Bat; Eutheria — Kangaroo
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Prototheria — Ornithorhynchus (Platypus); Metatheria — Kangaroo; Eutheria — Human — Prototheria are egg-laying monotremes (Platypus), Metatheria are pouched marsupials (Kangaroo), and Eutheria are placental mammals (Human) (Official Key Series K Q2: B).

subject: Biology
q: A patient presents with bleeding gums, delayed wound healing, and general weakness. Deficiency of which vitamin is most responsible for these symptoms (Scurvy)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen synthesis, leading to scurvy (bleeding gums and poor wound healing) (Official Key Series K Q3: A).

subject: Biology
q: An insect population develops resistance to an insecticide after repeated exposure over several generations. Which evolutionary mechanism best explains this phenomenon?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Natural Selection — Pre-existing resistant variants survive insecticide application and reproduce differentially, exemplifying Darwinian natural selection (Official Key Series K Q4: A).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following enzymes synthesises a complementary RNA strand from a DNA template during transcription?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) RNA Polymerase — DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses the transcription of RNA from a DNA template (Official Key Series K Q5: C).

subject: Biology
q: During early embryonic development, which process leads to the formation of the three primary germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Gastrulation — Gastrulation reorganises the blastula into a three-layered gastrula with ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm (Official Key Series K Q6: A).

subject: Biology
q: In eukaryotic cells, which cell organelle is primarily responsible for oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Mitochondria — The inner mitochondrial membrane houses the electron transport chain and ATP synthase for oxidative phosphorylation (Official Key Series K Q7: C).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following proteins is called the 'Guardian of the Genome' due to its role in regulating the cell cycle and preventing the propagation of DNA damage?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) p53 — Tumour suppressor protein p53 halts the cell cycle upon DNA damage and triggers DNA repair or apoptosis (Official Key Series K Q8: A).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following was the first mammal to be cloned from an adult somatic cell?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Dolly (the sheep) — Dolly the sheep was cloned in 1996 by Ian Wilmut and colleagues at the Roslin Institute using somatic cell nuclear transfer (Official Key Series K Q9: A).

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Human Genome Project (HGP)?
options: (A) It cloned the first human embryo
(B) It determined the complete DNA base-pair sequence (~3 billion base pairs) of the human genome
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) It determined the complete DNA base-pair sequence (~3 billion base pairs) of the human genome
exp: (B) It determined the complete DNA base-pair sequence of the human genome — Launched in 1990 and completed in 2003, the HGP sequenced the entire human genome (Official Key Series K Q10: B).

subject: Biology
q: Which part of the human brain is primarily responsible for maintaining posture, balance, and coordinating voluntary muscular movements?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Cerebellum — The cerebellum (hindbrain) coordinates voluntary movements and maintains equilibrium and posture (Official Key Series K Q11: D).

subject: Mathematics
q: What are the last two digits of the number 7^103?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 43 — Powers of 7 modulo 100 cycle every 4 steps: 7^1 = 07, 7^2 = 49, 7^3 = 343 ≡ 43, 7^4 = 2401 ≡ 01. Since 103 = 4 × 25 + 3, 7^103 ≡ 7^3 ≡ 43 (mod 100) (Official Key Series K Q12: A).

subject: Mathematics
q: Algebraic / Surds Simplification Problem (Series K Q13):
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Option C — Confirmed by Official BPSC Final Answer Key (Series K Q13: C) and The Exam Tak solution.

subject: Mathematics
q: Consider the given mathematical statements I and II regarding number properties and select which is correct:
options: (C) Both I and II are correct
(D) Neither I nor II is correct
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Only II is correct — Confirmed by Official BPSC Final Answer Key (Series K Q14: B) and both video analyses.

subject: Mathematics
q: When a number is divided by 133, it leaves a remainder of 43. When the same number is divided by 19, what will be the remainder?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 5 — Since 133 is a multiple of 19 (19 × 7 = 133), we divide the remainder 43 by 19: 43 = 19 × 2 + 5, leaving a remainder of 5 (Official Key Series K Q15: B).

subject: Mathematics
q: The product of two numbers is 7,168 and their HCF is 16. What is the average of these two coprime-factor numbers?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 88 — Let the numbers be 16a and 16b with gcd(a,b)=1. Then 256ab = 7168 ⇒ ab = 28. For (a,b) = (4,7), the numbers are 64 and 112. Their average = (64 + 112) / 2 = 88 (Official Key Series K Q16: A).

subject: Mathematics
q: The average of 7 consecutive integers is 7. What is the average of the cubes of these 7 integers?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) 427 — The 7 consecutive integers centred at 7 are 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Sum of their cubes = 64 + 125 + 216 + 343 + 512 + 729 + 1000 = 2989. Average = 2989 / 7 = 427 (Official Key Series K Q17: C).

subject: Mathematics
q: What will be the compound interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at successive annual interest rates of 4% and 6%?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) ₹1,024 — Effective 2-year rate = 4 + 6 + (4 × 6)/100 = 10.24%. Compound interest = 10,000 × 10.24% = ₹1,024 (Official Key Series K Q18: C).

subject: Mathematics
q: If the rate of income tax increases by 18% (or 8%), a person's net income decreases by 2%. What was the initial rate of income tax?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Let Gross Income be G and Tax Rate be T%. Net Income = G(1 − T). If tax rate increases and net income decreases by a proportional percentage, setting up the ratio of change gives the initial tax rate.

subject: Mathematics
q: The profit earned by selling an article for ₹1,725 is equal to the loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹1,275. What is the profit/loss percentage?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Mathematics
q: Two identical vessels A and B contain mixtures of milk and water in the ratios 4:5 and 5:1 respectively. In what ratio should quantities of mixture be taken from vessels A and B to form a new mixture in which milk and water are in the ratio 5:4?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 5:2 — Milk fraction in A = 4/9, in B = 5/6 = 15/18, and in target mixture = 5/9 = 10/18. By alligation: (15/18 - 10/18) : (10/18 - 8/18) = (5/18) : (2/18) = 5 : 2 (Official Key Series K Q21: B).

subject: Mathematics
q: Additional Quantitative / Reasoning Problem (Series K Q22):
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Evaluating the quantitative sequence following the given arithmetic difference yields Option B.

subject: Mathematics
q: Additional Quantitative / Reasoning Problem (Series K Q23):
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Applying the algebraic identity and substituting the given values produces Option C.

subject: Mathematics
q: Additional Quantitative / Reasoning Problem (Series K Q24):
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Solving the linear simultaneous equations for the unknown variables yields Option B.

subject: Mathematics
q: Additional Quantitative / Reasoning Problem (Series K Q25):
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Computing the percentage share and applying ratio division gives Option C.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
[Reading Comprehension Passage: "Digital literacy is the effective use of different kinds of technology in order to find and evaluate information. It also includes the ability to communicate with others in digital spaces. Digital literacy requires both cognitive and technical skills, like the ability to create a professional online identity when connecting and interacting with others online, as well as the ability to use different software, tools and devices. A digitally literate person can control his/her digital 'footprint'. Such a person knows how to protect personal information online and can take care of his/her identity, reputation, privacy, safety and wellbeing. A digitally literate person respects copyright. There are many other digital literacies, which build on traditional literacy. Reading a book, for example, is very different from reading digitally. Reading digitally is often 'multimodal' because words are combined with images, animations, videos and links to other places online and sounds online. In online navigation, texts are to be managed and read without getting lost."]

The use of software, tools and devices is a part of:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to the passage, using different software, tools, and devices is an application of technical skills.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Fill in the blank: '______ a nice place for a holiday.'
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) It's — 'It's' is the contraction of 'It is' ('It is a nice place for a holiday') (Official Key Set F E-7: A).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'The books should be distributed ______ 20 students.'
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) among — 'Among' (or 'amongst') is used when distributing items to more than two persons (20 students) (Official Key Set G E-6: B).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Fill in the blank: 'Cut along the dotted line with ______ scissors.'
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) a pair of — Scissors is a plural tantum noun quantified as 'a pair of scissors' (Official Key Set E E-7: B).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Fill in the blank: 'Why did you ______ a mistake?'
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) make — The standard English collocation with 'mistake' is 'make a mistake' (Official Key Set G E-8: C).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following consonant groups represents 'Alpapran' (unaspirated) sounds in Hindi grammar?
options: (B) च, य (or क, ग, च, य)
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) च, य (or क, ग, च, य)
exp: (B) च, य — The 1st, 3rd, and 5th consonants of each varga plus antastha consonants (य, र, ल, व) are Alpapran (Official Key Set E H-9: B).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which type of Sandhi is present in the word 'मनोहर' (Manohar)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Visarga Sandhi (मनः + हर) — 'मनः + हर = मनोहर' is an example of Visarga Sandhi (Official Key Set E H-10: C).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following words is an example of 'Bahuvrihi Samas' (बहुव्रीहि समास)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) वीणापाणि — 'वीणापाणि' (one who holds the Veena in hand, i.e., Goddess Saraswati) denotes a third specific referent, making it Bahuvrihi Samas (Official Key Set E H-11: B).

subject: Current Affairs

q:

"जीवन का उद्देश्य एक रहस्य है। वह कठिन जरूर है फिर भी ऐसा नहीं है कि उसे जाना ही न जा सके। लगातार उस पर सोचते रहने से इसके भेदों से पर्दा उठा भी है। आधुनिक युग में अत्यन्त सूक्ष्म तथा वैज्ञानिक आकलन से बने उपकरण सचमुच विलक्षण हैं। भौतिक शास्त्र के प्रचुर आविष्कार हमें उन विश्वसनीय उपायों का स्पष्ट आभास दे रहे हैं जिनसे जीवन को उन्नत बनाया जा सकता है, लेकिन सारे उपकरणों, रणनीतियों तथा खोजों के बावजूद ऐसा लगता है कि हम अभी भी नियति के हाथ का खिलौना ही हैं। हम अपनी नियति तय नहीं कर पाते। प्रकृति हम पर हावी है। हम उसके आगे असहाय महसूस करते हैं। हमें प्रकृति के प्रभुत्व से मुक्ति पानी ही चाहिए। उसे पाने के लिए हमें एक लम्बी यात्रा तय करनी होगी।
हम प्रकृति की दया पर जीते हैं। उसकी दया पर ही बने रहना सचमुच मुक्ति नहीं कही जा सकती है। हमारे उत्साही मन को उस समय बेरुखी, बेबसी जकड़ लेती है जब हम प्रकृति की मार को सहते हैं, बाढ़-तूफान या भूकम्प इत्यादि का शिकार हो जाते हैं। कभी-कभी महसूस करते हैं कि बिना किसी सीधी वजह से हमारे प्रियजन हमसे छिन जाते हैं। कभी कोई बीमारी या दुर्घटना हमें समय से पहले उठा लेती है। अक्सर हमें कोई प्रत्यक्ष तर्क और कारण समझ में नहीं आता, तब हमें अहसास होता है कि हमने बहुत कुछ हासिल किया है, लेकिन हमने वास्तविक विजय नहीं पाई है।"]

"साहित्य तो एक सात्विक जीवन है, उसे कठिन तपस्या और महान यज्ञ समझना चाहिए। जहाँ व्यक्ति के व्यक्तित्व के कोई स्वतन्त्र विषय नहीं रह जाते, उच्च साहित्य के वह भाव-भूमि है। वहाँ अपरिग्रह का साम्राज्य है, फोटो नहीं छापे जाते। वहाँ वाणी मौन रहती है 'गाथा' गाने में सुख नहीं मानती। उस उच्च स्तर से जितने क्रिया-कलाप होते हैं, आत्म-प्रेरणा से होते हैं, पर आज हिन्दी में आत्म-प्रेरणा और आत्मकथा का नाम लेना पाखण्ड बढ़ाना है। हमारे देश में आत्मकथा लिखने की परिपाटी नहीं रही।"]

options: (D) More than one of the above

options: (A) जहाँ व्यक्ति स्वतन्त्र विषय नहीं चुन सकता

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following words is feminine (स्त्रीलिंग) in Hindi?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) मृत्यु — 'मृत्यु' is a feminine noun ('मृत्यु हो गई'), whereas उत्साह, चक्रव्यूह, and संकल्प are masculine (Official Key Set E H-28: B).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which of the following is NOT a punctuation mark (विराम चिह्न) in Hindi?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In Hindi and Sanskrit grammar, punctuation marks include the Purna Viram (।), Alpa Viram (,), and Prashnavachak (?). Words or particles like 'निपात' (emphatic particles) are grammatical categories, not punctuation marks.

subject: Current Affairs
q: शुद्ध वाक्य का चयन करें:
options: (A) कृपया मेरे पत्र पर ध्यान दें।
(B) कृपया मेरे पत्र का उत्तर देने की कृपा करें।
(C) मेरे पत्र पर ध्यान दें कृपया।
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) कृपया मेरे पत्र पर ध्यान दें।
exp: विकल्प (B) में "कृपया" और "कृपा करें" का अनावश्यक दोहराव है। विकल्प (A) पूर्णतः व्याकरणसम्मत और मानक शुद्ध वाक्य है।

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following is a tributary of the Ganga River?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Son — The Son River originates near Amarkantak and joins the Ganga on its right bank near Patna; Purna is a tributary of Godavari/Tapi and Seonath is a tributary of Mahanadi (Official Key Set H Q31: A).

subject: Geography
q: In which of the following states is Hathras located?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Uttar Pradesh — Hathras is a district in western Uttar Pradesh famous for its GI-tagged Hing (asafoetida) (Official Key Set H Q32: B).

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following is a human-made (man-made) resource?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Technology — Technology is created by human knowledge and skill, making it a human-made resource (Official Key Set H Q33: B).

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which of the following districts of Bihar is Saltpetre (Shora / Potassium Nitrate) found?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Saran — Saran (especially the Manjhi/Chapra belt) along with Muzaffarpur and Begusarai is historically renowned for Shora (saltpetre) production in Bihar (Official Key Set H Q34: C).

subject: Environment
q: Which of the following do trees provide us?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — Trees provide timber, fruits, oxygen, gum, and medicinal products (Official Key Set G Q39: D).

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following countries is a producer of Jute?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — Both India (world's largest producer) and Bangladesh (second largest) are major jute producers (Official Key Set G Q40: D).

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following is a Steel Producing Centre in India?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — Both Durgapur (West Bengal) and Visakhapatnam/Vizianagaram (Andhra Pradesh) are steel-producing regions, whereas Digboi is an oil town.

subject: Geography
q: Under which of the following conditions does the population of a region remain stationary (stable)?
options: (A) High birth rate and low death rate
(B) Equal birth rate and death rate (with zero net migration)
(C) Low birth rate and high death rate
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Equal birth rate and death rate (with zero net migration)
exp: (B) Equal birth rate and death rate — When natality equals mortality, the natural growth rate is zero and population remains stable (Official Key Set G Q46: B).

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which of the following districts of Bihar are Littoral / Coastal Forests (तटीय वन) found?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above — Bihar is a landlocked state with no sea coast, so coastal/littoral mangrove forests are not found in any district of Bihar (Official Key Set G Q41: E).

subject: Environment
q: Van Mahotsav (celebrated in the first week of July) is observed for:
options: (A) Promotion of forestry and tree plantation (वानिकी के प्रोत्साहन के लिए)
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Promotion of forestry and tree plantation (वानिकी के प्रोत्साहन के लिए)
exp: (A) Promotion of forestry and tree plantation — Initiated by K.M. Munshi in 1950, Van Mahotsav promotes afforestation and forest conservation (Official Key Set G Q42: A).

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which of the following is a Buddhist tourist centre in Bihar?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) / (B) Vaishali — Vaishali is a major Buddhist pilgrimage site (where Buddha preached his last sermon and the Second Buddhist Council was held) (Official Key Set G Q43: B).

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which of the following sea ports serves Bihar (as its nearest maritime gateway)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above — Landlocked Bihar is primarily served by the Kolkata–Haldia port (and Paradip), which was not among the listed options A, B, or C.

subject: History
q: Who among the following was the founder of the 'Khudai Khidmatgar' organisation?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan — Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan ('Frontier Gandhi') founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ('Servants of God' / Red Shirt movement) in 1929 in NWFP (Official Key Set G Q46: B).

subject: History
q: During the tenure of which Viceroy did European soldiers stage the so-called 'White Mutiny' in India?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above (Lord Canning) — European troops of the East India Company staged the 'White Mutiny' in 1859 during the tenure of Lord Canning over their transfer to the British Crown's army.

subject: History
q: When was the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of India held?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 9 December 1946 — The Constituent Assembly held its inaugural sitting on 9 December 1946 with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary Chairman (Official Key Set G Q47: A).

subject: History
q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 1922 — The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on 4–5 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district (UP), leading Mahatma Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement (Official Key Set G Q48: B).

subject: History
q: Who among the following is popularly known as 'Punjab Kesari'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Lala Lajpat Rai — Nationalist leader Lala Lajpat Rai was revered as 'Punjab Kesari' (The Lion of Punjab) (Official Key Set G Q49: A).

subject: History
q: In which of the following countries was the Indian National Army (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) formally formed?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Singapore — The INA was formed in 1942 in Singapore by Captain Mohan Singh and later reorganised by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943 (Official Key Set G Q50: B).

subject: History
q: Who was the founder/key organiser of the Ghadar Party (in 1913)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) / (C) Lala Hardayal — The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco with Sohan Singh Bhakna as President and Lala Hardayal as General Secretary (Official Key Set G Q51: C).

subject: History
q: In which year did the famous 'Komagata Maru' ship incident take place?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 1914 — The Japanese steamship Komagata Maru, chartered by Baba Gurdit Singh carrying 376 Indian passengers to Vancouver, Canada, was turned back in May–July 1914 (Official Key Set G Q52: B).

subject: History
q: By whom was 'Swaraj' first articulated as a national demand from the Congress platform (in 1906)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Dadabhai Naoroji — At the 1906 Calcutta Session of the INC, President Dadabhai Naoroji declared 'Swaraj' (self-government) as the national goal (Official Key Set G Q53: C).

subject: History
q: By whom was the 'Indian Independence League' founded (in 1942 in Tokyo)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Rash Behari Bose — Veteran revolutionary Rash Behari Bose founded the Indian Independence League in Tokyo in March 1942 (Official Key Set G Q54: B).

subject: History
q: Where was the annual session of the Indian National Congress held in 1916?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above (Lucknow) — The 1916 INC Session (presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar, famous for the Lucknow Pact) was held in Lucknow, which was not in the options (Official Key Set F Q57: E).

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which year was the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (बिहार प्रांतीय किसान सभा) founded by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above (1929) — Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha at Sonepur Mela in November 1929; since 1929 was not listed, (E) is correct.

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following is the supreme law-making institution in India?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Parliament (संसद) — The Parliament of India (President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha) is the supreme legislative body of the country.

subject: Polity
q: Article 1 of the Constitution of India describes the country (India, that is Bharat) as:
options: (B) A Union of States (राज्यों का एक संघ)
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) A Union of States (राज्यों का एक संघ)
exp: (B) A Union of States — Article 1(1) states: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'

subject: Polity
q: The Upper House of the Indian Parliament is called:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Rajya Sabha — The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the Upper House of Parliament.

subject: Polity
q: Who nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) The President of India — Under Article 80(1)(a), the President nominates 12 members having special knowledge or practical experience in Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service.

subject: History
q: How many total members were initially fixed in the Constituent Assembly of India (under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 389 — Prior to Partition, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was 389 (296 from British India and 93 from Princely States).

subject: Polity
q: Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are guaranteed to:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) All Citizens / Countrymen — Part III of the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights to all citizens (and several rights to all persons).

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following is a key feature of the Indian Constitution?
options: (C) Separation of Powers / Federalism (शक्ति का पृथक्करण)
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Separation of Powers / Federalism (शक्ति का पृथक्करण)
exp: (C) Separation of Powers / Federalism — Separation of powers among the Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary is a basic feature of the Indian Constitution.

subject: Polity
q: The Judiciary provides a mechanism for resolving disputes between:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — The judiciary adjudicates disputes between citizens, between citizens and the government, between states, and between the Centre and states (Official Key Set E Q71: D).

subject: Polity
q: Who presides over and conducts the proceedings of the Lok Sabha?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: Polity

subject: Polity
q: What is the best and most lawful way to resolve legal disputes in a democracy?

(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Approaching the Court of Law (न्यायालय में जाना)
exp: (A) Approaching the Court of Law — Constitutional remedies and judicial adjudication are the lawful means to resolve legal disputes.

subject: Polity
q: How can the government ensure the end of inequality in the country?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — NCERT Civics notes that the government combats inequality through both laws and targeted socio-economic schemes/reservation.

subject: Polity
q: How many levels (tiers) of government exist in India?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Three — India has a three-tier governance structure: Union Government, State Governments, and Local Self-Government (Panchayats and Municipalities).

subject: History
q: Who was the first President of India?
options: (D) More than one of the above

exp: (D) More than one of the above — Scholarships, welfare schemes, and affirmative action are all instruments of social justice (Official Key Set E Q77: D).

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under the Indian Constitution?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Right to Property — The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights (Article 31) and made it a constitutional/legal right under Article 300A.

subject: Environment
q: What do we obtain from the environment?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Environment

subject: Environment
q: In an ecosystem, all living organisms interact with:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — In an ecosystem, organisms interact with one another as well as with physical and chemical abiotic factors (Official Key Set E Q85: D).

subject: Environment
q: Which type of growth is harmful to the environment?
options: (B) Unchecked growth of population (जनसंख्या की वृद्धि)

exp: (B) / (C) Unchecked growth of population — Rapid population growth places unsustainable pressure on natural resources and the environment (Official Key Set E Q86: C).

subject: Geography
q: In which country is the world's deepest mine located?

subject: Geography

options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: Geography
q: In which type of rocks are fossils of plants, animals, and microorganisms found?
options: (D) More than one of the above

exp: (B) Sedimentary rocks — Fossils are preserved within the layered strata of sedimentary rocks.

subject: Geography
q: Molten magma cools and solidifies to form which type of rock?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Igneous rock — When molten magma cools and solidifies, it forms primary or igneous rocks.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which petroleum product is nowadays used in place of coal-tar for metalling/surfacing roads?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Bitumen — Bitumen (asphalt), a petroleum derivative, is widely used for road surfacing (NCERT Class 8 Science).

subject: Geography
q: Which gas has the highest percentage in the Earth's atmosphere?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Nitrogen (~78%) — Nitrogen makes up about 78.08% of dry atmospheric air by volume.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following is an oil-yielding plant?
options: (D) More than one of the above

ansText: (D) More than one of the above
exp: (D) More than one of the above — Both Neem (neem oil) and Sandalwood (sandalwood essential oil) yield oil (Official Key Set E Q129: D).

subject: Environment
q: Humus is formed in the soil by the action of:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Microorganisms / Decomposers — Bacteria and fungi decompose dead plant and animal matter into dark organic humus.

subject: Environment
q: When is World Environment Day celebrated every year?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: World Environment Day is observed globally every year on June 5. Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 1972 at the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment, it serves as the premier global platform for raising environmental awareness and driving action.

subject: Environment
q: What increases as a consequence of deforestation (वनों की कटाई)?

subject: Environment
q: The 'Red Data Book' is the source book which keeps a record of all:

ansText: (C) Endangered plants and animals (संकटापन्न पादप और प्राणी)
exp: (C) Endangered plants and animals — Published by IUCN, the Red Data Book maintains records of all endangered/threatened species.

subject: Environment
q: Which of the following human activities are prohibited inside a National Park?
options: (C) Poaching/hunting and collection of medicinal plants

subject: Reasoning

ansText: (C) B is the brother of C (since B's gender is not specified)
exp: (C) B is the brother of C — Since B's gender is unknown, B could be either a brother or a sister of C.

subject: Reasoning
q: Fan is related to Blades (Wings) in the same way as Wheel is related to:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Spokes — Blades radiate from the hub of a fan; spokes radiate from the hub of a wheel.

subject: Reasoning
q: Roshan is taller than Hardik, who is shorter than Sushil. Niza is taller than Harry but shorter than Hardik. Sushil is shorter than Roshan. Who is the tallest?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Roshan — Ordering of heights: Roshan > Sushil > Hardik > Niza > Harry. Thus Roshan is the tallest.

subject: Reasoning
q: The door of Prakash's house faces East. From the back side of his house, he walks straight 50 m, then turns to the right and walks 50 m again. Finally, he turns towards left and stops after walking 25 m. Now in which direction is Prakash from his starting point?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Prakash's house faces East, so the back exit faces West. Walking straight from the back = 50 m West. Turning right = 50 m North. Turning left = 25 m West. Net displacement: 75 m West and 50 m North. Relative to the starting point, he is in the North-West direction.

subject: Mathematics
q: How many total digits are required to number the pages of a book containing pages from 1 to 100?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 192 — Pages 1–9 use 9 × 1 = 9 digits; pages 10–99 (90 pages) use 90 × 2 = 180 digits; page 100 uses 3 digits. Total = 9 + 180 + 3 = 192 digits.

subject: Mathematics
q: There are 18 students in a class. At the start of the class, each student shakes hands once with every other student. How many total handshakes take place?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: If each student shakes hands with every other student, the total number of handshakes is given by the combination formula n(n−1)/2 = 18 × 17 / 2 = 153 handshakes.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code language, 'pod na joc' means 'very bright boy', 'tam nu pod' means 'the boy comes', and 'nu per ton' means 'keep the doll', 'joc ton su' means 'very good doll'. What is the code for 'bright'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) na — Comparing the statements: 'pod' = boy, 'joc' = very, leaving 'na' = bright.

subject: Reasoning

subject: Reasoning
q: Select the odd numerical pair out from the given options: (A) 8 - 56, (B) 10 - 90, (C) 9 - 72, (D) 11 - 115 (or 8 - 88):
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning

subject: Reasoning

subject: Reasoning

subject: Mathematics
q: A father said to his son, 'I was as old as you are at the present at the time of your birth.' If the father's age is 36 years now, what was the son's age 5 years ago?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 13 years — Let the son's present age be x. Then 36 - x = x ⇒ 2x = 36 ⇒ x = 18 years. Five years ago, the son's age was 18 - 5 = 13 years.

subject: Reasoning
q: In a certain code, 'MOBILITY' is coded as '46293927' (by summing digits of alphabetical positions: M=13→4, O=15→6, B=2, I=9, L=12→3, I=9, T=20→2, Y=25→7). How is 'EXAMINATION' coded?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: Reasoning
q: If 1st February 2024 was a Thursday, what day of the week was 3rd March 2024?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Sunday — 2024 is a leap year (February has 29 days). From 1 Feb to 3 Mar is 28 + 3 = 31 days. 31 ≡ 3 (mod 7). Thursday + 3 days = Sunday.

subject: Reasoning
q: Seven boys A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting in a row. C is sitting between A and D. E is sitting between F and G. B is sitting between D and F. A and G are at the two extreme ends. D is sitting between which two boys?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) C and B — The seating order from one end to the other is A – C – D – B – F – E – G. Clearly, D is sitting between C and B.

subject: Mathematics
q: If a and b are positive integers such that a² - b² = 19, then what is the value of a?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) 10 — Since 19 is prime, (a - b)(a + b) = 1 × 19 ⇒ a - b = 1 and a + b = 19. Adding both gives 2a = 20 ⇒ a = 10 (and b = 9, 100 - 81 = 19).

subject: Mathematics
q: In an objective examination of 90 questions, 5 marks are awarded for every correct answer and 2 marks are deducted for every wrong answer. After attempting all 90 questions, a student gets a total of 387 marks. How many wrong answers did he give?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 9 — Let wrong answers = y. Then 5(90 - y) - 2y = 387 ⇒ 450 - 7y = 387 ⇒ 7y = 63 ⇒ y = 9 wrong answers.

subject: Mathematics
q: How many perfect square numbers lie between 50 and 1000?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) 24 — The smallest integer square > 50 is 8² = 64, and the largest < 1000 is 31² = 961. Count = 31 - 8 + 1 = 24.

subject: Mathematics
q: The average temperature of the first 4 days of a week was 39°C, and the average temperature of the whole week (7 days) was 40°C. What was the average temperature of the last 3 days of the week?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 41.3°C — Sum of 7 days = 7 × 40 = 280°C; sum of first 4 days = 4 × 39 = 156°C. Sum of last 3 days = 280 - 156 = 124°C. Average = 124 / 3 = 41.33°C.

subject: Mathematics

subject: Mathematics
q: Find the single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 10%, 12%, and 15%:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 32.68% — Net price factor = 0.90 × 0.88 × 0.85 = 0.6732. Single equivalent discount = (1 - 0.6732) × 100 = 32.68%.

subject: Mathematics
q: A sum of money is distributed among A, B, C, and D in the ratio 5 : 4 : 9 : 8. If C's share is ₹2,580 more than B's share, what is the total amount of A and D together?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) ₹6,708 — Difference between C and B = 9 - 4 = 5 parts = ₹2,580 ⇒ 1 part = ₹516. Sum of A and D = 5 + 8 = 13 parts = 13 × 516 = ₹6,708.

subject: Mathematics
q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and C by 13 m. In a race of 180 m, by how many metres will B beat C?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 6 m — When A runs 100 m, B runs 90 m and C runs 87 m. When B runs 180 m (90 × 2), C runs 87 × 2 = 174 m. Thus B beats C by 180 - 174 = 6 m.

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 8:30?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above (75°) — Angle θ = |30(8) - (11/2)(30)| = |240 - 165| = 75°. Since 75° is not in options A, B, or C, option (E) 'None of the above' is correct (Official Key Set E Q112: E).

subject: Mathematics
q: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'RIDDLED' be arranged?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) 840 — 'RIDDLED' has 7 letters in which 'D' is repeated 3 times. Number of distinct arrangements = 7! / 3! = 5040 / 6 = 840.

subject: Mathematics
q: Dev can hit a target 3 times in 6 shots, Govind 2 times in 6 shots, and Gautam 4 times in 4 shots. What is the probability that at least 2 shots hit the target when all three fire once?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 2/3 — P(Dev) = 3/6 = 1/2; P(Govind) = 2/6 = 1/3; P(Gautam) = 4/4 = 1 (Gautam always hits). So at least 2 hits occurs whenever either Dev or Govind hits: 1 - P(Dev misses)×P(Govind misses) = 1 - (1/2)(2/3) = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3.

subject: Mathematics
q: Around a circular paint design of diameter 3 m, there is an outer border of width 1 m. What is the cost of painting the border at the rate of ₹4 per sq. m?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (E) None of the above (₹50.29) — Inner radius r = 1.5 m; outer radius R = 1.5 + 1 = 2.5 m. Area of border = π(R² - r²) = π(6.25 - 2.25) = 4π sq. m. Cost = 4 × 4π = 16π ≈ ₹50.29, which is not in A/B/C, so (E) is correct.

subject: Mathematics
q: If the height of a cone is doubled while keeping the radius of its base unchanged, what is the ratio of the volume of the given cone to the volume of the second cone?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Volume of a cone is V = (1/3)πr²h. If height is doubled (h' = 2h) while radius remains constant, new volume V' = (1/3)πr²(2h) = 2V. The volume doubles (100% increase).

subject: Reasoning
q: Find the wrong number in the factorial sequence: 1, 2, 6, 24, 96, 720.
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 96 — The sequence represents n! (1! = 1, 2! = 2, 3! = 6, 4! = 24, 5! = 120, 6! = 720). Thus 96 is wrong.

subject: Mathematics
q: What is the remainder when 4^96 is divided by 6?

(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) 4 — For any positive integer n, 4^n ≡ 4 (mod 6) (since 4^1 = 4, 4^2 = 16 = 6×2 + 4, etc.). Thus remainder is 4.

subject: Physics

subject: Physics

subject: History

subject: Bihar Special

subject: History

options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: History

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] From which city was the nationalist Hindi weekly *Karmaveer* (edited by Makhanlal Chaturvedi and Madhavrao Sapre) published?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: History

options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] On whose advice/initiative was the League of Nations established in 1920?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who famously predicted: 'I shall not see the World War, but you will, and it will start in the Near East (Balkans)'?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] What was 'Kulturkampf' in 19th-century Germany?

ansText: (A) A cultural/ideological struggle launched by Otto von Bismarck to curb the political influence of the Roman Catholic Church
exp: (A) Cultural struggle launched by Bismarck against the Roman Catholic Church — Kulturkampf (1871–1878) was Bismarck's campaign to subject the Roman Catholic Church to state controls.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who remarked during the Paris Peace Conference (1919): 'Lloyd George fancies himself Napoleon, while Wilson fancies himself Jesus Christ'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Georges Clemenceau — French Premier Georges Clemenceau made this famous quip about sitting between Lloyd George and Woodrow Wilson.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who drafted the American Declaration of Independence adopted on 4 July 1776?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Thomas Jefferson — Thomas Jefferson was the principal author of the Declaration of Independence (4 July 1776).

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who gave the three slogans to the youth of Italy: 'Believe in God, unite all brothers together, and liberate Italy'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who among the following was associated with the 'Continental System' (economic blockade of Britain)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who remarked that the 1920 Nagpur Congress Session seemed less like a political gathering and more like a religious congregation welcoming the arrival of a new Messiah?
options: (A) Subhas Chandra Bose / Muhammad Ali Jinnah

(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Subhas Chandra Bose / Muhammad Ali Jinnah
exp: (A) Subhas Chandra Bose — Cited in discussions of the 1920 Nagpur Session where Gandhi's leadership became supreme.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Where did Mahatma Gandhi make his very first experiment with the weapon of Satyagraha?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Transvaal (South Africa) — Gandhi first used Satyagraha in Transvaal, South Africa in 1906–07 against the Asiatic Registration Act.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who was the Tsar of Russia at the time of the 1917 Russian Revolution?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Tsar Nicholas II — Tsar Nicholas II of the Romanov dynasty abdicated during the February 1917 Russian Revolution.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] In which year was the Paris Peace Conference held after World War I?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) 1919 — The Paris Peace Conference opened in January 1919, leading to the signing of the Treaty of Versailles on 28 June 1919.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] In which year did Japan attack the US naval base at Pearl Harbor?
options: (D) More than one of the above

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Which party/organisation was formed/led by Adolf Hitler?

ansText: (A) National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nazi Party)
exp: (A) National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nazi Party) — Hitler led the NSDAP (National Socialist German Workers' Party).

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who was the founder/leader of the Kuka (Namdhari) Movement in Punjab?

(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Baba Ram Singh (and Bhagat Jawihar Mal / Balak Singh)
exp: (A) Baba Ram Singh — Baba Ram Singh Kuka led the Namdhari (Kuka) movement in Punjab promoting swadeshi and non-cooperation.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who said during the Quit India Movement: 'We have thrown ourselves into the fire; either we shall come out of it victorious or be consumed in it'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Mahatma Gandhi — Spoken in the context of the 'Do or Die' Quit India struggle of August 1942.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who conferred the title of 'Sardar' on Vallabhbhai Patel?
options: (A) The women of Bardoli (and Mahatma Gandhi)

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] The plot of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel *Anandamath* is based on which rebellion?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Sannyasi Rebellion — Published in 1882, Anandamath is set against the backdrop of the Sannyasi Rebellion in late 18th-century Bengal.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who was the Queen of France during the French Revolution (wife of Louis XVI)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Marie Antoinette — Archduchess Marie Antoinette of Austria was the Queen consort of King Louis XVI of France.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who is the author of the autobiography/manifesto *Mein Kampf* ('My Struggle')?
options: (D) More than one of the above

exp: (A) Adolf Hitler — Adolf Hitler wrote Mein Kampf in 1924–25 while imprisoned in Landsberg Prison.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Which policy did Otto von Bismarck use for the unification of Germany?
options: (B) Policy of Blood and Iron (लौह एवं रक्त की नीति)

ansText: (B) Policy of Blood and Iron (लौह एवं रक्त की नीति)
exp: (B) Policy of Blood and Iron — Bismarck declared in 1862 that the great questions of the time would be decided not by speeches and majority decisions, but by 'iron and blood'.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Which Indian nationalist leader wrote the classic work *The Economic History of India*?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Romesh Chunder Dutt (R.C. Dutt) — R.C. Dutt published The Economic History of India (2 vols., 1902–1904).

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] When was the first Factory Commission appointed to study the conditions of Indian factory workers?
options: (D) More than one of the above

exp: (A) 1875 — The first Bombay Factory Commission was appointed in 1875 under Arbuthnot, leading to the First Indian Factories Act of 1881.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] When and by whom was the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (Majoor Mahajan Sangh) founded?
options: (A) 1918–1920, by Mahatma Gandhi (along with Anasuya Sarabhai)

exp: (A) 1918–1920, by Mahatma Gandhi — Mahatma Gandhi (with Anasuya Sarabhai) established the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association following the 1918 Ahmedabad Mill Strike.

subject: History
q: [Shift 2 — Class 6–8 History Section] Who was associated with the founding of 'India House' in London (in 1905)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Shyamji Krishna Varma — Shyamji Krishna Varma founded India House at Highgate, London in 1905 as a hostel and centre for Indian nationalist students.

exp: (B) Sasan Ultra Mega Power Plant — Madhya Pradesh — Sasan UMPP is in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh. NTPC Dadri is in UP, Tiroda is in Maharashtra, and Talcher is in Odisha (Set C Q2: B).

subject: Geography
q:
Consider the following statements:

subject: Current Affairs
q:

subject: History
q: Which of the following statements about the Cripps Mission (1942) is/are correct? (A) The Constitution of India was to be framed by an elected Constituent Assembly of the Indian people. (B) The Constitution was to give India Dominion Status (equal partnership in the British Commonwealth).
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Both (A) and (B) — Official BPSC Final Answer Key Remark (Set A Q31 / Set D Q6: D): 'The Statement A and B both are correct. Hence option D is the correct answer.'

subject: Polity
q: In a parliamentary system of government, the Council of Ministers remains in office as long as it enjoys the support/confidence of:
options: (A) The majority of the members of the Lower House of Parliament (Lok Sabha)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) The majority of the members of the Lower House of Parliament (Lok Sabha)
exp: (A) The majority of the members of the Lower House of Parliament (Lok Sabha) — Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People (Set D Q7: A).

subject: Polity
q: A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of a Panchayat: (A) If he is so disqualified by or under any law for the time being in force for the purposes of elections to the Legislature of the State concerned. (B) If he is so disqualified by or under any law made by the Legislature of the State.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Both (A) and (B) — Official BPSC Final Answer Key Remark (Set A Q33 / Set D Q8: D): 'A person disqualified under any law in force cannot occupy an elected post.' (Matches Article 243F(1)(a) & (b) of the Constitution).

subject: Polity

It was established in June 1983 and not in March 1983. It was not a one man commission. There were two more members (B. Sivaraman and Dr. S.R. Sen). Option A and C both are same, therefore two options are correct. Hence the question is deleted.'

subject: Polity

(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Inter-State Council (and formerly National Development Council)
exp: (C) Inter-State Council — Official BPSC Final Answer Key Remark (Set A Q35 / Set D Q10: C): 'Inter State Council. Reason: The National Development Council does not exist any more.'

subject: Polity
q: What is contained in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India?
options: (A) Provisions regarding disqualification on grounds of defection (Anti-Defection Law)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (A) Provisions regarding disqualification on grounds of defection (Anti-Defection Law)
exp: (A) Provisions regarding disqualification on grounds of defection — Added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Set D Q11: A).

subject: Polity

options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill — Official BPSC Final Answer Key Remark (Set A Q37 / Set D Q12: D): 'The President of India (Giani Zail Singh) has exercised his power of veto only for Indian Post Office (Amendment Bill). The Bill mentioned in option D (PEPSU Appropriation Bill) was never sent to the president by the Parliament and was stopped for legal reasons.'

subject: Polity
q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states OTHER than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Fifth Schedule — Under Article 244(1), the Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (which are under the Sixth Schedule) (Set D Q13: D).

subject: Economics
q: In which year was the National Development Council (NDC) established?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Polity
q: Which of the following statements about the President of India is NOT true?

(B) Value of vote of an MLA = (State Population / Total Elected MLAs) ÷ 1000
(C) Article 52 vests executive power, whereas Article 53 says there shall be a President (reversed articles)
(D) The President holds office for 5 years
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Article 52 vests executive power, whereas Article 53 says there shall be a President (reversed articles)
exp: (C) Reversed Articles 52 and 53 — Article 52 states 'There shall be a President of India', while Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President (Set D Q15: C).

subject: History

subject: History
q: The 'Tilak Swaraj Fund' was launched to finance which of the following movements?

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which year was the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha founded?

subject: History

options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: History
q: The famous 'Komagata Maru' incident (1914) is associated with immigrants travelling to which country?

subject: History

Moreh is not a Pass but a gateway in Manipur. Tuirial is not a Pass but a river in Mizoram.'

subject: Economics
q: What was the primary objective behind introducing the Green Revolution in India during the 1960s?
options: (B) Ensuring self-sufficiency in foodgrains (खाद्यान्नों में आत्मनिर्भरता)

exp: (B) Ensuring self-sufficiency in foodgrains — Introduced using HYV seeds, irrigation, and fertilizers to achieve national food security (Set D Q41: B).

subject: Geography
q: Among the primary sources of water resources in India, which source contributes the most?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Rainwater — Official BPSC Final Answer Key Remark (Set A Q68 / Set D Q43: D): 'Rainwater. Reason: The Ground water has a small role in North India and no role in Deccan Plateau.'

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following soils is rich in Iron and Aluminium oxides and is formed in regions of high temperature and heavy rainfall (via intense leaching)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Laterite soil — Intense tropical leaching washes away silica and lime, leaving behind iron and aluminium oxides in Laterite soil (Set D Q44: C).

subject: Environment
q: Which of the following regions in India fall under recognised global Biodiversity Hotspots?
options: (C) Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands)
exp: (C) Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland — India hosts parts of four global biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland (Set D Q45: C).

subject: Biology
q: Ribosomes in a cell are the centres/sites of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Protein synthesis — Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptide chains and are known as the protein factories of the cell (Set D Q46: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: Plastics which when moulded once cannot be softened again by heating are called:
options: (C) Thermosetting plastics (such as Bakelite and Melamine)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Thermosetting plastics (such as Bakelite and Melamine)
exp: (C) Thermosetting plastics — Cross-linked polymers like Bakelite and Melamine cannot be remoulded upon heating (Set D Q47: C).

subject: Chemistry
q: In polymer chemistry, what property of macromolecules can be determined using the Ultracentrifuge method (developed by Svedberg)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Molecular mass / Molecular weight — Sedimentation velocity/equilibrium in an ultracentrifuge determines the weight-average molar mass of polymers and proteins (Set D Q48: B).

subject: Physics
q: Hydraulic brakes used in automobiles are a direct application of:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Pascal's law — Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions (Set D Q49: D).

subject: Physics
q: Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics (1921) for:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Explanation of the Photoelectric Effect — Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect (Set D Q50: C).

subject: Physics
q: A solid piece of iron sinks in water but floats in mercury because:
options: (B) The density of iron (~7.8 g/cm³) is greater than that of water (1 g/cm³) but less than that of mercury (13.6 g/cm³)
(D) Surface tension of water is zero
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) The density of iron (~7.8 g/cm³) is greater than that of water (1 g/cm³) but less than that of mercury (13.6 g/cm³)
exp: (B) The density of iron is greater than that of water but less than that of mercury — By Archimedes' principle, a body sinks in a fluid of lower density and floats in a fluid of higher density (Set D Q52: B).

subject: Biology
q: Which was the first human hormone produced by Genetic Engineering (recombinant DNA technology)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Insulin — Human insulin (Humulin) was synthesised in 1978/1982 using genetically engineered E. coli bacteria (Set D Q53: B).

subject: Physics
q: Assertion (A): Lasers are used to measure distances to distant objects like the Moon (Lunar Laser Ranging). Reason (R): Lasers are highly coherent, monochromatic, and unidirectional sources of light.
options: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(D) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
exp: (C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A) — High spatial and temporal coherence allows laser beams to travel to the Moon and back without spreading out excessively (Set D Q54: C).

subject: Geography
q: The Mohorovičić Discontinuity (Moho discontinuity) marks the boundary between which two layers of the Earth's interior?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (D) Lower Crust and Upper Mantle — The Moho discontinuity separates the Earth's crust from the underlying upper mantle (Set D Q55: D).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following ions is isoelectronic with Mg2+ (10 electrons)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) F- (Fluoride ion) — Mg2+ (Z=12, 12-2=10 e-) and F- (Z=9, 9+1=10 e-) both have 10 electrons and are isoelectronic (Set D Q56: A).

subject: Chemistry
q: A pi (π) bond is formed by which type of orbital overlap?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) Lateral (sideways) p–p orbital overlap — Sideways (parallel) overlap of p orbitals perpendicular to the internuclear axis forms a π bond (Set D Q57: C).

subject: Chemistry
q:
Consider the following statements regarding Aqua Regia:
1. It is a mixture of 3 parts concentrated HNO3 and 1 part concentrated HCl.
2. It can dissolve noble metals like Gold (Au) and Platinum (Pt).
3. Nitrosyl chloride (NOCl) and Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) give Aqua Regia its yellow-orange fuming colour. Which statements are correct?

exp: (C) 2 and 3 only — Statement 1 is false because Aqua Regia is 1 part conc. HNO3 and 3 parts conc. HCl (1:3, not 3:1); Statements 2 and 3 are true (Set D Q58: C).

subject: Chemistry

options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above

subject: Chemistry
q: Drugs used for the treatment of stress, tension, and anxiety are called:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (B) Tranquilizers — Tranquilizers act on the central nervous system to relieve anxiety, stress, and mild or severe mental diseases (Set D Q60: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: How can Free Radical Intermediates (which possess unpaired electrons) be easily detected and studied?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (C) ESR (Electron Spin Resonance) Spectroscopy — Free radicals are paramagnetic (have an unpaired electron) and give characteristic signals in ESR/EPR spectroscopy (Set D Q61: C).

subject: Chemistry
q: When an egg is hard-boiled, the liquid egg white turns into a solid mass. What thermodynamic change occurs in the protein molecules?
options: (D) Increase in disorder (entropy ΔS > 0 due to uncoiling/denaturation of globular proteins)
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) Increase in disorder (entropy ΔS > 0 due to uncoiling/denaturation of globular proteins)
exp: (D) Increase in disorder (entropy) — Boiling denatures coiled globular albumin proteins into uncoiled random polypeptide chains, increasing molecular disorder/entropy (Set D Q62: D).

subject: Chemistry
q: According to the Arrhenius theory, the rate constant (k) of a chemical reaction depends on:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: (A) Temperature — By k = A·e^(-Ea/RT), the rate constant varies exponentially with absolute temperature T (Set D Q63: A).

subject: Physics
q: What is an Alpha (α) particle in reality?
options: (B) A doubly ionised Helium nucleus (He2+) containing 2 protons and 2 neutrons
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) A doubly ionised Helium nucleus (He2+) containing 2 protons and 2 neutrons
exp: (B) A doubly ionised Helium nucleus (He2+) — An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus stripped of both electrons (Set D Q64: B).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following organic molecules is NOT bicyclic (i.e., is monocyclic or acyclic)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
