exp: Section III Bihar Proverbs: (#9) Everyone stands with you in prosperity, none in adversity; (#10) One cannot knowingly swallow a live fly / commit a blatant wrong; (#11) Boasting beyond one's modest roots; (#12) As you sow, so shall you reap.

subject: History
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 1, Section I — 114 Marks] Q1 Short notes: (a) Indian Councils Act, 1861; (b) Role of Bihar in Quit India Movement; (c) Santhal uprising; (d) Patna Kalam painting; (e) Mauryan Art and Architecture. Q2: Champaran Indigo Movement & its impacts OR British policy & emergence of Indian National Movement. Q3: Expansion of Western Education in Bihar from mid-19th century OR Constructive works of Mahatma Gandhi.
exp: Covers Lord Canning's portfolio system (1861), Patna Secretariat Firing (11 Aug 1942) & Azad Dasta, Santhal Hul (1855–56), Patna Kalam artists (Sewak Ram, Hulas Lal, Ishwari Prasad Verma), and Champaran Agrarian Act 1918.

subject: Current Affairs
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 1, Section II — 114 Marks] Q4: (a) Opposition coalition politics after Delhi Assembly Elections 2025; (b) Three years of Russia-Ukraine war; (c) Prayagraj Maha Kumbh Fair (13 Jan – 26 Feb 2025) as symbol of Indian culture & harmony; (d) Need and importance of caste-based Census in Bihar; (e) Future of USA under President Donald Trump. Q5: Uttarakhand Uniform Civil Code (UCC) OR President's Rule in Manipur. Q6: 'One Nation, One Election' OR Women's Reservation Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Act).
ansText: Descriptive Current Affairs & Polity Section (114 Marks)
exp: Covers Prayagraj Maha Kumbh 2025, Bihar Caste-based Survey (2023) & Rs 2 lakh assistance scheme for 94 lakh poor families, Uttarakhand UCC implementation (Jan 2025), President's Rule in Manipur (Feb 2025), Kovind Committee on simultaneous elections, and 106th Amendment Act (2023).

subject: Mathematics
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 1, Section III Data Interpretation — 72 Marks] Q7: State-wise competitive exam selection table (1994–2000) OR Crop production bar diagram of paddy, wheat, and maize (2002–2005). Q8: Family A & B monthly expenditure pie charts OR Company X, Y, Z export line graph (1993–1999).
ansText: Q7(B) Exact Answers: Ratio = 273:208:132 | Maize % = 21.53% | Avg Wheat/Paddy = 76.19% | Maize increase = 3.41%
exp: In Q7(B), total production over 2002–2005 is Paddy = 273 tons, Wheat = 208 tons, and Maize = 132 tons (Total = 613 tons).

subject: Polity
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 2, Section I — 114 Marks] Q1: (a) Article 32 as 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'; (b) Criminalisation of politics in Bihar; (c) Caste as a political phenomenon; (d) Collegium system & criticisms; (e) 73rd/74th Amendments & women empowerment at grassroot level in Bihar. Q2: Evolution of Political Parties to Coalition era OR Role and discretion of Governor. Q3: Political impact of linguistic identity OR Constitutional changes in J&K after abrogation of Article 370.
exp: Covers Bihar Panchayati Raj Act 2006 (50% reservation for women in PRIs), Three Judges Cases & NJAC (2015), B.P. Singhal v. Union of India (2010) on Governor tenure, and SC's December 2023 judgment upholding Article 370 abrogation.

subject: Geography
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 2, Section II — 114 Marks] Q4: (a) Mechanism of winter rainfall in India; (b) Mangrove forest benefits; (c) Geographical conditions for millets; (d) Ecological conditions for Makhana (Fox nut) crop & Govt measures; (e) Automobile industry in 4 largest metro regions. Q5: Mineral richness of Peninsular India OR Alluvial vs. Diluvial soils. Q6: Out-migration from Bihar & stabilization measures OR Solar energy benefits in India.
exp: Covers Western Disturbances & NE Monsoon winter rain, MISHTI mangrove scheme, Shree Anna (millets), Mithila Makhana (stagnant 1–1.5m water bodies, 20–35°C, GI tag, National Makhana Board in Budget 2025–26), and Bihar migration stabilization.

subject: Biology
q: [70th Mains GS Paper 2, Section III Science & Tech — 72 Marks] Q7: (a) S&T in agricultural productivity & food preservation; (b) Cyber crime types & mitigation; (c) S&T from cancer treatment to ticket booking; (d) DNA fingerprinting in forensic science; (e) STEM education for Bihar workforce; (f) Drone technology in national security. Q8: Chandrayaan & Mangalyaan milestones and applications in agriculture/disaster/urban planning OR WiFi technology in economy and higher education.
exp: Covers VNTR/STR DNA profiling in forensics, ISR drones & Indrajaal counter-drone system, Chandrayaan-3 south pole landing, FASAL/NADAMS/Bhuvan space applications, and PM-WANI / BharatNet WiFi expansion.

subject: Polity
q: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was the number of Ministers in the Council of Ministers limited to 15% of the total number of members of the House of the People / Legislative Assembly?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A), capping the size of the Council of Ministers at 15% of the strength of the lower house (asked again in 70th Re-Exam Jan 2025 & LDC Sep 2025).

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which Indian city was designated by UNESCO as India's first 'City of Literature'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Kozhikode (Kerala) was declared India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature' under the Creative Cities Network (also asked in the 4 January 2025 Re-Exam).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following is an iron ore?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Limonite (FeO(OH)·nH₂O) is one of the four principal iron ores alongside hematite, magnetite, and siderite.

subject: Geography
q: Which type of rock is formed from cooling and solidification of lava?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Igneous rocks form directly through the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava.

subject: Polity
q: What is the object of 'cut motion' in Parliament?
options: (A) To restrict day-to-day financial expenditure of the government
(B) To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the budget proposals
(C) To restrict the grants of the Government
(D) To restrict grants from Consolidated Fund of India
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the budget proposals
exp: A cut motion is a special power vested in Lok Sabha members to move a proposal to reduce the amount of a demand for grant in the Union Budget.

subject: History
q: When did the Britishers shift the capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Announced by King George V at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911, the capital formally shifted to Delhi in 1912 under Lord Hardinge II.

subject: Polity
q: What is the position of representation of Anglo-Indian Community in Lok Sabha?
options: (A) Two Anglo-Indians are nominated by the President
(B) Nomination of them has been done away with by 104th Constitutional Amendment
(C) One Anglo-Indian is nominated by the President
(D) They are nominated as per their population
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Nomination of them has been done away with by 104th Constitutional Amendment
exp: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Where was the 13th Ministerial Conference of World Trade Organization (WTO) held in February 2024?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) was held in Abu Dhabi, UAE from 26 February to 2 March 2024.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who won the Men's Singles title at the French Open Tennis Tournament 2024?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Carlos Alcaraz of Spain defeated Alexander Zverev in five sets to win the 2024 Roland Garros Men's Singles title.

subject: Polity
q: What is the eligibility age, after the changes made in March 2024, for senior citizens to vote by postal ballot?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: In March 2024, the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 were amended raising the qualifying age for senior citizen postal ballots from 80 to 85 years.

subject: Economics
q: In the Union Budget speech for 2024-25, which oilseed was NOT covered under the goal of 'Atmanirbharta' (self-reliance) for oilseeds?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Union Budget 2024-25 targeted Atmanirbharta in five oilseeds: mustard, groundnut, sesame, soybean, and sunflower (excluding coconut).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Copper is more reactive than silver and displaces Ag from AgNO₃ solution (Cu + 2AgNO₃ -> Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag).

subject: Bihar Special
q: Bihula Festival is celebrated especially in which district of Bihar usually in the month of August each year?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bihula-Bishari is the major folk festival of the Anga region (Bhagalpur district) dedicated to Goddess Mansa and Behula.

subject: Physics
q: Heat transfer that does not require a medium is called:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Thermal radiation transfers heat via electromagnetic waves and requires no material medium.

subject: Biology
q: Which of the following acids is secreted in the human stomach?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Parietal (oxyntic) cells in the gastric mucosa secrete hydrochloric acid (HCl) to activate pepsinogen.

subject: History
q: Ramakrishna Mission was founded by:
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Swami Vivekananda established the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 at Belur Math near Kolkata to carry out social welfare, disaster relief, medical philanthropy, and dissemination of the spiritual teachings of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.

subject: Bihar Special
q: In which city of Bihar is the recently inaugurated National Dolphin Research Centre (NDRC) located?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: India's first National Dolphin Research Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 on the Patna University campus along the Ganga in Patna.

subject: Polity
q: Which Article of the Constitution restricts a Member of Parliament from holding an office of profit?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Article 102(1)(a) disqualifies an MP from holding any office of profit under the Union or State Government.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which country became the first to bring soil samples from the far (dark) side of the Moon in June 2024?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: China's Chang'e-6 mission returned 1,935.3 grams of lunar samples from the Moon's far side in June 2024.

subject: Geography
q:
Following are the mountain ranges/peaks of India:
1. Garo Hills,
2. Nanda Devi,
3. Kamet,
4. K2. What is their correct sequence from East to West?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: From East to West: Garo Hills (~90°E) -> Nanda Devi (~79°58'E) -> Kamet (~79°35'E) -> K2 (~76°30'E).

subject: Polity
q: Who among the following served as Speaker of the Lok Sabha prior to his election as President of India?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy served twice as Speaker of the Lok Sabha before becoming the 6th President of India in 1977.

subject: History
q: Who gave the slogan 'DO OR DIE' and when?
options: (A) Subhash Chandra Bose during Quit India Movement
(D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Mahatma Gandhi gave the mantra 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro) on 8 August 1942 during the Quit India speech at Gowalia Tank Maidan.

subject: Current Affairs
q: When was the undersea cable-based Chennai–Andaman and Nicobar Islands (CANI) Project inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 2,312-km submarine optical fibre cable connecting Chennai and Port Blair (CANI) was inaugurated on 10 August 2020.

subject: History
q: Who wrote 'New Lamps for Old'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Sri Aurobindo Ghosh published the article series 'New Lamps for Old' in Indu Prakash in 1893–94 critiquing Moderate Congress mendicancy.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In which Lok Sabha constituency did members of the Shompen tribe (a PVTG) exercise their right to vote for the first time in April 2024?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Seven members of the Shompen PVTG of Great Nicobar voted for the first time in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands constituency in April 2024.

subject: Current Affairs
q: After remaining neutral for almost 200 years, which country officially joined NATO in March 2024?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: After maintaining military non-alignment and neutrality for more than two centuries, Sweden officially became the 32nd member of NATO in March 2024 following security recalibrations in Northern Europe.

subject: Physics
q: The meter used to measure the total distance moved by a vehicle is known as:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: An odometer records total distance travelled, whereas a speedometer measures instantaneous speed.

subject: History
q: When did the Muslim League observe 'Direct Action Day'?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The All-India Muslim League Council, headed by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, observed 'Direct Action Day' on 16 August 1946 to enforce its demand for Pakistan, leading to communal riots known as the 'Great Calcutta Killings'.

subject: Economics
q: What was the global rank of India in the manufacturing of mobile phones in 2023?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Backed by the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, phased manufacturing policy, and large-scale electronics manufacturing clusters, India emerged as the world's second-largest mobile phone manufacturer after China, producing hundreds of millions of smartphone units annually.

subject: Polity
q: Which two words among the following were incorporated into the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

subject: Chemistry
q: Who was the first scientist to propose a structural model for the atom?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: J.J. Thomson proposed the first scientific structural model of the atom in 1904 (the 'Plum Pudding' or watermelon model), depicting the atom as a sphere of positive electric charge with negatively charged electrons embedded within it.

subject: Economics
q: According to the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) data from MoSPI, which use-based indices experienced significant growth in FY 2023?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Capital goods and infrastructure/construction goods led IIP growth on the back of government infrastructure capex.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In April 2024, how many members of the UN Security Council either rejected or abstained from voting on the resolution to admit Palestine as a full UN member?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Out of 15 UNSC members, 12 voted in favour, 1 voted against (USA), and 2 abstained (UK and Switzerland), making 3 in total.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Which statement about Ruchira Kamboj, the first woman Indian Permanent Representative to the UN who retired in 2024, is true?
options: (D) She held the position of Permanent Representative of India to UNESCO, Paris
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (D) She held the position of Permanent Representative of India to UNESCO, Paris
exp: Ruchira Kamboj served as Permanent Representative of India to UNESCO in Paris (2014–2017) prior to her UN New York posting.

subject: Chemistry
q: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained: i. Law of conservation of mass, ii. Law of constant composition, iii. Law of radioactivity, iv. Law of multiple proportions.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Dalton's theory explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportions, and multiple proportions, but not radioactivity.

subject: Polity
q: Under Article 243J of the Constitution, who may by law make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Article 243J empowers the Legislature of a State to make laws regarding maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts.

subject: Environment
q: What is the full form of PCRA?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: PCRA stands for Petroleum Conservation Research Association (under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas).

subject: Polity
q: Who decides the disqualification of members of a State Legislative Assembly for matters other than those in the Tenth Schedule?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Under Article 192, the Governor decides non-Tenth Schedule disqualifications in accordance with the opinion of the Election Commission.

subject: Biology
q: Which bacterial disease is also called 'splenic fever'?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Anthrax (caused by Bacillus anthracis) is known as splenic fever due to acute enlargement of the spleen.

subject: Geography
q: Which one of the following rivers is different from the others in drainage direction?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea, whereas Tungabhadra, Mahanadi, and Penganga belong to east-flowing Bay of Bengal river systems.

subject: History
q: Who was the founder of the Faraizi Movement?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in eastern Bengal in 1818, urging Muslims to abandon un-Islamic cultural practices, observe fundamental Islamic duties (Fara'iz), and resist oppression by British planters and Zamindars.

subject: Economics
q: According to a CRISIL Ratings report, how much is India's corporate bond market expected to grow to by Financial Year 2030?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: CRISIL projected India's corporate bond market to double from ~₹43 lakh crore to ₹100–120 lakh crore by FY30.

subject: History
q:
Match the Political Organisation with its Founder:
I. Khaksars,
II. Congress Socialist Party,
III. Independent Labour Party,
IV. Forward Bloc with a. Subhash Chandra Bose, b. Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi, c. Jayaprakash Narayan, d. B. R. Ambedkar.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Khaksars (Mashriqi, 1931), CSP (JP Narayan, 1934), ILP (Ambedkar, 1936), and Forward Bloc (Bose, 1939).

subject: Bihar Special
q: Shreyasi Singh, MLA who represented India in shooting at the Paris Olympics 2024, was elected from which Assembly constituency in Bihar?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Shreyasi Singh, international trap shooting champion and Commonwealth Games gold medalist who represented India at the 2024 Paris Olympics, was elected as Member of the Bihar Legislative Assembly representing the Jamui assembly constituency.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Before his elevation as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India in July 2024, Justice N. Kotiswar Singh served as the Chief Justice of which High Court?
options: (B) Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
ansText: (B) Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
exp: Justice N. Kotiswar Singh served as Chief Justice of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh until July 2024.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which of the following districts of Bihar has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe (ST) population among the given options as per Census 2011?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Among the four options, Katihar has the highest ST share at 5.86% (overall in Bihar, West Champaran is highest at 6.35%).

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following are exothermic processes? i. Evaporation of water, ii. Dilution of an acid (H₂SO₄), iii. Reaction of water with quicklime, iv. Sublimation of camphor.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Dilution of concentrated acid and slaking of quicklime release heat (exothermic), while evaporation and sublimation are endothermic.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Match List-I (District of Bihar) with List-II (Product/Industry): a. Vaishali, b. Bhagalpur, c. Jamui, d. Madhepura with
1. Silk Textile,
2. Gold,
3. Rail Coach/Locomotive Factory,
4. Floriculture.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Vaishali (Floriculture, 4), Bhagalpur (Silk, 1), Jamui (Gold, 2), and Madhepura (Electric Locomotive Factory, 3).

subject: Polity
q: Within what time limit does a Governor have to return an Ordinary Bill to the State Legislature for reconsideration under Article 200?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Article 200 specifies 'as soon as possible' but prescribes no fixed numerical time limit.

subject: History
q: Which ruler ruled Kamarupa (Assam) during the time of Emperor Harshavardhana?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty was the ruler of Kamarupa and ally of Harshavardhana.

subject: History
q: Who headed the Royal Commission on Indian Finance and Currency appointed in 1913?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Sir Austen Chamberlain chaired the 1913 Royal Commission on Indian Finance and Currency (of which J. M. Keynes was a member).

subject: Current Affairs
q: In which Freestyle weight category did Aman Sehrawat qualify for and win a medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Aman Sehrawat competed in the Men's 57 kg Freestyle category and won a bronze medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Who was the President of the 27th Indian National Congress Session held at Bankipore (Patna) in 1912?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Rao Bahadur R. N. Mudholkar presided over the 1912 Bankipore (Patna) Congress Session.

subject: Reasoning
q: Gaurav walks 20 m North, turns left and walks 40 m, turns left and walks 20 m, then turns right and walks 20 m. How far is he from his original position?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: North 20 m and South 20 m cancel vertically; West 40 m + West 20 m = 60 metres from the starting point.

subject: Economics
q: What were the shares of Agriculture, Industry, and Services in overall GVA at current prices in FY24 per Economic Survey 2023-24?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Per Economic Survey 2023-24, sectoral GVA shares in FY24 were Agriculture 17.7%, Industry 27.6%, and Services 54.7%.

subject: Chemistry
q: Corundum and Cryolite are important ores of which metal?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Corundum (crystalline Al₂O₃) and Cryolite (Sodium hexafluoroaluminate, Na₃AlF₆) are essential minerals of Aluminium, with cryolite used as a flux to lower the melting point of alumina in the Hall-Héroult electrolytic extraction process.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following represents the suitable condition for the liquefaction of gases?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to Le Chatelier's principle, an exothermic reaction accompanied by a decrease in gaseous moles is favoured by low temperature and high pressure to maximize equilibrium product yield.

subject: Polity
q: The Indian National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Constituent Assembly of India officially adopted the National Flag (the Tricolour with the 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra, designed by Pingali Venkayya) on 22 July 1947, just weeks before independence.

subject: History
q: During the Quit India Movement, parallel 'National Governments' were established at several places. Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Prati Sarkar (Satara), Jatiya Sarkar (Tamluk), and Talcher Praja Mandal were 1942 parallel governments; 'Raiyati Sarkar — Kheda' is incorrect.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which temple complex in Bihar was announced in Union Budget 2024-25 to be developed on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: The Vishnupad Temple Corridor in Gaya and Mahabodhi Temple Corridor in Bodh Gaya were announced in Union Budget 2024-25.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who became the first Indian mountaineer to scale Mount Everest and Mount Lhotse twice in a single season (May 2024)?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Satyadeep Gupta scaled both Mt. Everest and Mt. Lhotse twice in the May 2024 climbing season.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following Indian ports is an artificial port?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Chennai is an artificial all-weather harbour on the east coast, whereas Mumbai, Mormugao, and Kochi are natural harbours.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The nationalist book 'Gharib Hindustan', banned in Bihar in 1930 by the British, was written by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Mohammad Wali Hassan of Patna wrote 'Gharib Hindustan', which was proscribed by the colonial government in 1930.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following was the first artificially prepared chemical element?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Technetium (Z = 43) was synthesized in 1937 by Perrier and Segrè as the first man-made element.

subject: Bihar Special
q: When did the Bihar Government introduce the 'Green Budget' for the first time?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bihar became India's first state to table a separate Green Budget in Financial Year 2020-21.

subject: History
q:
Match the Maratha Ashtapradhan officials with their departments: a. Sachiv, b. Peshwa, c. Sumant, d. Amatya with
1. Prime Minister,
2. Royal Correspondence,
3. Finance Minister,
4. Foreign Minister.
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Sachiv (Correspondence, 2), Peshwa (PM, 1), Sumant/Dabir (Foreign Affairs, 4), and Amatya/Mazumdar (Finance, 3).

subject: History
q: In October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose set up the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind), which was recognized by how many Axis-aligned countries including Japan?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Nine countries (Japan, Germany, Italy, Croatia, Burma, Thailand, Philippines, Manchukuo, and Nanjing China) recognized the Azad Hind government.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which ruler founded the Haryanka Dynasty in ancient Magadha (Bihar)?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Bimbisara (c. 544–492 BCE) founded the Haryanka dynasty with its capital at Rajagriha.

subject: Reasoning
q: If February 1, 1996 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was March 3, 1996?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: 1996 is a leap year (Feb has 29 days). Elapsed days = 28 + 3 = 31 ≡ 3 (mod 7). Wednesday + 3 days = Saturday.

subject: Economics
q: By how much did India's Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR) increase from 2017-18 to 2022-23 according to NSSO PLFS?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: According to the official Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) annual reports published by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), India's Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR) in usual status expanded significantly from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 37.0% in 2022-23.

subject: Bihar Special
q: 'History of the Indian National Congress in Bihar (1885–1985)' (Hundred Years of INC in Bihar) was edited by:
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: Dr. P. N. Ojha edited the centenary volumes published by the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Patna in 1985.

subject: Bihar Special

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is a cause of rural to urban migration in India ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: D. All the above. An inclusive-set option is right only when every item listed survives on its own, and here none is false. High labour demand in cities is the textbook pull factor: construction, small manufacturing, transport and personal services absorb unskilled labour at wages well above the prevailing rural agricultural wage. That wage gap is central to both Everett Lee's 1966 push–pull framework and the Lewis two-sector model of surplus labour transfer.

subject: General Studies
q: In which organisms does spore formation occur as a mode of reproduction ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Fungi. In school biology, spore formation is a named mode of asexual reproduction, and it is taught with a fungus: Rhizopus, the black bread mould. An upright hypha carries a swollen sporangium that matures and bursts, and the scattered spores germinate into new mycelia wherever they meet moisture and food. The thick-walled spores travel on air currents, which is why uncovered bread grows mould without anyone introducing it. The option set points the same way.

subject: General Studies
q: Motorcycle is related to battery in the same way as Life is related to
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. Sun. Begin by putting the first pair into a full sentence, because a vague relationship is what makes analogies feel arbitrary. A battery is the source of the energy that a motorcycle runs on: it turns the starter, fires the ignition and powers the lights and horn, and without it the machine will not come alive. So the relationship is 'X is powered by its source of energy Y'. Substitute the second pair and ask what supplies the energy that life runs on. The answer is the Sun.

subject: General Studies
q: Choose the group of letters which is different from others.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. PSVX. Convert every letter to its position in the alphabet and the question answers itself. Option (b) ORUX is O = 15, R = 18, U = 21, X = 24, so the steps are +3, +3, +3. Option (c) JMPS is J = 10, M = 13, P = 16, S = 19: again +3, +3, +3. Option (d) CFIL is C = 3, F = 6, I = 9, L = 12: +3, +3, +3 once more. Option (a) PSVX is P = 16, S = 19, V = 22, X = 24, and its steps are +3, +3, +2.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following cities is located along the side of river Seine ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Paris. The Seine rises on the Langres plateau in Burgundy, runs about 777 kilometres north-westward across the Paris basin through Troyes, Paris and Rouen, and empties into the English Channel at Le Havre. Paris was founded on the Île de la Cité, an island in the river, and the Seine still divides the city into a Right Bank and a Left Bank.

subject: General Studies
q: If ÷ means +, – means ÷, × means – and + means ×, then the value of ((36 × 4) – 8 × 4) / (4 + 8 × 2 + 16 ÷ 1) is
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. 0. Write the substitution table out before touching the expression, because every error in this kind of question comes from doing the replacement in your head: ÷ becomes +, – becomes ÷, × becomes −, and + becomes ×. The long slash that separates the two brackets is the fraction bar of the expression itself, not one of the four redefined symbols, so it stays as an ordinary division. Now translate the numerator. (36 × 4) – 8 × 4 becomes (36 − 4) ÷ 8 − 4. Work the bracket first: 36 − 4 = 32.

subject: General Studies
q: Which one of the following is an example of melamine used for making floor tiles ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. Thermo setting plastic. Plastics divide into two families by what heat does to them once moulded. A thermoplastic has long polymer chains with only weak forces between them; heat lets the chains slide, so it softens, can be reshaped, and hardens again on cooling, repeatedly. A thermosetting plastic cross-links during moulding into a single three-dimensional network held by covalent bonds, and heat cannot undo it: the article can only char or burn, never be remelted.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is a technopolis ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Silicon valley. A technopolis, or technopole, is not simply a big city with computers: economic geography uses the term for a planned or deliberately nurtured concentration of high-technology research and production, built around universities and research institutes, where firms, laboratories, venture finance and skilled labour cluster and feed one another. Silicon Valley is the textbook case, widely described as the world's leading technopole.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is a zaid crop ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Fodder. India's cropping calendar has three seasons, and zaid is the short summer one between them, roughly March to June, after the rabi harvest and before the monsoon starts the kharif sowing. With no rain in that window, a zaid crop needs irrigation and must mature quickly. The standard zaid list in the NCERT geography textbook is watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops, and fodder is the only item from it among these options.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is the fluid part of the blood ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Plasma. Blood is a fluid connective tissue, and like every connective tissue it has a matrix in which cells sit. In blood that matrix is liquid, and the liquid is plasma. Spin a sample in a centrifuge and it separates cleanly: about 55 per cent of the volume is a straw-coloured plasma layer on top, about 45 per cent is a packed red column of cells below, with a thin greyish buffy coat of white cells and platelets between. Plasma is roughly 90 to 92 per cent water.

subject: General Studies
q: How many triangles are there in the following figure PQRS ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. 12. Read the printed figure precisely first, because the whole question turns on how far the two extra lines run. Rectangle PQRS has both diagonals PR and QS, crossing at the centre O. A horizontal segment runs from M, the midpoint of the left side PS, rightward to O and stops there. A vertical segment runs from O downward to N, the midpoint of the bottom side SR, and stops there.

subject: General Studies
q: Name the place where Donald Trump was speaking at an election rally when an alleged Shooter, Thomas Matthew Crooks, shot and injured him.
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Pennsylvania. The shooting took place on 13 July 2024 at an open-air campaign rally on the Butler Farm Show grounds, near the town of Butler in western Pennsylvania. Thomas Matthew Crooks, a 20-year-old from Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, fired from the roof of an AGR International warehouse between about 120 and 140 metres north of the stage, minutes after Trump began speaking. One round grazed the upper part of Trump's right ear; Secret Service agents pulled him down and he left the stage with a raised fist.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following radiation is used to get relief from body aches ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Infra-red radiation. Infrared lies just beyond the red end of visible light, from roughly 700 nanometres to about a millimetre in wavelength, and biological tissue absorbs it and converts it directly into heat. An infrared lamp aimed at a shoulder or knee warms the tissue a few millimetres below the skin. Local blood vessels dilate, blood flow rises, muscle tone relaxes and pain falls. That is the basis of the physiotherapy infrared lamp; a heat pad or hot-water bottle is the same therapy by contact.

subject: General Studies
q: The Andes extends along which of the following ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. West Coast of South America. The Andes run for roughly 7,000 kilometres down the whole Pacific margin of South America, through Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina: the longest continental mountain range on Earth. They exist because the oceanic Nazca Plate is being subducted eastwards beneath the continental South American Plate.

subject: General Studies
q: What is the structural and functional unit of life ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Cell. The phrase in the stem is the standard wording of the second tenet of cell theory, and its two words do different work. STRUCTURAL means every living body is built of cells and of nothing smaller that is itself alive: a bacterium is one cell, a human being some tens of trillions.

subject: General Studies
q: What is the name of the one month long cattle fair organized at the confluence of Ganga and Gandak rivers ?
options: (D) More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Sonepur Mela. The Gandak rises in Nepal as the Kali Gandaki, becomes the Narayani and enters India as the Gandak. It runs some 300 km southeast across the Bihar plain, through West Champaran, Gopalganj, East Champaran, Saran, Muzaffarpur and Vaishali, and empties into the Ganga at Sonpur, opposite Patna.

subject: General Studies
q: Which component of fertilizer is used for stimulating early growth purpose ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. Phosphorus. In the standard NPK division of labour, phosphorus owns root establishment, seedling vigour and early maturity, and the reason is biochemical. Phosphorus is part of ATP and ADP, of DNA and RNA, and of membrane phospholipids. A germinating seedling divides cells and transfers energy at maximum rate, both consuming phosphate, so a shortage at the two-to-four leaf stage stunts it permanently. The second reason is physical.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following the chlorophyll in photosynthesis is used for ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. Absorbing light. Chlorophyll is a pigment, and NCERT defines pigments as 'substances that have an ability to absorb light, at specific wavelengths.' Chlorophyll a is 'the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis': its absorption spectrum peaks in the blue and the red, the same wavelengths at which the action spectrum of photosynthesis peaks. Green light is largely reflected, which is why leaves look green.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following human races inhabitates in China, Mangolia and Japan ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: D. Mongoloid. In the classical racial classification still printed in school geography and anthropology syllabi, the peoples of East and North-East Asia (China, Mongolia, Japan, Korea and Siberia) are grouped as the Mongoloid stock, named after Mongolia itself, so the stem nearly answers itself. The older texts list the group's traits as the epicanthic fold, high cheekbones, a flat facial profile, straight coarse black hair, sparse body and facial hair, yellowish-brown skin and medium stature.

subject: General Studies
q: The political strategy Struggle -Truce - Struggle or S-T-S came into prominence with a call for
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. Khilafat issue. Struggle–Truce–Struggle is Bipan Chandra's name for the Gandhian strategy, defined in India's Struggle for Independence as 'a phase of vigorous extra-legal mass movement and open confrontation with colonial authority' followed by a phase in which confrontation is withdrawn and concessions are worked and 'shown to be inadequate', gathering forces 'for another mass movement at a higher level.

subject: General Studies
q: According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), what is the forecast for headline inflation in Financial Year 2025 ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: C. 4.5%. The Monetary Policy Committee's resolution of 5 April 2024, the year's first policy, says: 'assuming a normal monsoon, CPI inflation for 2024-25 is projected at 4.5 per cent with Q1 at 4.9 per cent; Q2 at 3.8 per cent; Q3 at 4.6 per cent; and Q4 at 4.5 per cent.' RBI's mandate is CPI inflation of 4 per cent within a band of plus or minus 2 per cent, so 4.5 meant inflation inside the band but above target; the Committee held the rate, staying 'focused on withdrawal of accommodation'.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following was not one of the features of the Government of India Act, 1935 ?
options: (B) Reconstruction of the Governor-General’s Executive Council
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: D. Appraisal of the Act of 1935. The decisive point is a category distinction: an appraisal is a judgement passed on the Act, not a provision contained in it. Every other option names something the statute did or proposed to do; this one names what historians and politicians said about it afterwards. The options read like a textbook chapter's sub-headings, with the evaluative section listed last.

subject: General Studies
q: Which part of alimentary canal receives bile from the liver ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: D. Small intestine. NCERT's Class 10 chapter on Life Processes says: 'The small intestine is the site of the complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. It receives the secretions of the liver and pancreas for this purpose.' Bile made in the liver is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder and delivered through the common bile duct into the duodenum, the first and shortest part of the small intestine, where the pancreatic duct also opens. Bile does two jobs there.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following has highly elongated elliptical orbit ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Comet. An orbit's stretch is measured by its eccentricity: 0 is a perfect circle and 1 a parabola. Earth's is about 0.017; Halley's Comet's is 0.967. Halley comes in to 0.59 astronomical units at perihelion, closer to the Sun than Venus, and swings out to 35.14 au at aphelion, roughly Pluto's distance, over 74 to 80 years. The elongation explains how a comet behaves.

subject: General Studies
q: In which of the following states of India has major reserves of coal ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: D. All the above. The Ministry of Coal's state-wise inventory as on 1 April 2023 (billion tonnes) puts Odisha first at 100.99, Jharkhand second at 93.25 and Chhattisgarh third at 85.26, against a national total of 378.21. Together the three hold 279.50 billion tonnes, close to 74 per cent of India's coal resources. No fourth state comes near: West Bengal has 34.39, Madhya Pradesh 33.56 and Telangana 23.29. Each named state qualifies on its own, so only All the above does not understate the position.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is a major cause of air pollution ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Burning of fossil fuels. Combustion of coal, petroleum products and natural gas in power stations, vehicles, industrial boilers, brick kilns and household stoves is the single largest human source of air pollution, and the only option whose primary output goes straight into the atmosphere. A flame emits sulphur dioxide from the sulphur in coal and diesel, oxides of nitrogen formed at high flame temperatures, carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons from incomplete combustion, and the fine particulate matter (PM2.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following drainage systems drains the lands of Bihar ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: B. Ghagra. The Ghaghara rises in the Mapchachungo glaciers of Tibet at about 3,962 metres, where it is called the Mapcha Tsangpo. It runs 507 km through Nepal as the Karnali, that country's longest river, then crosses eastern Uttar Pradesh, where its lower course through Awadh is the Sarayu of Ayodhya. It joins the Ganga at Revelganj, a little upstream of Chhapra in Saran district, Bihar. About 1,080 km long, it is the Ganga's largest tributary by volume of water and its second longest after the Yamuna.

subject: General Studies
q: Which of the following is a non-contact force ?
options: (E) None of the above / More than one of the above
(E) None of the above / More than one of the above
exp: A. Magnetic force. A force is non-contact when two bodies influence each other across empty space, with no touching and no intervening medium required. A bar magnet lifts an iron nail before the nail reaches it, deflects a compass needle from across a table, and does both inside a vacuum, because the interaction is carried by the magnetic field around the magnet.

subject: Polity
q: Appellate Jurisdiction of Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters is
exp:
The correct answer is Limited.
Key Points
The Appellate Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in India refers to its authority to hear appeals against the judgments of lower courts such as the High Courts.
In the context of criminal matters, the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is limited as specified in the Constitution of India.
Under Article 134 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction in criminal cases involving substantial questions of law or cases where a High Court has reversed an acquittal to impose a death sentence.
Appeals in criminal cases to the Supreme Court also require certification by the High Court that the case involves a substantial legal question or has grave importance.
This ensures that only cases of significant judicial and constitutional importance are brought before the Supreme Court for adjudication.
Additional Information
Article 134 of the Indian Constitution:
This article defines the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in criminal cases.
It specifically allows appeals to the Supreme Court in cases where a High Court has reversed an acquittal and sentenced the accused to death.
It also allows appeals in cases where the High Court certifies that the case involves a substantial question of law.
Appeals with Special Leave (Article 136):
Under this provision, the Supreme Court can grant special leave to appeal in any case, including criminal matters, where it deems it necessary to address a legal or constitutional question.
This power is discretionary and allows the Court to provide justice in cases of exceptional importance.
High Court Certification:
In most criminal cases, the High Court must certify that the matter involves a substantial question of law before it can be appealed to the Supreme Court.
This certification acts as a filter to ensure that the Supreme Court does not get overburdened with ordinary criminal cases.
Death Penalty Appeals:
The Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction to hear appeals in cases where the High Court has imposed a death penalty after reversing an acquittal.
This ensures the highest level of judicial scrutiny in cases involving capital punishment.
Important Points
The appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is not unlimited. It only entertains cases that meet specific constitutional and legal criteria.
In addition to criminal matters, the Supreme Court also has appellate jurisdiction over civil cases under Article 133 of the Indian Constitution.
The Supreme Court’s jurisdiction can also extend to disputes between states or between the Union and states under its original jurisdiction (Article 131).
The limited appellate jurisdiction ensures that the Supreme Court focuses on cases with substantial constitutional or legal implications.

subject: Biology
q: In 2024, which international agreement on Artificial Intelligence was signed by over 25 countries, including the USA and UK to promote safe AI development?
exp:
The correct answer is Bletchley Declaration.
Key Points
The Bletchley Declaration was signed in 2024 by over 25 countries, including major nations such as the USA and UK, to promote the safe and ethical development of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
It aims to establish international guidelines for ethical AI research, development, and deployment, ensuring that AI technologies do not pose harm to humanity.
The declaration is named after Bletchley Park, a historic site in the UK known for its role in deciphering codes during World War II, symbolizing collaboration and innovation.
The signing of this agreement reflects the growing global recognition of the need to address challenges like AI safety, bias, privacy concerns, and misuse.
The Bletchley Declaration is considered a landmark step in fostering international cooperation to regulate and govern AI technologies effectively.
Additional Information
Ethical AI Convention:
Although the name suggests a focus on ethics, there is no formal agreement called Ethical AI Convention signed by nations in 2024.
Many organizations like UNESCO and OECD promote ethical AI guidelines, but these are not referred to as a convention.
AI Geneva Charter:
This option is fictitious as there is no international agreement or charter named AI Geneva Charter signed in 2024.
Geneva is known for hosting discussions on humanitarian issues, but this name does not correspond to any AI-related global agreement.
Global AI Framework Agreement:
While the name suggests a comprehensive framework, no such agreement was signed in 2024.
Global frameworks for AI governance are being discussed under multiple forums like the UN, but this specific name does not exist.
Bletchley Park:
Bletchley Park is a historic site in the UK, famous for the work of codebreakers during World War II.
The location was chosen for the declaration to symbolize innovation, international cooperation, and the ethical application of technology.
Important Points
Global AI Challenges:
Major concerns include data privacy, bias in algorithms, misuse for surveillance, and potential existential risks.
Global cooperation is essential to address these issues effectively.
AI Governance:
International organizations like UNESCO, OECD, and EU are actively working on creating frameworks for ethical AI use.
Many nations are drafting their own AI policies and laws while participating in global discussions.
Future Implications:
The Bletchley Declaration sets the foundation for future treaties and guidelines on AI governance.
It highlights the importance of balancing technological advancement with ethical considerations and public safety.

subject: Chemistry
q: Which of the following are present in higher amount in hard water?
exp:
The correct answer is Calcium and Magnesium.
Key Points
Hard water contains a high concentration of calcium (Ca2+) and magnesium (Mg2+) ions, which cause the water to be "hard."
These minerals are typically dissolved in water as it passes through rocks, particularly limestone, chalk, or gypsum, which are rich in calcium and magnesium carbonates and sulfates.
When hard water is heated or evaporates, the dissolved calcium and magnesium salts precipitate out, forming scale or limescale deposits.
Calcium and magnesium are the primary contributors to water hardness, and their concentrations are measured in terms of parts per million (ppm) or milligrams per liter (mg/L).
Sodium and manganese ions are not significant contributors to water hardness. Sodium is a soft water ion, while manganese is present in water in very minimal amounts compared to calcium and magnesium.
Additional Information
Types of Hardness:
Temporary Hardness: Caused by the presence of dissolved bicarbonate minerals such as calcium bicarbonate (Ca(HCO3)2) and magnesium bicarbonate (Mg(HCO3)2). It can be removed by boiling the water, which precipitates the bicarbonates as carbonates.
Permanent Hardness: Caused by the presence of sulfate or chloride compounds of calcium and magnesium. It cannot be removed by boiling and requires chemical treatment, such as using washing soda or ion-exchange resins.
Effects of Hard Water:
Hard water causes scaling in pipes, boilers, and household appliances, leading to reduced efficiency and increased maintenance costs.
It reduces the effectiveness of soap and detergent, forming scum instead of lather.
Hard water can sometimes cause skin dryness and hair damage due to the deposit of calcium and magnesium salts.
Softening Hard Water:
Temporary hardness can be removed by boiling, which breaks down bicarbonate ions into carbonates.
Permanent hardness is treated by methods such as ion-exchange resin, adding washing soda (sodium carbonate), or using commercial water softeners.
Measurement of Water Hardness:
Water hardness is usually expressed in terms of milligrams per liter (mg/L) as calcium carbonate (CaCO3).
Soft water contains less than 60 mg/L of CaCO3, while very hard water exceeds 180 mg/L.
Uses of Calcium and Magnesium:
Calcium: Used in the manufacturing of cement, glass, and steel and is essential for human bone and teeth development.
Magnesium: Used in the production of lightweight alloys, fireworks, and as a dietary supplement for maintaining muscle and nerve function.
Important Points
WHO Guidelines: The World Health Organization (WHO) does not set a mandatory limit for water hardness but suggests that water with hardness above 500 mg/L may not be suitable for drinking.
Health Impacts: While hard water is not generally harmful, excessive calcium and magnesium intake can lead to kidney stones in some individuals.
Industrial Impact: Hard water can cause scaling in machinery and industrial processes, leading to increased maintenance and operational costs.
Geographical Distribution: Hard water is commonly found in areas with high concentrations of limestone and gypsum, such as parts of the United States, India, and Europe.

subject: Economics
q: Mule Hunter. ai has been introduced by
exp:

Key Points
Mule Hunter.ai is an advanced platform introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to tackle financial fraud and cybercrime.
It is designed to detect and prevent fraudulent activities in the banking and financial sector, particularly focusing on money mule operations.
The initiative aims to enhance cyber security and reduce the risks associated with money laundering and other illegal financial transactions.
Money mules are individuals who transfer stolen money or illegally obtained funds between different accounts, often unwittingly.
This platform leverages artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for real-time monitoring and analysis of suspicious transactions.
Additional Information
Reserve Bank of India (RBI):
Established in 1935, the RBI is India's central banking institution responsible for regulating the monetary policy of the country.
The RBI plays a critical role in ensuring the stability of the financial system and promoting economic growth.
It supervises and regulates banks, manages foreign exchange, and oversees payment systems in India.
Recently, RBI has focused on enhancing cybersecurity measures to combat modern financial challenges.
It is headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
Money Mule Operations:
Money mule operations involve using individuals to transfer illicit funds between accounts to disguise the origin of the money.
These operations are often part of larger cybercrime networks and contribute to money laundering schemes.
In many cases, money mules are unaware of their involvement in illegal activities.
Detecting and preventing money mule operations is critical for safeguarding the financial system.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Banking:
AI is increasingly used in the banking sector for fraud detection, risk management, and enhancing customer experience.
It enables real-time analysis of large datasets to identify patterns of fraudulent behavior.
AI-powered tools like Mule Hunter.ai provide actionable insights to prevent financial crimes.
Other Cybersecurity Initiatives:
The RBI has launched various initiatives to strengthen cyber resilience in banks, including guidelines for data protection and cyber threat management.
Financial institutions are encouraged to adopt state-of-the-art technology solutions to mitigate cyber risks.
Collaborations with international organizations help in combating global financial fraud.
Important Points
Role of AI in Financial Security: AI can identify trends, flag anomalies, and predict fraudulent activities, making it indispensable in combating financial crimes.
Global Cyber Threats: Financial institutions worldwide face increasing cyber threats, making platforms like Mule Hunter.ai essential for risk mitigation.
Impact of Money Laundering: Money laundering undermines economic stability and trust in financial institutions, emphasizing the need for stringent measures.
RBI's Commitment: The RBI's initiatives reflect its commitment to protecting India's financial ecosystem from emerging threats.

subject: Biology
q: Glycogen is primarily stored in which organs of human beings?
exp:
The correct answer is Liver and muscles.
Key Points
Glycogen, a branched polymer of glucose, is the primary form of carbohydrate storage in humans.
It is predominantly stored in two major organs: the liver and skeletal muscles.
The liver stores glycogen to help regulate blood glucose levels. It releases glucose into the bloodstream during fasting or between meals to maintain homeostasis.
In muscles, glycogen serves as a local energy reserve and is utilized during intense physical activity for ATP production.
The liver can store approximately 100 grams of glycogen, while muscles collectively store around 300-400 grams.
Unlike muscle glycogen, which is used exclusively by muscle cells, liver glycogen can be broken down into glucose and released into the bloodstream to be used by other tissues.
Additional Information
Glycogen metabolism:
Glycogenesis: This is the process of glycogen synthesis, where glucose molecules are added to chains of glycogen for storage, primarily occurring in the liver and muscles.
Glycogenolysis: This is the breakdown of glycogen into glucose. In the liver, glycogenolysis provides glucose for the bloodstream, while in muscles, it supplies energy directly to muscle cells.
Role of hormones:
Insulin: Promotes glycogen synthesis by enhancing glucose uptake and activating glycogen synthase.
Glucagon: Stimulates glycogen breakdown in the liver during fasting to maintain blood glucose levels.
Epinephrine: Triggers glycogenolysis in both liver and muscles during stress or physical activity.
Comparison of glycogen storage in the body:
Liver: Glycogen in the liver acts as a readily available source of glucose for the entire body. It plays a critical role in maintaining blood glucose levels between meals.
Muscles: Muscle glycogen is used for energy production during physical activity and is not shared with other tissues.
Other storage forms: Although glycogen is the primary short-term energy store, the body also relies on fat stored in adipose tissue for long-term energy needs.
Important Points
Skin and bones: These do not store glycogen. Instead, they serve structural and protective functions in the body.
Brain and spinal cord: While the brain requires glucose as its primary energy source, it does not store glycogen. Instead, it relies on a continuous supply of glucose from the bloodstream.
Kidneys and lungs: These organs do not store glycogen either. The kidneys regulate blood filtration and electrolyte balance, while the lungs facilitate gas exchange.
Energy needs: Glycogen is critical for short-term energy storage, but for prolonged energy demands, fats and proteins may also be metabolized.

subject: History
q:
With reference to the Vijayanagara Empire, consider the following statements.
The Vijayanagara Empire was od founded by Harihara I and Bukka I.
Krishnadevaraya, the greatest ruler of the Tuluva dynasty, authored 'Amuktamalyada' in Telugu.al
The city of Hampi, the capital of Vijayanagara, was sacked after the Battle of Talikota.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
exp:
The correct answer is Option 2 - All three.
Key Points
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara I and Bukka I in the year 1336 CE. They were brothers and served under the Kakatiya dynasty before establishing Vijayanagara. Hence, Statement 1 is correct.
Krishnadevaraya, the most celebrated ruler of the Tuluva dynasty in Vijayanagara, authored the literary masterpiece ‘Amuktamalyada’ in Telugu. This work is considered one of the finest examples of Telugu literature and provides insights into governance and dharma. Hence, Statement 2 is correct.
The city of Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, faced destruction after the Battle of Talikota in 1565 CE. The battle was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates, resulting in the defeat of Vijayanagara and the subsequent sacking of Hampi. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.
All three statements provided in the question align with historical evidence and are correct.
Additional Information
Harihara I and Bukka I:
The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 CE by Harihara I and Bukka I, who were originally feudatories under the Kakatiya and Kampili kingdoms.
They founded the empire to protect South India from the invasions of the Delhi Sultanate.
The empire served as a beacon of Hindu culture, art, and architecture during its time.
Krishnadevaraya:
He ruled Vijayanagara from 1509 to 1529 CE and is considered one of the greatest rulers of the empire.
Krishnadevaraya was a patron of literature, art, and architecture. His reign saw the construction of several iconic temples, including the Vitthala Temple at Hampi.
‘Amuktamalyada’ is a treatise on statecraft, written in Telugu, focusing on governance principles and the welfare of citizens.
Battle of Talikota:
The Battle of Talikota occurred in 1565 CE between Vijayanagara and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates—Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, and Bidar.
The defeat of Vijayanagara marked the decline of the empire and led to the destruction of Hampi, which was looted and razed.
Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stands as a testament to the architectural and cultural achievements of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Key Contributions of the Vijayanagara Empire:
The empire played a significant role in the preservation of Hindu culture and traditions during its rule.
Architectural wonders like the Virupaksha Temple, Lotus Mahal, and the Stone Chariot at Hampi showcase the advancements in art and architecture.
The empire facilitated trade and commerce, connecting South India with international markets.
Important Points
Hampi:
Hampi was the capital city of Vijayanagara and a major center for religion, trade, and culture.
It features stunning examples of Dravidian architecture, mixed with Indo-Islamic influences.
Today, Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, attracting tourists and historians worldwide.
Literature and Art:
The Vijayanagara Empire was known for its patronage of literature in languages like Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, and Sanskrit.
Poets like Allasani Peddana and Tenali Ramakrishna flourished during Krishnadevaraya’s reign.
End of the Empire:
The destruction of Hampi after the Battle of Talikota marked the decline of Vijayanagara, but its cultural and architectural legacy continues to inspire.

Key Points
