exp: Rajagriha. Magadha's first capital was Girivraja, which Pali and Prakrit texts call Rajagaha or Rajagriha: modern Rajgir in Nalanda district, about 100 km south-east of Patna. The old town lies inside a ring of five hills behind a cyclopean wall of undressed stone laid without mortar, usually given as about 40 km long, among the oldest surviving fortifications anywhere in India. Every strand of tradition puts Magadha's earliest royal seat here.

subject: History
q:
Which of the following statements about the Vernacular Press Act is/are correct?
1. It was enacted by Lord Lytton.
2. It came to be known as a ‘Gagging Act’.
3. The Act was repealed by Lord Ripon.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: 1, 2 and 3. All three statements hold. Statement 1: the Vernacular Press Act was Act IX of 1878, 'An Act for the better control of publications in Oriental languages', passed at a single sitting of the Legislative Council in March 1878 under Viceroy Lord Lytton (1876–1880). It answered the Indian-language press's attacks on his handling of the famine of 1876–78 and his forward policy in Afghanistan.

subject: History
q:
Which of the following statements about Lord Mayo’s Resolution of 1870 are correct?
1. It was the first step that bifurcated Central and Provincial finances.
2. Provincial Governments were empowered to administer certain services.
3. It attempted to rectify existing imparity.
4. It focussed on the actual needs of the Provinces.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: Only 1 and 2. Lord Mayo (Richard Southwell Bourke, 6th Earl of Mayo, Viceroy 1869–1872) issued the Resolution on provincial finance in December 1870, effective from the financial year beginning 1 April 1871. Statement 1 holds: until then all revenue belonged to the Government of India, and provinces bargained for allotments. Mayo's Resolution cut that single imperial purse in two for the first time.

subject: History
q: Nitisara, an early book of politics, was written by
exp: Kamandaka. The Nitisara, properly the Kamandakiya Nitisara, 'the essence of polity', is a Sanskrit verse treatise on statecraft attributed to Kamandaka. It is conventionally placed in the Gupta age, roughly the fourth to sixth centuries CE, a range inferred from its language and its dependence on the Arthashastra rather than from any colophon. The text names its own lineage.

subject: History
q: Futuhat-i-Alamgiri was written by
exp: Ishwardas Nagar. The Futuhat-i-Alamgiri, 'the victories of Alamgir', is a Persian chronicle of Aurangzeb's reign by Ishwardas Nagar, a Nagar Brahmin of Gujarat in Mughal service who wrote as an eyewitness rather than as a court historiographer. Elliot and Dowson's The History of India as Told by its Own Historians, Vol.

subject: Bihar Special
q: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
exp: Samudragupta. The episode survives only in Chinese writing, hence 'according to Chinese source'. Xuanzang, compiling the Si-yu-ki in 646 CE, writes in Book VIII that the Mahabodhi sangharama outside the northern gate of the Bodhi-tree enclosure 'was built by a former king of Simhala (Ceylon)'. The king's brother, a monk, had been 'treated with disdain as a foreigner' at India's convents.

subject: Polity
q: When was Bihar first separated from the Bengal Presidency under the British-ruled India?
exp: 1912. George V announced at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911 'a new Lieutenant-Governorship in Council administering the areas of Bihar, Chota Nagpur, and Orissa'. The change was executed on 22 March 1912, when three proclamations were notified together.

subject: Geography
q:
Consider the following statements :
1. Lake Victoria is the third largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.
2. It is one of the great lakes of Africa.
3. It is bordered by four countries—Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda and Kenya.
4. The only outflow from Lake Victoria is the Nile River, which exits the lake near Jinja, Uganda.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
exp: 1 and 3. Statement 1 is wrong by one rank. The Lake Victoria Basin Commission, the East African Community's institution for the lake, states that 'Lake Victoria is the 2nd largest freshwater body in the world': about 68,800 sq km, behind Lake Superior (about 82,100 sq km) and ahead of Lake Huron (about 59,600 sq km). Statement 3 is wrong on the count and on one name. Only three states share the shore: Tanzania with about 49 per cent of the surface, Uganda about 45 per cent and Kenya about 6 per cent.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Consider the following statements regarding ‘heat wave’ :
1. Heat wave is considered if the maximum temperature of a station reaches at least 30 °C or more for plains.
2. Heat wave is considered if the maximum temperature of a station reaches at least 40 °C or more for hilly regions.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Neither 1 nor 2. IMD's Weather FAQ defines a heat wave as 'a continuous spell of abnormally hot weather' and rules that it 'need not be considered till maximum temperature of a station reaches at least 40º C for Plains and at least 30º C for Hilly regions'. NDMA's heat-wave page repeats those criteria word for word. The plains floor is 40 °C and the hill floor 30 °C; the stem has swapped two genuine India Meteorological Department figures, making both statements false.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Match List–I with List–II : List—I (Explorer) a. Christopher Columbus b. Jacques Cartier c. Sir Francis Drake d. Ferdinand Magellan List—II (Birthplace)
1. Portugal
2. United Kingdom
3. Italy
4. France
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: a b c d 3 4 2 1. Columbus was born at Genoa, eldest son of the wool-comber Domenico Colombo and Suzanna Fontanarossa; the year is uncertain, given as about 1446 or 1451. Genoa is in present-day Italy: a-3. Cartier was born at Saint-Malo in Brittany in 1491 and died there in 1557: France, b-4. Drake was born, 'according to local tradition, at Crowndale, near Tavistock', in Devon, about 1539-41 (the Dictionary of National Biography heads his entry '1540?

subject: Polity
q: The emirates of UAE are
options: (A) Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al-Quwain, Fujairah, Ras Al-Khaimah
(B) Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Jeddah, Kuwait, Bahrain, Umm Al-Quwain
(C) Umm Al-Quwain, Fujairah, Ras Al-Khaimah, Riyadh, Dammam, Taif, Dubai
(D) Sharjah, Abu Dhabi, Ajman, Fujairah, Dubai, Bahrain, Kuwait
ansText: (A) Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al-Quwain, Fujairah, Ras Al-Khaimah
exp: Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al-Quwain, Fujairah, Ras Al-Khaimah. The UAE Government portal (u.ae, 'The Seven Emirates') names exactly these seven and calls the country 'a constitutional federation of seven emirates'. The number is fixed by the Constitution: under Articles 45–50 the Federal Supreme Council, the highest constitutional authority, 'consists of the Rulers of all the emirates composing the Federation', and 'each emirate has a single vote'.

subject: Geography
q: The river Subarnarekha originates near which of the following villages?
exp: Nagri. India-WRIS, the Central Water Commission's water-resources wiki, states it twice on the basin page: the Subernarekha 'rises near Nagri village in the Ranchi District of Jharkhand at an elevation of 600 m' and flows 395 km to the Bay of Bengal. Nagri is a village and CD block of Ranchi Sadar subdivision, roughly 15–16 km west of Ranchi on the Chota Nagpur plateau.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Which of the following National Parks/Wildlife Sanctuaries are in Bihar?
1. Valmiki National Park
2. Dudhwa National Park
3. Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary
4. Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: 1 and 4. Only Valmiki National Park and Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary are in Bihar. The Forest Survey of India's India State of Forest Report 2023 settles three placements: its national-park table enters 'Valmiki: Bihar' at number 95 and 'Dudhwa: Uttar Pradesh' at number 20, Valmiki being the only national park against Bihar. Annexure V enters 'Bhimbandh (Sanctuary) Bihar' at serial 55. Gajner is in no Bihar list; the Government of Rajasthan's tourism department places it near Bikaner.

subject: Geography
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the ‘Gangetic Dolphin’ :
1. The Gangetic River Dolphin has been categorized as ‘endangered’ under the IUCN’s Red List.
2. It does not have a crystalline eye lens rendering it effectively blind.
3. Navigation and hunting are carried out using echolocation.
4. It has been recognized as India’s National Aquatic Animal.
Which of the above statements are correct?
exp: All of the above. All four statements check out against the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), the environment ministry's autonomous institute. Statement 1: WII records the species as 'Endangered in IUCN red list', following the 2022 assessment of Platanista gangetica (e.T41756A50383346), one rung below Critically Endangered; its population is 'estimated to be less than 2000 individuals'. Statement 2: WII calls Gangetic dolphins 'essentially blind'.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The other name of river Gandak is
exp: Narayani. The Gandak of Bihar and the Narayani of Nepal are one river. UNESCO's World Heritage description of Chitwan National Park places its core 'between the Narayani (Gandak) and Rapti rivers', and calls 'the Narayani (Gandaki)' the third-largest river in Nepal.

subject: Polity
q: Gold is found in which of the following districts of Bihar?
exp: Jamui. The Ministry of Mines told the Lok Sabha on 1 December 2021 (PIB release 1776759): 'The entire resource of gold ore in Bihar is located in Sono area of Jamui district.' Sono is one of Jamui's ten blocks, where the Chotanagpur plateau pushes north across the Bihar–Jharkhand border. The same reply, from the National Mineral Inventory as on 1 April 2015, gives India 501.83 million tonnes of primary gold ore containing 654.74 tonnes of metal. Bihar has 222.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The Triveni Canal has been constructed on which of the following rivers?
exp: Gandak. West Champaran's district page says: 'Tirhut, Tribeni and Done canals are the most prominent canals operating in this district. They get their water supply from the Gandak river at Balmikinager'. India-WRIS project JI02076, the Gandak Major Irrigation Project (a diversion scheme shared with Nepal, begun in the Third Plan and completed in the Sixth), states that its 'Command Includes Tribeni canal, Western and Eastern Gandak canal, Teur and Dhaka Canal'.

subject: Geography
q: Assertion (A) : Rich placer deposits of gold are found on the Ghana coast and gold-bearing veins are found in Brazil. Reason (R) : At some points of time, these continents were joined together along the Atlantic coast. Select the correct answer.
options: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(C) A is false but R is true
(D) A is true but R is false
ansText: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
exp: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. The stem comes almost word for word from NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Chapter 4. 'The occurrence of rich placer deposits of gold in the Ghana coast and the absolute absence of source rock in the region is an amazing fact. The gold bearing veins are in Brazil and it is obvious that the gold deposits of the Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side.

subject: Bihar Special
q:
Bihar’s geographical structure consists of rock systems. Match the rock systems with their descriptions : a. Dharwar rock system b. Vindhyan rock system c. Quaternary rock system d. Tertiary rock system
1. Created by the rapid deposition of alluvium by Himalayan and Peninsular rivers
2. Can be found in the West Champaran district
3. Part of the oldest Archaean rock system
4. Sandstone, limestone, dolomite, quartzite and shale are the main constituents of this rock system
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: a b c d 3 4 1 2. The Dharwar Craton is Archaean, formed about 3.6 to 2.5 billion years ago and reckoned the peninsula's oldest part; in the textbook four-fold scheme (Archaean, Purana, Dravidian, Aryan) the Dharwars are the oldest metamorphosed sediments, grouped with the Archaean. The Vindhyan is a thick, essentially unmetamorphosed sedimentary pile whose standard lithology is sandstone, limestone, dolomite, quartzite and shale. In Bihar it forms the Kaimur Range towards Sasaram in Rohtas.

subject: Geography
q: Which one of the following is the world’s richest region from a marine biodiversity perspective, comprising twenty-one islands with estuaries, beaches, forests of the nearshore environment, sea grasses, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves?
exp: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve. UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere entry (on the World Network since 2001) calls it 'one of the world's richest regions from a marine biodiversity perspective', with 4,223 species across about 10,500 sq km. The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve Trust, a Government of Tamil Nadu trust, states that an area of 560 sq km 'encompassing 21 uninhabited islands, surrounding coral reef areas and shallow water habitat' was declared a Marine National Park in 1986.

subject: Reasoning
q: What is the local time of Thimphu (Bhutan) located at 90° East longitude when the time at Greenwich (0°) is 12:00 noon?
exp: 6:00 p.m. The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so it covers 15° of longitude every hour: one degree is worth 4 minutes of time, one minute of arc 4 seconds, and one second of arc a fifteenth of a second. The stem places Thimphu at 90° East, so the gap from Greenwich is 90 ÷ 15 = 6 hours. The sign comes from the direction of spin. The Earth rotates from west to east, so a place east of the prime meridian meets the Sun earlier and its clock is ahead of Greenwich.

subject: Geography
q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: (A) Natural gas is found in Dharwar rock formation.
(C) Cuddapah series is famous for diamonds.
(D) Petroleum reserves are found in Aravalli hills.
exp: Mica is found in Kodarma. Kodarma (also spelt Koderma), in northern Jharkhand, is the centre of the Kodarma–Giridih–Hazaribagh belt, the largest muscovite-bearing tract in India and long called the mica capital of the country. The mica sits in coarse pegmatite veins intruding the Precambrian gneisses and schists of the Chhotanagpur plateau. Only pegmatites grow mica crystals large enough to split into sheets, so sheet mica is never a sedimentary mineral.

subject: Geography
q: How many latitudes are there on the globe drawn at 1 degree interval?
exp: 179. Count the circles, not the degrees. Stepping north from the Equator one degree at a time gives parallels from 1° N to 89° N: 89 circles. Stepping south gives another 89. Add the Equator, the 0° parallel: 89 + 89 + 1 = 179. The poles, 90° N and 90° S, are left out because each is a single point. A parallel is a circle at a constant angular distance from the Equator, and its length, 2πR cos φ, falls from about 40,075 km at the Equator to roughly 20,000 km at 60° and to zero at 90°.

subject: Geography
q: The average height of the Kosi plain from mean sea level is
exp: 30 m. The Kosi plain is the Indian part of the Kosi megafan: the tract of Supaul, Saharsa, Madhepura, Araria, Purnia and Katihar through which the river spreads before joining the Ganga near Kursela. It is among the lowest-lying land in India. The Ganga Basin Report of the Central Water Commission and the National Remote Sensing Centre (India-WRIS) puts the Middle Ganga Plain generally below 100 m, rising to 130 m in the north-west and 150 m in the south.

subject: Geography
q: On which plateau, the Tropic of Cancer and the Indian Standard Time Line intersect each other?
exp: Baghelkhand. The Tropic of Cancer is the parallel of 23°26′ N, rounded to 23°30′ in most textbooks. The Indian Standard Time line is the meridian of 82°30′ E, conventionally placed at Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. They meet near 23°26′ N, 82°30′ E, in Sonhat tahsil of Koriya district, northern Chhattisgarh, roughly 40 km south of the Madhya Pradesh border: the Koriya upland on the south-eastern shoulder of the Baghelkhand plateau. A safer route skips the pinpointing.

subject: Geography
q: Which district of Uttarakhand is not situated along the Tibbet boundary?
exp: Almora. Uttarakhand's frontier with Tibet (China) runs along the crest of the Great Himalaya, and only three of its thirteen districts reach it: Uttarkashi, Chamoli and Pithoragarh. Pithoragarh's administration says 'the whole northern and eastern boundaries of Pithoragarh district are international', naming Lipulekh, Kungri Bingri, Lampiya Dhura and Belcha as openings towards Tibet. Almora sits behind all three.

subject: Geography
q: Where does the El Niño current flow?
options: (D) More than one of the above
exp: The Pacific Ocean. El Niño belongs to the equatorial Pacific and to no other basin; NOAA defines El Niño and La Niña as 'climate patterns in the Pacific Ocean'. In a normal year the trade winds blow east to west along the equator, dragging warm surface water towards Indonesia and letting cold, nutrient-rich water upwell off Peru and Ecuador. In an El Niño year the trades weaken, the warm water sloshes back east and the upwelling shuts down.

subject: Polity
q:
Consider the following statements about the collegium system :
1. The Supreme Court collegium is a five-member body, which is headed by the incumbent Chief Justice of India (CJI) and comprises four other seniormost Judges of the Court at that time.
2. The Parliament by law has evolved the collegium system.
3. The Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed only through the collegium system.
4. The collegium system was introduced in the year 1993 by Justice P. N. Bhagwati in the landmark First Judges Case.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: 1 and 3. Statement 1 restates the Third Judges Case (In re Special Reference No. 1 of 1998, (1998) 7 SCC 739, a Presidential reference under Article 143): the CJI recommends Supreme Court appointments 'in consultation with the four seniormost puisne Judges', five members in all. Statement 3 holds as a description of selection: since 1993 no Supreme Court or High Court judge has been appointed except on a collegium recommendation, and there is no parallel channel.

subject: Polity
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution of India :
1. It added three words to the Preamble—‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’.
2. It added eight Fundamental Duties to the Constitution.
3. It added new Directive Principles, i.e., Article 39A, Article 43A and Article 47.
4. It granted power to the President, in consultation with the Election Commission, to disqualify members of the State Legislatures.
Which of the above statements are incorrect ?
exp: 2 and 3. The stem asks which statements are incorrect, so find the two false ones. Statement 2 is incorrect. Section 11 inserted Part IVA with Article 51A, clauses (a) to (j): ten Fundamental Duties, not eight. Statement 3 is incorrect by one article number. Sections 8, 9 and 10 inserted Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (workers' participation in management) and Article 48A (environment, forests and wild life).

subject: Mathematics
q:
The specifications required for a community to be declared as a Scheduled Tribe are 1. indications of primitive traits 2. distinctive culture 3. shyness of contact with the community at large 4. backwardness and geographical isolation
Which of the above are correct?
exp: All of the above. Every item is an accepted criterion. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes lists five 'essential characteristics' for a community to be identified as a Scheduled Tribe: 'Primitive way of life and habitation in remote and less easily accessible areas, Distinctive culture, Shyness of contact with the community at large, Geographical isolation, and General backwardness in all respects.' The exam's four items map onto them without a gap.

subject: Polity
q: From which country, the Indian Constitution has taken reference for the idea of the Fundamental Rights?
exp: United States of America. Part III is modelled on the United States Bill of Rights, the first ten amendments to the American Constitution, ratified on 15 December 1791. What India borrowed is a device: a written catalogue of rights placed above ordinary law, with courts empowered to strike down a law that violates it. Article 13(2) carries that device, making void any law that 'takes away or abridges' the rights in the Part.

subject: Polity
q: Untouchability is abolished by which Article of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Article 17. Headed 'Abolition of Untouchability', it reads: "'Untouchability' is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of 'Untouchability' shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law." The stem's verb settles it. In Part III only two Articles use 'abolished': Article 17 for untouchability and Article 18 for titles.

subject: Polity
q: The authority to determine the number of Judges in a High Court rests with which of the following entities?
options: (B) The Chief Minister of the State
exp: The President. Article 216 is one sentence: 'Every High Court shall consist of a Chief Justice and such other Judges as the President may from time to time deem it necessary to appoint.' 'Such other Judges' leaves the number open; 'from time to time' lets it change with caseload; and 'as the President may … deem it necessary' names the authority. No Act of Parliament and no State concurrence is needed.

subject: Polity
q: The Fifth Schedule deals with the governance and protection of the interests of which specific group of people?
exp: Scheduled Tribes. The Schedule names the group in its title. Printed under the reference '[Article 244(1)]', it is headed 'Provisions as to the Administration and Control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes', and no other community appears in it. Article 244(1) applies it to 'any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram'. Every mechanism inside is built around Scheduled Tribes. Paragraph 3 makes the Governor report to the President annually or when required.

subject: Polity
q: In which case(s) did the Supreme Court of India give for the first time the doctrine of ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution?
options: (B) Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
(C) Minerva Mills vs. Union of India
ansText: (B) Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala
exp: Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala. State of Kerala. It was decided on 24 April 1973 by thirteen judges, the largest Bench the Supreme Court has ever assembled, by 7:6 (AIR 1973 SC 1461; (1973) 4 SCC 225). The doctrine is in the judgment itself. Sikri CJ wrote at paragraph 316 that 'every provision of the Constitution can be amended provided in the result the basic foundation and structure of the Constitution remains the same'.

subject: History
q:
Match the following political parties listed in List–I with their years of establishment in List–II : List—I (Political Parties) a. Communist Party of India (Marxist) b. Communist Party of India c. Bahujan Samaj Party d. All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) List—II (Years of Establishment) 1. 1964 2. 1998 3. 1925 4. 1984
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: a b c d 1 3 4 2. (a) The Communist Party of India (Marxist) dates its formation to 7 November 1964, the closing day of its founding (Seventh) Congress at Calcutta; P. Sundarayya was its first General Secretary: a–1. (b) The Communist Party of India was founded on 26 December 1925 at its first Conference in Kanpur (then Cawnpore). David Petrie's intelligence survey Communism in India 1924–1927 records the conference in 'the last week of 1925', with about 500 attending.

subject: Polity
q: Under which Article(s), the Speaker can allow any member of the House to speak in his/her mother tongue?
exp: Article 120 (1). Business in Parliament 'shall be transacted in Hindi or in English', and the proviso to Article 120(1) adds that the Chairman of the Council of States or Speaker of the House of the People, or person acting as such, 'may permit any member who cannot adequately express himself in Hindi or in English to address the House in his mother-tongue'. That sentence settles three things. The default is narrow: Hindi or English, and no other language as of right.

subject: Economics
q:
The Foreign Exchange Reserves (FER) of RBI include which of the following?
1. Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)
2. Gold
3. Special Drawing Rights (SDR)
4. Reserve Tranche Position
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: All of the above. Table 2 of the RBI's Weekly Statistical Supplement, 'Foreign Exchange Reserves', has exactly four sub-lines under the total. The issue dated 29 September 2023, reporting the position on 22 September 2023, gives Total Reserves of US$ 590,702 million, made up of 1.1 Foreign Currency Assets US$ 523,363 million, 1.2 Gold US$ 44,307 million, 1.3 SDRs US$ 18,012 million and 1.4 Reserve Position in the IMF US$ 5,019 million. The four add to US$ 590,701 million, the gap being rounding.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Consider the following statements about ‘Rules of Origin’ :
1. Rules of Origin are the criteria needed to determine the national source of a product.
2. Rules of Origin help the custom agencies to know what regulations and fees apply to a given product.
3. These are used for the purpose of trade statistics.
4. Their importance is derived from the fact that duties and restrictions in several cases depend upon the sources of imports.
Which of the above statements are correct?
exp: All of the above. Three statements are lifted almost word for word from the WTO's technical note on rules of origin. Its definition reads: 'Rules of origin are the criteria needed to determine the national source of a product. Their importance is derived from the fact that duties and restrictions in several cases depend upon the source of imports.' That is statements 1 and 4.

subject: Chemistry
q:
Consider the following statements about infant mortality rate :
1. It is the probability of dying between birth and exactly 1 year of age, expressed per 10000 live births.
2. The infant mortality rate in the year 1950 was 189·6.
3. In the year 2019, the infant mortality rate was 30.
4. As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) Bulletin of Registrar General of India (RGI), the State with the highest infant mortality rate in the year 2019 was Uttar Pradesh.
Which of the above statements are correct?
exp: Only 2 and 3. The Registrar General's SRS Statistical Report 2019 settles three of the four statements. Statement 1 fails on one number. The report's formula is infant deaths during the year ÷ live births during the year × 1000, and paragraph 4.11 defines IMR as 'infant deaths (less than one year) per thousand live births'. The statement says per 10,000. Statement 3 is right: IMR 'registered 2-point decline to 30 in 2019 from 32 in 2018 at the National level', with rural 34 and urban 20.

subject: Current Affairs
q:
Human capital formation as a concept is better explained in terms of a process, which enables 1. individuals of a country to accumulate more capital 2. increasing the knowledge 3. increasing the skill levels 4. increasing the knowledge, skill levels and capacities of the people of the country
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: Only 4. Human capital is the knowledge, skill, competence and health embodied in a country's people, and human capital formation is the process of adding to it. Statement 4, 'increasing the knowledge, skill levels and capacities of the people of the country', is the only item that states that definition whole. Statement 1 is a different concept.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements regarding insolvency and bankruptcy :
1. Bankruptcy refers to a financial state in which an individual or entity is unable to pay off their debts as they become due.
2. Insolvency refers to a legal process, where the assets of the debtor are liquidated or reorganized for the benefit of creditors.
3. Bankruptcy is a state whereas insolvency is the conclusion.
4. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Only 4. Statements 1, 2 and 3 run the two words the wrong way round; statement 4 is the only one the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 supports. Under Section 79(3) a 'bankrupt' is 'a debtor who has been adjudged as bankrupt by a bankruptcy order under section 126', an order that comes at the end of the process. What starts it is default, defined in section 3(12) as non-payment of a debt that has become due.

subject: Polity
q: In which year was the Industrial Policy Resolution adopted?
exp: 1956. The document settles the date. It is headed 'GOVERNMENT OF INDIA (INDUSTRIAL POLICY RESOLUTION) New Delhi, the 30th April, 1956', under No. 91/CF/48, and the Second Five Year Plan records that it 'was placed before Parliament by the Prime Minister on the 30th April, 1956'. It is the founding charter of India's mixed economy. Schedule A listed seventeen industries whose future development would be 'the exclusive responsibility of the State'.

subject: Polity
q:
Consider the following statements regarding the SVAMITVA scheme :
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Mines.
2. This scheme seeks to create geopositioning infrastructure like CORS network to benchmark the location and provides five centimetre level accuracy.
3. CORS means Cross-Origin Resource Sharing.
4. The scheme is a reformative step towards establishment of clear ownership of property in rural inhabited (Abadi) areas, by mapping of land parcels using drone technology.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
exp: 1 and 3. Each wrong statement attaches a false label to something the scheme really does. Statement 1: SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages And Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) is indeed a Central Sector Scheme, but its Framework for Implementation names the 'Nodal Ministry (Ministry of Panchayati Raj)'. The Ministry of Mines has no role in it.

subject: Polity
q:
Which of the following is/are the consequence(s) of invoking Article 360, declaration of a financial emergency?
1. The President may order the States to reduce the salaries and allowances of all or any class of employees serving in connection with the State affairs.
2. Money Bills or other financial bills passed by the State Legislature are not required to be reserved for the consideration of the President.
3. The President can issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of employees serving in connection with the affairs of the Union, including the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
4. Money Bills or other financial bills are to be reserved for the consideration of the President after they are passed by the Legislature of the State.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: Only 1, 3 and 4. Article 360(4) decides it: the four statements paraphrase its three limbs, with one inverted. Clause (4)(a)(i) lets a direction to a State require 'the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of a State' (statement 1). Clause (4)(a)(ii) lets it require 'all Money Bills or other Bills to which the provisions of article 207 apply' to be reserved for the President after the State Legislature passes them (statement 4).

subject: Economics
q:
Which of the following factors could potentially contribute to stagflation in the Indian economy?
1. High inflationary pressures due to increased Government spending
2. Decline in industrial production and sluggish economic growth
3. Decrease in aggregate demand and consumer spending
4. Appreciation of the domestic currency leading to reduction of export competitiveness
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: Only 1 and 2. Stagflation is a specific pairing: a high and rising price level together with stagnant or falling output. A factor contributes only if it supplies one of those legs without cancelling the other. Statement 1 supplies the price leg: more government spending raises aggregate demand, and if output cannot keep up, the excess spills into prices. Statement 2 supplies the output leg; falling industrial production and sluggish growth are the 'stagnation' in the word.

subject: Physics
q:
As per the Economic Survey, 2023,
which of the following statements describe(s) the trend of Foreign Direct Investment in India?
1. It has decreased due to the less participation of the private sector.
2. It has increased compared to the prepandemic levels.
3. It has increased rapidly without decreasing in any Financial Year after the telecom sector was entirely reformed.
4. It has decreased due to a weak global economic situation. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: 2 and 4. The two look contradictory and are not. The Economic Survey 2022-23 says both in one passage: 'Amidst heightened global uncertainty, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the manufacturing sector moderated in the first half of FY23. However, inflows stayed well above the pre-pandemic levels.' Statement 4 is the first half and statement 2 the second; one compares with last year, the other with FY20. The numbers back both. Gross inflows were 'US$ 39.3 billion as compared to US$ 42.

subject: Economics
q: Which of the following statements about non-plan expenditures of the Central Government is correct?
options: (A) The expenditure is on interest payments.
(B) The expenditure is on science and technology.
ansText: (A) The expenditure is on interest payments.
exp: The expenditure is on interest payments. Until the Budget for 2017-18 the Union Budget split spending into Plan, flowing from the current Five Year Plan's outlays, and Non-Plan: everything the government was already committed to, such as interest, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions, grants to States and Union Territories, police, and upkeep of assets from earlier Plans. The test was discretion, not usefulness, and interest payments are the purest Non-Plan item.

subject: Economics
q: Which of the following is not true about globalization and its impact on India?
options: (A) It has expanded trade in goods and services.
(B) It has led to greater flow of Foreign Direct Investment.
(C) Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports.
ansText: (C) Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports.
exp: Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports. The stem asks which statement is not true. Statement (c) fails on the Economic Survey 2022-23's figures. Merchandise exports rose from US$ 305.0 billion in April-December 2021 to US$ 332.8 billion in April-December 2022, up about US$ 27.8 billion. Imports rose from US$ 441.5 billion to US$ 551.7 billion, up about US$ 110.2 billion, roughly four times as much. Para 11.14 records the result: a merchandise trade deficit of US$ 218.9 billion against US$ 136.

subject: Economics
q:
Consider the following statements about the latest developments in the Union Government finances :
1. The fiscal deficit of the Union Government had reached 9·2 percent of GDP during the pandemic FY21.
2. The fiscal deficit has moderated to 7·7 percent of GDP in FY22.
3. The revenue collection over the last two years has gone down.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Only 1. All three statements come from one sentence of the Economic Survey 2022-23, Chapter III, para 3.4 (page 43), with two altered. The Survey says: 'The fiscal deficit of the Union Government, which reached 9.2 per cent of GDP during the pandemic year FY21, has moderated to 6.7 per cent of GDP in FY22 PA and is further budgeted to reach 6.4 per cent of GDP in FY23 .. supported by buoyant revenue collection over the last two years.' Statement 1 reproduces the 9.2 per cent exactly.

subject: History
q:
Which of the following were the reasons for the failure of the Revolt of 1857?
1. The military superiority of the British
2. The rebels did not have a unified programme and ideology
3. There was a lack of support from all the sections of society
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: All of the above. The three reasons are not rivals; they work at three levels. (1) Military superiority. The rebels fought largely with swords, pikes, matchlocks and captured guns; the Company had the Enfield P-53 rifle, disciplined artillery, and Lord Dalhousie's railway (opened April 1853) and telegraph (working from 1854); the telegraph let John Lawrence disarm suspect regiments in Punjab.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The cook from Bihar who saved Mahatma Gandhi’s life from a murder attempt by food poisoning in 1917 was
exp: Batak Mian. Batak Mian Ansari is the name attached, in Bihar's public memory and in every retelling, to a plot to poison Gandhi at Motihari during the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917. As the story is told, he was a cook in an indigo planter's household, was ordered to serve Gandhi poisoned milk, and saw to it that Gandhi never drank it, losing his job, house and village for it. The setting is documented: W. S.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The Bakasht Movement in Bihar during 1937–1938 was organized by whom?
exp: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati. Bakasht (bakhast in the records), which the Government of Bihar's History of the Freedom Movement in Bihar defines as 'land in cultivation of landlord', was the zamindar's home farm. Much of it had passed to tenants, or had been sold out of tenants' hands for rent arrears during the Depression, and the fight over it became Bihar's central agrarian conflict of the late 1930s.

subject: History
q:
Consider the following events during India’s Freedom Struggle :
1. Home Rule Movement
2. Surat Split
3. Kheda Satyagraha
4. Minto-Morley Reforms Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events given above?
exp: 2–4–1–3. The Surat Split (2) came first, at the Congress session of December 1907, shifted there from Nagpur: the Moderates put up Rash Behari Ghosh for president, the Extremists refused, and the Congress divided for nine years. The Minto–Morley Reforms (4) followed as the Indian Councils Act 1909, which enlarged the legislative councils, put an Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council for the first time and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

subject: Polity
q: Lord Lytton is not associated with which of the following?
exp: The Ilbert Bill. Lord Lytton was Viceroy from 1876 to 1880; the Ilbert Bill belongs to his successor, Lord Ripon (1880 to 1884). Drafted by Sir Courtenay Ilbert, the Law Member, as an amendment to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1882, it would have let senior Indian judges try European British subjects. Leave to introduce it was moved on 2 February 1883 and it was introduced on 9 February 1883, over two years after Lytton had left. The other three are Lytton's.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Which treaty was signed after the Battle of Buxar?
exp: The Treaty of Allahabad. The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 at Buxar, on the Ganga in today's Buxar district of Bihar, where Major Hector Munro's Company army beat Mir Qasim (the deposed Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. Robert Clive, back in Bengal from May 1765, settled it at Allahabad in August 1765 in two agreements.

subject: Economics
q: In which of the following movements did Mahatma Gandhi make the first use of the hunger strike as a weapon?
exp: Ahmedabad Strike. In the Ahmedabad mill-hands' strike of February-March 1918, the workers wanted a fifty per cent rise; the owners, led by Anasuyabehn Sarabhai's brother Sheth Ambalal Sarabhai, offered twenty and refused arbitration. Gandhi advised a strike on four conditions: no violence, no molesting blacklegs, no dependence on alms, and honest labour for bread meanwhile.

subject: Bihar Special
q: The Quit India Movement in 1942 witnessed significant contributions from leaders of Bihar. Which prominent Bihar leader was known as the ‘Bihar Kesari’ and actively participated in the Quit India Movement?
exp: Shri Krishna Singh. Shri Krishna Sinha (21 October 1887 – 31 January 1961), 'Shri Babu', carried the title Bihar Kesari, the Lion of Bihar, for the roar of his platform oratory. He gave up the bar for Non-Cooperation in 1921, spent about eight years in British jails in all, and in 1940 was named by Gandhi as Bihar's first individual satyagrahi. The AICC adopted the resolution at Gowalia Tank on 8 August 1942, Sinha was arrested on 10 August 1942, and he was released from Hazaribagh jail only in 1944, seriously ill.

subject: Polity
q: In response to the mass agitation of the Champaran Movement, the British Government took which step to address the issue?
options: (A) Appointed Mahatma Gandhi as the Governor of Champaran
(B) Enforced strict curfew and imposed Martial Law in the region
(D) Declared Champaran as an independent State
exp: Instituted the Champaran Agrarian Committee. Gandhi reached Champaran in April 1917 at Raj Kumar Shukla's insistence and began recording the peasants' statements. When the Bihar Government asked whether he should not leave, he replied that it had two honourable exits: redress the ryots' grievances, or accept that they had made a prima facie case and institute an official inquiry. It chose the second. Sir Edward Gait, Lieutenant-Governor of Bihar and Orissa, appointed the inquiry with Sir Frank Sly as Chairman and invited Gandhi onto it.

subject: Polity
q:
Match List–I with List–II : List—I a. Servants of India Society b. Tattwabodhini Sabha c. Atmiya Sabha List—II
1. Debendranath Tagore
2. Gopal Krishna Gokhale
3. Ram Mohan Roy
4. Keshab Chandra Sen
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
exp: a b c 2 1 3. The Servants of India Society (a) was founded at Pune on 12 June 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale (2), who left the Deccan Education Society to start it. Its members took vows of poverty and lifelong service and worked by strictly constitutional means; V. S. Srinivasa Sastri led it after Gokhale's death in 1915.

subject: Bihar Special
q: Ambabai, a woman freedom fighter, belonged to which of the following States of India?
exp: Karnataka. Ambabai is the woman satyagrahi of the Civil Disobedience years placed at Udupi (Udipi in older records) on the Kannada-speaking coast. The accounts agree: married at twelve and widowed at sixteen, she picketed foreign-cloth and liquor shops at Udupi, was imprisoned, and between terms made speeches, taught spinning and organised prabhat pheris. Udupi has never belonged to the other three States.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Who among the following was not the member of the Cabinet Mission?
exp: J. Andrew. Andrew. The Cabinet Mission that Clement Attlee's Labour government sent in 1946 had exactly three members, all serving Cabinet ministers: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Secretary of State for India, who led it; Sir Stafford Cripps, President of the Board of Trade; and A. V. Alexander, First Lord of the Admiralty. It reached India on 24 March 1946 and issued its plan on 16 May 1946. Option (a), 'P. Lawrence', is the paper's compressed form of Frederick William Pethick-Lawrence; option (b) is exact. 'J.

subject: History
q: “The Indian National Congress was founded on the basis of safety valve theory, to protect the British Government from threats.” Which leader said that?
exp: Lala Lajpat Rai. It comes from his book Young India: An Interpretation and a History of the Nationalist Movement from Within (New York, B. W. Huebsch, 1916), in its chapter on India from 1857 to 1905. On page 122 he writes that 'the idea of the Indian National Congress was a product of Lord Dufferin's brain'. On page 124 he says Dufferin aimed at an association 'which should serve more as a "safety valve" than as a genuine Nationalist organisation'. On page 125 he quotes A. O.

subject: Polity
q: In which of the following Indian National Congress Sessions, the resolutions related to the Fundamental Rights were passed for the first time?
exp: Karachi Session—1931. The Congress met at Karachi at the end of March 1931 under Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, mainly to endorse the Gandhi–Irwin Pact of 5 March, and adopted the Resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy, dated 31 March 1931. Drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru with Gandhi's edits, it was the first charter of rights a Congress session owned.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In a certain code language, ‘GAME’ is written as ‘$ ÷ * %’ and ‘BEAD’ is written as ‘# % ÷ ×’. How will the word ‘MADE’ be written in that code language?
exp: * ÷ × %. This is a positional substitution code and both clues agree, so it takes under a minute once you line them up. Step 1: read each clue position by position. GAME is '$ ÷ * %', so G = $, A = ÷, M = *, E = %. BEAD is '# % ÷ ×', so B = #, E = %, A = ÷, D = ×. Step 2: check the clues against each other.

subject: Reasoning
q: Q travels towards East. M travels towards North. S and T travel in opposite directions. T travels towards right of Q. Which of the following is definitely true?
options: (A) M and S travel in the opposite directions
(D) M and S travel in the same direction
ansText: (D) M and S travel in the same direction
exp: M and S travel in the same direction. The chain has only two links and it runs in one direction, so do it in order and do not draw more than a cross on the page. Link 1: fix T. The stem says T travels towards the right of Q, and Q is travelling East. In a direction-sense question 'the right of' a moving person means that person's own right hand, not the right-hand side of the page, so you turn ninety degrees clockwise from the direction Q faces. Clockwise from East is South. T therefore travels South. Link 2: fix S.

subject: Current Affairs
q: A man ‘Ramesh’, who owns a plot of land of 100 square yards, increases his plot of land by acquiring 10% more from his neighbour ‘Suresh’, who also owns 100 square yards land. After 2 years, he sells back 10% of the total plot to the neighbour. Which of the following is correct?
options: (A) Ramesh’s land is more than Suresh
(B) Suresh’s land is more than Ramesh
ansText: (B) Suresh’s land is more than Ramesh
exp: Suresh’s land is more than Ramesh. Ramesh ends with 99 square yards and Suresh with 101. Step 1: the transfer. Both men start with 100 square yards. Ramesh increases his holding by 10 per cent, and 10 per cent of 100 is 10 square yards, which comes out of Suresh's plot. Ramesh 110, Suresh 90. This step is unambiguous only because the two men start equal: 10 per cent of Ramesh's holding and 10 per cent of Suresh's holding are the same 10 square yards. Step 2: the sale back.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Find the odd pair among the following options.
exp: Snobbery : Shoes. The relation being tested is trade-or-goods to product: in each of the other three pairs the first word names a craft, a manufacturing place or a class of merchandise, and the second word names what it deals in. Millinery is the trade of designing, making and selling women's hats: the word descends from Milaner, a dealer in fancy wares brought from Milan, which is exactly how it settled on hats and trimmings.

subject: Physics
q: What should come in place of question mark (?) in the following number series? 132 156 ? 210 240 272
exp: 182. Work the first differences of the terms the paper actually prints. 156 − 132 = 24; the next gap is the unknown one; then 210 → 240 = 30 and 240 → 272 = 32. The two gaps at the tail differ by 2, so the ladder of differences is climbing by 2 at every step, which forces the two unknown gaps to be 26 and 28. That gives 132 + 24 = 156, 156 + 26 = 182, and 182 + 28 = 210, and 210 is a term the paper prints, so the rule is checked against the question rather than assumed from it.

subject: Biology
q: Select the missing number from the given alternatives : 44 49 37 52 ? 41 58 35 53
exp: 77. The booklet prints these nine numbers as a three-by-three block, and that layout is the question: 44 49 37 in the first row, 52 ? 41 in the second, 58 35 53 in the third. Two rows are complete, so a candidate rule can be tested twice before it is used once. Take the two outer numbers of a row and subtract, then multiply by 7. Row 1: 44 − 37 = 7, and 7 × 7 = 49, which is the printed middle entry. Row 3: 58 − 53 = 5, and 5 × 7 = 35, again the printed middle entry.

subject: Current Affairs
q: Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement. Statement : In a one-day cricket match, the total runs made by a team were 200, of which 160 runs were made by spinners. Conclusions : 1. 80% of the team consisted of spinners. 2. The opening batsmen were spinners. Select the correct answer.
exp: Neither 1 nor 2 follows the statement. The rule in this family is that a conclusion follows only if it cannot be false while the statement is true, and each conclusion must be put through that test on its own. Take conclusion 1 first. The statement supplies two quantities, both of them runs: 200 in total and 160 by spinners. 160 out of 200 is indeed 80 per cent, but 80 per cent of the runs, not of the players. The conclusion silently moves that figure onto a different population.

subject: Current Affairs
q: In a code language, if GREAT is written as 718222620 and MONK is written as 13121411, then how will VIGOROUS be written in the same language?
exp: 22187121812619. Build the rule from the two samples before touching the target word. In GREAT, three letters give their plain alphabet position: G is 7th, R is 18th, T is 20th, and the code opens 7, 18 and ends 20. The other two do not: E is the 5th letter but codes as 22, and A is the 1st but codes as 26. Both are vowels, and 22 = 27 − 5 while 26 = 27 − 1, which is the reverse position, the number a letter has when the alphabet is counted backwards from Z = 1 to A = 26.

subject: Mathematics
q: Find the odd one in the following groups : Q,W,Z,B B,H,K,M W,C,G,J M,S,V,X
exp: W,C,G,J. Write the alphabet position under each letter and take the gaps, treating the alphabet as a circle so that A follows Z: when the next position is the smaller number, add 26 before subtracting. Group one, Q,W,Z,B: 17, 23, 26, 2, so the gaps are 23 − 17 = 6, 26 − 23 = 3 and (2 + 26) − 26 = 2, giving 6, 3, 2. Group two, B,H,K,M: 2, 8, 11, 13, so the gaps are 6, 3, 2. Group four, M,S,V,X: 13, 19, 22, 24, so the gaps are again 6, 3, 2. Three groups therefore share one signature.

subject: Mathematics
q: Four branches of a company are located at M, N , O and P . M is in the North of N at a distance of 4 km; P is in the South of O at a distance of 2 km; N is in the Southeast of O by 1 km. What is the distance between M and P in km?
exp: 5·34. Set coordinates rather than sketching: put O at the origin, with East along the positive x-axis and North along the positive y-axis, and measure everything in kilometres. P is 2 km due South of O, so P = (0, −2). N is 1 km Southeast of O, and in these items Southeast always means the exact 45-degree bisector, so that 1 km splits equally into an eastward and a southward component of 1 ÷ √2 ≈ 0·707 km each: N = (0·707, −0·707).
